name: Rosie
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can live with others or be an only dog & I don't mind cats!

I'd like a secure garden to excercise and play safely in.

I'm a little unsettled at the moment, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home!

31-07-26 Rosie is the sweetest lady who has arrived all the way from Romania in search of her forever home. Despite her long journey, she is already trying so hard to be brave.

She will happily approach us with a wiggly bum, and if we spend a little time sitting quietly with her, she soon starts to relax. Before long, she'll lie down beside us and happily accept some gentle bum scratches. Rosie is still quite worried by sudden movements and loud noises, which is completely understandable given how much change she has been through.

Rosie is currently kennelled with other dogs and really enjoys their company. She gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends but is so people oriented that she could be an only dog in the right home with experienced adopters, or live with kind resident dogs who don't mind sharing their space, with this happy-go-lucky lady! She does prefer calmer dogs, so if she were to be homed with a resident dog, she would like for them to be on the calmer and understanding side. Rosie's adopters will need to have experience with rescue dogs and understanding that it may take time for them to decompress and settle in.

Rosie has recently been introduced to lead walking and is taking her learning at a slow pace, but with continued training and gentle encouragements she should pick this up. As Rosie has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her to adjust at her own pace. Rosie can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who understand that she will need time to settle in. She has met cats fine at the rescue, and we would consider homing her with dog-savvy cats.

Rosie is a gentle, affectionate girl with a lovely nature. She is already showing us that she wants to trust people, and with a calm home, a confident canine friend, and plenty of patience, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the comforts of family life.

Rosie has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Alfie
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I am fine with cats!

I would love a garden to potter around in.

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have age related cataracts, and have had 13 teeth removed.

24-07-26 Alfie is a wonderful older man who was originally adopted from us and has sadly found himself back in our care after spending many years in a home. He is now looking for a very special retirement home where he can enjoy all the comforts he loves.

As Alfie has got older, he has developed a few age-related quirks. He can become a little confused at night and, during a recent adoption, found it difficult to settle, often pacing and becoming restless. Since returning to us, we have found a routine that helps him feel safe and secure, and he now settles well to sleep in a crate. For this reason, his new home will need to provide him with a quiet space where he can rest undisturbed, and we would like his adopters to continue this routine.

Alfie is an early riser and is usually awake around 6am, although he has been making lovely progress with settling quietly for a little longer each morning. Once he's up, he still has a real spring in his step! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time for a walk and can be quite vocal while his lead is being put on, but as soon as he's out and about he is the perfect gentleman. He walks beautifully, enjoys exploring, and is friendly with everyone he meets, both people and dogs.

Despite being an older gentleman, Alfie still loves getting out and about and enjoys keeping busy. A good walk and plenty of things to keep his mind occupied help him settle well afterwards, and once he's had his exercise there's nothing he loves more than curling up on the sofa for a cuddle.

Alfie gets on well with other dogs and could happily live with calm canine companions. Equally, he is quite an independent little chap and would also be perfectly content as the only dog in the home. Like many older dogs, Alfie has become very enthusiastic about his food. He can be a little grabby with treats and has occasionally grumbled around mealtimes, but this has never escalated and is easily managed by feeding him separately from other dogs and allowing him to enjoy his meals in peace.

Alfie is a truly special little boy who has stolen the hearts of everyone at the rescue. He is looking for a kind and understanding family who will embrace his little quirks, continue the routine that helps him thrive, and give him all the love, comfort and adventures he still enjoys. In return, they will gain a happy, affectionate companion who still has so much love to give.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Molly
description:
I can live with dog-savvy teens, and would love an active home!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would love plenty of adventures once I am fully vaccinated!

I am just a puppy! Please be patient with me while I learn the basics!

My adopter will need to agree to have me spayed when I'm old enough.

01-08-26 Molly is an amazing puppy who has come to us with her siblings following an accidental litter. She is a happy, confident girl who is full of fun and has a wonderful zest for life.Mollyis already a big girl for her age, and we believe she is a Cane Corso Cross, so her adopters will need to be prepared for her to grow into a large adult dog.

Mollyis a friendly and affectionate pup who is looking for a loving home where she can continue to learn and explore the world. She has started learning about walking on a harness, and would like to continue this, out and about, once she is fully vaccinated and settled into her new home, she will love getting out and about on plenty of adventures with her family.

Mollycould live with older, dog-savvy children, aged 13+ who understand that she is a large, boisterous puppy and will need help learning her manners as she grows. She could happily live with another friendly dog who doesn't mind sharing their home with a playful youngster, or she could be an only dog, providing her new family have plenty of time to dedicate to her training, socialisation, and exercise.

As with all puppies,Mollywill need continued guidance with house training, lead walking, and all the basics of family life. Her adopters must be committed to taking her to puppy socialisation and training classes to help her develop into a confident, well-mannered adult and agree to have her spayed when she is of age.

Mollyis a truly lovely girl with so much potential. She is looking for a family who will give her the love, time, and commitment she deserves, and in return she is sure to become a wonderful and loyal companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lucky
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have a Grade 2 heart murmur & have had 7 teeth extracted.

22-07-26 Lucky is a worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still finding her feet. She is unsure of her surroundings and can be nervous around people at first. However, once she is being gently handled, she settles well, she simply needs time, patience, and understanding to help her build her confidence.

Lucky takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind, confident resident dog in her new home that she can look to for reassurance as she continues to gain confidence and learn about the world around her. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who are sensible and allow her time to settle in. She can be a bit flighty so she will need an extra secure home and garden as she builds trust.

As Lucky has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns about house training and lead walking. With gentle guidance, consistency, and plenty of encouragement, she has every chance to thrive.

In a loving, calm, and patient home, we are confident that Lucky will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion.

Lucky has arrived with a Grade 2 heart murmur that will need to be monitored in her new home. She has also had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Ulyssa
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fencing.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

19-07-26 Ulyssa has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a very scared little girl who is feeling overwhelmed by all the changes in her life. She will need plenty of kindness, patience and reassurance as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

Ulyssa is looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of helping scared ex-breeding dogs. She will need a family who understand that progress may be slow at times and who will allow her to build trust at her own pace without expecting too much too soon.

Ulyssa takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need to live with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who can help guide her, reassure her and show her that people and home life are nothing to be afraid of. Having a canine friend will be essential in helping her grow in confidence.

She has never lived in a home before, so her new family will need to be patient and understanding while she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She does not yet walk on a lead or harness and will need to first practice around the home and garden until she is feeling brave enough to venture further.

Ulyssa is a gentle soul who has a long journey ahead of her, but with experienced, compassionate adopters and the support of a confident canine companion, she will slowly begin to blossom. Watching a frightened dog learn to trust and enjoy life is incredibly rewarding, and Ulyssa deserves the chance to experience the love and security she has always missed.

Ulyssa has been given the Gift of Life by Lesley Beattie

name: Yahtzee
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a doggy friend in my new home. No cats please!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I've started harness training but I'm still unsure of the lead

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

18-07-26 Yahtzee is a sweet lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a lovely little girl who is still a little nervous around people, but she will accept a gentle fuss once she feels comfortable. Yahtzee really thrives in the company of her kennel friend, who gives her the confidence and reassurance she needs. Out in the play yard she is much more relaxed, enjoying the chance to have some zoomies, play, and then snuggle up in her cosy bed afterwards.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace and learn all about life as a much loved family member.

Yahtzee gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. However, she has not met cats well at the rescue, and will need a home without any cats.

As Yahtzee has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, walking on a lead and harness, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her to adjust to her new surroundings at her own pace.

Yahtzee is a gentle, sweet-natured little girl who is already beginning to show her playful side. With a calm home, a confident canine companion, and plenty of patience, we hope she will continue to blossom and enjoy all the comforts that family life has to offer.

Yahtzee has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Charlton

name: Tippins
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a larger doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats yet!

I would like a large, and secure garden that I can settle into.

I do walk on a lead, but am still gaining my confidence and will need support.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

06-07-26 Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a little apprehensive when she first meets new people, but she is already showing signs that her confidence is growing. Once she knows you, she enjoys a fuss and is happy to be handled. Tippins has a big personality and is a fun girl to spend time with.

At the moment, Tippins is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with at least one other confident resident dog for support and companionship. She has always lived with bigger dogs and seems happiest around them. Tippins can be a little bossy with less confident dogs, so she wouldn't be suitable to live with smaller or younger dogs. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see if she could adapt to being an only dog. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience that can understand her needs.

As Tippins has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she settles in and learns what home life is all about. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that can allow her time to settle into a calm environment.

Tippins already walks on a lead, but doesn't seem to be overly confident on this so she will need continued support as she learns, and once she has settled into her new home, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog so that she can continue lead training.

Tippins is a lovely girl with lots of character. She's already showing us what a sweet dog she is, and we hope that, with time and patience, she'll continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.

Tippins is now receiving regular cleanings from the vets for waxy ears and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Elana
description:
I can live with calm, older teens, aged 16+ who allow me time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden of at least 6ft to exercise in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I have lived in a home but I need to learn to walk on a lead.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home!

Elana is a nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. Although she came from a breeder, she has never been used for breeding and has never had any litters. We have been told she was born at the breeder's with a naturally small tail, which is why she was never bred from.

Since moving into foster, Elana has settled in beautifully. She is a stunning girl with the sweetest nature. On arrival, she trotted straight into the kitchen, gently greeted all of the resident small dogs, and soon found herself a cosy dog bed where she was happy to relax and watch home life going on around her. She enjoys observing everything around her and is becoming more comfortable each day. She can still be wary if people approach her too quickly for a fuss and may choose to move away, so she will need adopters who are happy to let her build trust at her own pace.

She absolutely loves other dogs and really enjoys their company. Elana has spent her life living in a rural setting, mostly off lead, and has had very little experience of people outside of those she already knew. Because of this, strangers can still be quite worrying for her, but having confident canine companions gives her reassurance.

Elana has also started lead walking and is travelling well in the van to the secure exercise field. She enjoys having a run around, although she is currently a little less confident in large open spaces. With time and encouragement, we think she will soon learn to enjoy these adventures even more.

Although she was not used for breeding, she will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand the background she has come from. Elana will need another kind and confident dog in the home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system as she settles into family life and continues to build her confidence. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who will provide her with a calm and understanding home.

Elana has lived in a home before, so she is familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. She sleeps quietly all night in the kitchen, is crate trained, and is happy to be left alone for sensible periods. She is a quiet girl who isn't a barker and has discovered that she is rather fond of her treats! She may still need some help with house training and lead walking as she continues to settle into her new routine. She will also need an extra secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to help keep her safe.

Elana is a truly gorgeous girl who we think will adapt wonderfully to family life if given the time and patience she deserves. With kind adopters, a confident canine friend by her side, and plenty of understanding, we have no doubt she will continue to blossom into a lovely companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would love a good sized garden to explore!

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was quite overwhelmed when he first arrived, but is starting to come out of his shell more and more each day. He can be worried when he first meets new people, but will now greet his kennel mummy with a wagging tail every day! Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

Cooper would love to find adopters who are experienced with dogs and, whilst not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who is quite overwhelmed to find himself here, but is starting to settle in and adjust to his new surroundings. Understandably, he is feeling quite scared at the moment, especially when he first meets new people. With those he knows, he is starting to come out of his shell and its lovely to see his confidence growing. Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Whispy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 2 mammary lumps removed and 2 teeth extracted.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes grumble or bark, but this has always come from a place of pure fear rather than aggression.

After spending a couple of weeks settling into her kennel routine, it is clear that Whispy has experienced very little kindness in her life. Her fears are deeply ingrained, and she has no understanding of what people's intentions are. When someone enters her kennel, she will often bark and grumble in panic because she is so frightened of what might happen next. Despite this, she allows gentle handling, strokes, and being picked up without any fuss, almost as though she has simply resigned herself to it. It is incredibly sad to see, and all she really needs is someone who will show her that people can be kind.

Whispy takes enormous comfort from other dogs and has formed lovely bonds with her two current kennel companions, who she happily shares everything with. She can be selective about the dogs she befriends and seems to prefer smaller, calm, gentle dogs rather than larger or more boisterous companions. Once she trusts another dog, they become an enormous source of reassurance, so she will need at least one kind, quiet, confident resident dog in her forever home who can help her navigate the world and show her that life doesn't have to be so frightening.

Whispy is looking for a calm, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that trust cannot be rushed. As she has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning everything from house training to settling into a routine. Walks are not something she is ready for at the moment, and her adopters must be prepared to let her progress entirely at her own pace. Gentle garden exploration will be much more appropriate until she feels safe enough to take the next steps.

Because Whispy is an older girl and her fears are so deeply rooted, she may never completely lose all of her worries or become the confident dog people often imagine. Her adopters will need to love and accept her exactly as she is, celebrating every tiny step forward without expecting her to become a different dog. For the right family, watching Whispy slowly learn to feel safe will be incredibly rewarding.

Whispy is a very special little lady who has spent far too much of her life living in fear. She deserves a safe place to call home, where she knows nobody will ever hurt or give up on her again. With endless patience, understanding, and unconditional love, we hope she can finally experience the peaceful and happy life she has always deserved.

She has had two mammary lumps removed at the time of her spay and has also had two teeth extracted.

Whispy has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Smith

Whispy has been on my section for a couple of weeks now and oh my goodness is she a heartbreaker. I have no idea what she’s been through in her life, but her fears are deeply ingrained. She has no trust in anything or anyone, apart from a select few dogs at the rescue that she has dropped her guard with. She has absolutely no idea about human kindness, nor what our intentions are. She grumbles and barks when we enter her kennel in pure panic, as she’s so scared of what we’re going to do to her. Even though she may sound a little scary, she lets me stroke her and pick her up absolutely fine .. kind of like she’s just given up. It’s quite sad actually.Whispy currently has 2 kennel friends who she gets on well with and shares everything with. One is a Shih Tzu Cross and one is a Poodle Cross. I have tried quite a few dogs with her and it does seem as though she favours smaller dogs to larger ones. And definitely calmer, quieter ones that don’t get in her face.Whispy will need a very patient and understanding home with adopters who have experience with very scared dogs. Because she’s on the older side, she may never truly lose all of her worries and fears, and may never become a ‘normal’ dog, and this is something her adopters will need to be okay with, and love her and accept her anyway. Things such as going out for walks are not currently in the near future for Whipsy, and it’s going to take a lot of time and gentle guidance to ease her into such things.This poor, sweet girl does not deserve to live her life in fear and panic mode. She deserves to have a safe place to call her own, where she knows nobody is going to hurt her. She deserves to be loved unconditionally, and to not be given up on no matter what.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down, and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes be a little grumbly, but this was simply because she is so frightened and overwhelmed by her surroundings.

Since then, she has started to settle in and is trying so hard to be brave. She can be vocal with people and is still nervous to approach you but with patience and kind handling she has been joining in on yard times and taking treats, but she still has a ways to go. Whispy has never known the kindness of people so will retreat to a corner when she feels stressed.

Whispy will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her all the time, patience and understanding she needs to settle and learn to trust.

She relies on other dogs for reassurance and so she will need at least one other confident, laid back resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and provide reassurance as she begins to build confidence. She can be selective over the dogs she enjoys spending time with however once she takes to a friend, she does so well with them and it boosts her confidence. She will need a very placid dog in the home who won’t worry when she is scared. She has had a few grumbles when meeting new dogs but she is just scared and needs time to develop a bond with them.

As she has never lived in a home before, Whispy will need kind and understanding adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will be too overwhelming for her at the moment and once she is more comfortable she can begin learning in a secure garden until she feels brave enough to venture further.

Whispy is a very special lady looking for an equally special home. She has missed out on so much in her life and will need a home who will take things day by day with her and give her the support and love she’s so desperate for.

name: Kira
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now spent a week in foster care and has made lovely progress. Her first day was understandably overwhelming, and she spent hours pacing around the garden, too frightened to come into the house. However, with patience and reassurance, she has already started to settle into her new routine.

Kira has grown in confidence over the past week and now happily follows her foster carer around the house, enjoying being nearby. She is curious about what is going on around her and is no longer fazed by everyday household noises. Although she is still a little shy, she will happily sniff an outstretched hand, gently take treats, and accept a little fuss as people pass by, even if she doesn't actively seek attention just yet. It seems that chicken is certainly the way to Kira's heart!

Kira has a healthy appetite and would happily help herself to the resident dogs' meals if given the opportunity! She enjoys the company of the other dogs and has even started joining in with their excited races up the garden whenever they spot a squirrel, although she's still learning exactly how the game works. She hasn't shown much interest in toys yet and hasn't quite discovered the sofa, but we are sure these milestones will come in time as her confidence continues to grow.

She has been wonderfully clean in the house from the very beginning, helped by having easy access to the garden, and she sleeps soundly through the night. However, she may some reminders of this in her new home. She is also happy wearing a harness, and her foster carers will soon begin introducing lead walking once she is ready.

Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can continue to blossom at her own pace. She will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. Her coat is also beginning to grow back nicely where she had alopecia, and she is looking healthier every day.

In the right home, we believe this gentle little girl has every chance of becoming a wonderful and devoted companion. With kindness, patience, and plenty of tasty chicken treats, Kira's future is looking brighter every day.

Kira has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

After a week in Foster Kira has made good progress. She found her first day here overwhelming and spent hours pacing the garden too frightened to come into the house.

A week later what a difference she now shadows her Foster Carer, is curious but not phased by household noises. Kira has a good appetite but given the chance will move in on the resident dogs food bowls.

She sleeps through the night and has been clean in the house from the start, helped by the back door always being open. Chicken is the way to win over the heart of this gentle little girl. She happily wears her harness and we will start lead training in the coming days. Kira will sniff a hand, take treats and accept a little fuss in passing but does not seek attention.

She has started joining in on squirrel alert racing up the garden with my girls but doesn’t understand the rules of the game. She has not shown any interest in toys and has not jumped up onto the sofa yet, Kira is not using a crate.

Kira’s coat is starting to grow back where she has alopecia.

Kira is a super sweet and gentle lady who has come to us from a breeder. At the moment, she is feeling quite unsure of her surroundings and will often stand completely still when approached, as she is still learning to feel safe and confident.However, after spending some time with her, Kira begins to relax and will even give a little tail wag, showing that beneath her shy exterior is a lovely girl who wants to trust. With patience, kindness, and understanding, we are confident that she will continue to come out of her shell.Kira is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace without any pressure. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, gentle garden explorations may be a great way for her to build confidence and start experiencing the world around her.Kira will need plenty of time, reassurance, and TLC as she learns that life can be full of comfort, companionship, and love. In the right home, we believe this sweet girl has every chance of blossoming into a wonderful and devoted companion.

name: Indie
description:
I would like an understanding home, and I can live with older children, 10+

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Indie is a gentle, sensitive little Poodle who came into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. When she first arrived, people were very unfamiliar to her and she found handling quite worrying. Although she was always trying her best to be brave, she would often shy away from people and needed time to learn that the world wasn't such a scary place.

Since moving into foster, Indie has already made wonderful progress. Like many ex-breeding dogs, she initially found life in a home quite overwhelming. For the first few days she struggled to settle, pacing around the house and barking during the night. However, after about a week she began to relax, and she has now settled beautifully into her foster home, sleeping soundly through the night and becoming much more comfortable with everyday household life.

Each day her confidence continues to grow. Indie is naturally very curious and enjoys following her foster carer around the house to see what's happening, especially if there might be something tasty involved! She's a big foodie, happily takes treats from your hand and, although she can be a little fussy with her meals, she's found a food she absolutely loves.

She's also discovering how much fun life can be. Indie enjoys playing with toys and absolutely loved exploring a secure field, where her foster carer saw her playful personality really beginning to shine. She is making steady progress with lead training, although she still finds walking on a lead quite frightening, so her new family will need to continue building her confidence at her own pace.

Although Indie enjoys gentle strokes, she isn't quite brave enough to approach people asking for affection just yet. She prefers to be close to her people without too much physical contact and continues to become more comfortable as her trust grows.

Indie has done brilliantly with her toilet training and is now mostly reliable, following a routine and toileting outside consistently during the day, although does have a puppy pad out at night incase.

One thing that has remained constant throughout Indie's journey is just how much she relies on other dogs. She absolutely must have at least one kind, confident resident dog in her new home. Having another dog gives her reassurance, helps her understand home life and encourages her to be brave enough to try new things.

She has met both adult visitors and visiting children in foster and has coped well, remaining calm and happy to share their space, although she tends to not actively seek attention. She has met older children in her foster home, and we believe she could live with older, dog-savvy kids who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

Indie is currently living in foster with a cat, but she isn't comfortable around cats and prefers to avoid them, so she is looking for a cat-free home.

When left for short periods, Indie may be a little unsettled initially but settles again quickly. She can wear a harness and use a crate with gentle encouragement and reassurance, and although she can still be a little wary of handling, her confidence continues to improve every day.

Indie is looking for a calm, patient family who understand that confidence can't be rushed. She will need adopters who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, celebrate the little milestones and continue showing her that people can be kind.

She has already shown just how much she can blossom when she's given love, patience and understanding. We truly believe that, with the support of another dog and the right family beside her, Indie will continue to flourish into a wonderfully loyal and loving companion.

Indie has been given the Gift of Life by Kimberley Page

Indie found living in a home quite overwhelming for the first few days and struggled to settle and would pace around. She also struggled to settle at night and would bark and howl. After a week of being here she has now settled and the barking at night has stopped completely. She toilets outside consistently during the day but at night needs puppy pads.Indie is very curious and will follow me everywhere checking on what I’m doing and wondering if I’m going to give her something nice to eat (she’s a big foodie). She will take treats nicely from me and does eat well although she is quite fussy with her food. I have found a food she loves so will discuss this with adopter.Indie likes to play with toys and has really enjoyed going to the secure field where she really showed her true personality. I am working on walking on a lead with her but it is slow progress as she is still quite frightened.Indie likes to be stroked but isn’t quite brave enough to approach me to ask for it.Indie will need a home where someone is willing to work with her and give her the space and time she needs to settle. Someone who won’t overwhelm her and just let her progress at her own pace. I truly believe that in the right home she will make someone a wonderful companion.Indie is very reliant on other dogs so will need at least one other dog in her new home to help her come out of her shell

Indie is a gentle and worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. At the moment, she is not comfortable approaching people in her kennel and will often shy away from her handlers. She is still learning that people can be kind and trustworthy, and she finds handling difficult right now, sometimes showing that she is touch-sensitive.

Indie will need a patient and understanding home with adopters who are experienced with, or knowledgeable about, ex-breeding dogs and the challenges they can face when adjusting to life in a home environment. She can live with older teens, aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her the patience she needs. She will need time to settle at her own pace and should never be rushed.

She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home. A friendly canine companion will help her learn about home life, provide reassurance, and support her as she continues to build her confidence.

As Indie has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning all the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. To begin with, gentle garden explorations may be the best way for her to experience the world while she gains confidence.

Indie is a timid girl who will need plenty of love, patience, and understanding from her adopters as she learns about trust, companionship, and all the comforts of family life. In the right home, given the time and support she needs, we believe she has every chance of blossoming into a happy and devoted companion.
