name: Nelly
description:
I will need an adult only home with breed-experience.

I’d like to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on the lead but I am strong, so I will need continued training!

I have lived in a home, but may need a few reminders as I settle in.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Nelly, also known as 'Nellyphant' amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

Nelly is a typical fun-loving Bulldog girl who is full of character. She loves attention, affection and being involved in everything her people are doing. She enjoys a good play session, especially when there is a ball involved! Tennis balls, footballs, honestly, anything she can throw around will make her happy. She is even learning that dropping the ball means the fun can start all over again. Once playtime is finished, she is just as happy settling down for a well-earned rest.

Sadly, the instability Nelly has experienced has left her feeling worried when she is left alone. She can become distressed when separated and will need a home where she is not left for long periods. Her adopters will need to build up time apart gradually, using patience and consistency to help her understand that her people will always return.

Nelly is currently learning about other dogs and is not yet comfortable around them. She is doing brilliantly with her muzzle training, which allows her to enjoy her walks safely while she learns that other dogs are not something to worry about. She can enjoy walking alongside calm, quiet dogs, but she may react if she feels overwhelmed, especially with larger dogs or if another dog barks at her first. Her new family will need to continue her muzzle training on walks and support her with positive, patient guidance.

Nelly can already walk on a lead, although she is a strong and enthusiastic girl who can pull when excited. She will need adopters who are confident handling her and who are happy to continue her lead training. She loves getting out for walks, having zoomies and exploring, but she is equally happy being a cuddle-loving couch potato afterwards.

Nelly has come from a home before, so she may already understand some household routines, but she may need gentle reminders as she settles into a new environment. She will need an adult-only home with breed-experienced adopters who understand her bouncy nature and can provide the boundaries, consistency and love she needs. She will need to be the only dog in the home, with no visiting dogs and no cats. She will also need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft+.

Nelly is wonderful at the vets and loves the attention she receives there. She enjoys spending time with the staff, soaking up the fuss and showing everyone what a friendly and affectionate girl she is.

Nelly is a resilient, loving dog who has been through more than she should have, yet she continues to greet the world with excitement and affection. She is ready for a family who will spoil her, make her feel safe and show her just how wonderful life can be. For lovers of Bulldog breeds, Nelly’s silly personality and loving nature are sure to bring endless joy.

*Nelly has been measured by our local Dog Licensing Officer and confirmed that she is not considered a banned breed.

Nelly, AKA 'Nellyphant', plays football and she’s amazing at it! She also absolutely loves a herding ball. In fact, Nelly would play with any ball or toy for hours if she had her way, and we have to remind her to take breaks and relax for a bit.

Nelly has an exuberant nature, and no day is bad when Nelly's about. Nelly is now muzzle trained and proudly trots along the lanes near the rescue, donning her bright pink muzzle.

Nelly really is a delightful, confident, and human-loving dog, and as much as she likes to play, she will settle down and chill, often contentedly hanging out with the office staff at the rescue whilst they're busy working away.

Nelly's ideal home would have no other dogs and adult humans who have plenty of time to play and hang out with her, as well as knowledge and experience of bull breeds.

This super lady really does deserve to find a lovely home of her own soon.

Nelly, also known as Hippo amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

name: Nana
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a large male resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am harness training and doing really well.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have some hormonal alopecia, but this should grow back. Read below for more!

Nana has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a sweet girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment and she is very nervous of being handled. We will continue gently helping her learn that human hands can be kind. If pushed out of her comfort zone, she may panic and choose to make the wrong decision, so it's important her adopters take things slowly with her.

Nana will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust. She can be quite vocal when she first meets you, but she is quick to make friends when you offer her some tasty treats.

She relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance, so Nana will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure. She gets along better with larger male dogs and so would need a larger male resident dog in her new home and cannot live with female dogs.

As Nana has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who will be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. Nana is harness training right now, and she’s doing really well but can be a diva sometimes. In her new home she will need to first practice in the garden as she builds confidence.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nana will begin to leave the past behind her and let her true personality shine through.

Nana has some hormonal alopecia, but this should start to grow back once she has been spayed. She has a small inguinal hernia that has been repaired and has had several teeth removed at the time of her spay.

Nana has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

Nana got to be a pampered princess today. Unfortunately, she needed to be shaved due to matting when she first arrived with us, but she has had enough hair growth now that she could have a fluffier haircut!

Although she's still nervous, she's come on leaps and bounds with being handled and picked up. She still finds humans a bit scary; however, you can tell she gets nosier every day and that bit more confident.

She took to the grooming like a champ, and although it was all very new to her, she really seemed to enjoy it and came out looking as cute as we all know she is.

Nana is a big personality in a small dog. She'd suit a bigger male dog in a calm and patient home. We all hope she's not waiting too much longer, as she truly does deserve the world.

She relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance, so Nana will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure. She gets along better with male dogs and so would need a male resident dog in her new home and cannot live with female dogs.

As Nana has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who will be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness, first practicing in the garden as she builds confidence.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Raven
description:
I need an understanding, adult-only home with ex-breeder experience.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I am in foster with a cat!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I love going for walks, but will need to continue gaining confidence!

I am in a foster home and doing well with house training!

I have Grade 2 luxating patellas, which may improve with exercise.

Raven is a sweet, curious girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived she was quite worried, but her confidence has steadily grown and her cheeky, comical personality is really starting to shine through.

She has been settling into foster life and continues to go from strength to strength. Home life was completely new to Raven at first and she found it overwhelming, but she has adapted beautifully and is now fully house-trained. She has embraced many of the comforts of home, loves relaxing on the sofa beside her fosters, and has quickly learned the household routine. In fact, she's always happy to remind everyone when it's dinner time, just in case they've forgotten!

Sadly, Raven was briefly adopted, but she struggled to form a bond with her adopters. As they found handling her difficult, Raven became frightened and, when she felt cornered, reacted out of fear by nipping. Since returning to her foster home, it is as though she has never been away. She settled straight back into her familiar routine and her confidence has continued to blossom.

Raven is still a naturally timid and sensitive little girl, but she has made incredible progress. She now actively seeks out affection from her foster mummy and always wants to be close by whenever they sit down. She will happily accept gentle fusses from trusted people and is beginning to extend that trust to visitors too, allowing them to sit beside her and stroke her. She can still be worried if unfamiliar people approach her whilst standing, although a tasty treat often helps, as Raven is a proper foodie!

She has such a lovely, gentle temperament and has been wonderful for bathing, grooming and handling. Following her return she needed to be clipped quite short, and she was an absolute star for the groomer, allowing herself to be fully handled. Her coat will require daily brushing to keep it looking its best.

Raven absolutely adores other dogs and must have at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide and reassure her. She relies heavily on canine companionship, gets on brilliantly with the dogs in foster, and is also living happily alongside a cat, who she ignores, so she could potentially live with a dog-savvy feline. She would find young children too much at the moment, but we would consider gentle, dog-savvy older teenagers who would allow her to settle at her own pace.

One of Raven's favourite parts of the day is walkies! She has gone from taking her very first tentative steps on a lead to genuinely loving her walks and walks beautifully without pulling. She has also seen light traffic, travels well in a crate in the car, and has started recall work on a long line, which is progressing nicely.

Raven is now looking for an experienced home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and the time they need to settle. She is likely to take a step backwards when she moves into a new home, just as she did previously, so she will need patient, confident and consistent adopters who will give her the time and space to build trust at her own pace. Once she feels safe, Raven truly is a wonderful little dog with so much love to give, and watching her become the superstar she is in foster will be incredibly rewarding.

Our vets have noted that Raven has Grade 2 patella luxation, which may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. She also had an abdominal hernia repaired at the time of her spay and has been treated for an ear infection.

I have been given the Gift of Life by Jean James

Since being unfortunately returned, Raven is thriving and going from strength to strength in foster. Her confidence has grown immensely. She has learned the house routines and likes to remind us when it’s dinner time, just in case we’ve forgotten! it’s actually very cute. She is fully housetrained.Raven will now actively seek touch and attention from us, and always tries to be next to me when I sit down (if the other dogs don’t get there first!) She will allow visitors to the home to sit next to her and stroke her, but will still back off from new people if they approach her standing up (unless food is involved - she is a proper foodie)

Upon her return Raven had to be clipped very short, she was a star for the groomer and allowed her to fully handle her. This girlie needs brushing daily.  Raven loves other dogs and her favourite time of the day is Walkies.

Raven is likely to regress when adopted, as she did before. She will need adopters who are confident and consistent with her, that will give her the time and space to feel brave enough to be the superstar she is here.

Raven is making sure and steady progress in foster. She is still timid and hand-shy, but will jump up on the sofa next to us and enjoys a fuss. She is a good girl to bath and groom. Raven has a lovely temperament and I haven’t seen her have even the slightest grumble at a human, cat or dog. She is now completely house-trained. It is so sweet watching her get excited to go out walking, she really enjoys it and is not a puller on the lead. We have started recall training on a longline and it’s going well so far. She has seen light traffic and been fine. Raven travels well in a crate in the car. She will definitely need a kind doggy companion in her new home. I hope her people find her soon, she’s so deserving of a loving forever home.

Raven has been in foster for just over a week. She was quite overwhelmed to start off with but is already starting to settle in and come out of her shell. She is a nosey little lady and her curiosity along with her love of yummy food helps her to overcome her fears. She is quick to learn about housetraining, and with good management accidents are rare. Raven gets along brilliantly with other dogs and ignores my cat. She would find children too much but could live with older teenagers who are patient and kind.

She is worried about being handled but tolerates it, If we put her on the sofa with us she settles down and likes a fuss.

We have started getting Raven used to being brushed. She will need owners that will take care of her thick curly coat and take her to the groomers regularly. Raven is a beginner on the lead but enjoys a walk and a sniff in quiet places. With time and love Raven will be just wonderful. Her temperament is lovely and we are starting to glimpse the comical, cheeky girl that she is destined to be.

Raven’s confidence has improved massively since she first arrived and her cheeky, curious and comical personality is really starting to shine through now. She is an absolute foodie and her favourite time of day is definitely treat time, or my dinner time!! She likes to see exactly what I have and figure out if she will like it too, and then politely ask me for a little share. She’ll put her two front paws on my lap and look at me with doting puppy dog eyes that I can’t say no to. She’s too adorable! She’s also a little thief and will try to steal things if you leave them out. This week she very sneakily stole a packet of crisps and started running around the yard with them!!! We were sat in the yard with her so she didn’t get very far with them, but it was so lovely to see her full of joy and almost like a ‘normal’ dog.

Raven is still hand shy with humans and will run away if you try to touch her or approach her, but she is okay to pick up once she jumps into one of her beds. She’s also had a bath and a groom since her arrival and she was a very good girl!! I don’t think it will take too long for her to get used to being touched and stroked, especially once she’s in a home. I think she will actually start to enjoy it in time!

Raven is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder. She can be a little worried at times, but she is easy to handle and very curious about the world around her.

Raven will need a kind and confident resident dog in the home to help boost her confidence and show her love and reassurance. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead, all at her own pace.

She could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers who respect her space as she settles in. With plenty of time, patience, and TLC, Raven will soon blossom into a loving and loyal companion.

Our vets have noted that Raven has Grade 2 patella luxation. This may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle, but it is something her adopters and their vet will need to monitor going forwards. She has had an abdominal hernia repaired at the time of her spay and is currently being treated for a ear infection.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Flash
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with ex-breeding experience to understand me

I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a good sized, secure garden to explore.

I can walk on a lead but find this very overwhelming at the moment.

I have entropion in both eyes, which have been repaired by the vets.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle with a big personality, a sensitive soul, and an oversized puppy spirit. He first came to us after his previous owners could no longer give him the time and exercise he needed. Since then, we’ve watched him grow from a worried boy into a much more confident and affectionate companion, and he continues to make us proud every single day.

Flash is still very much a character, goofy, playful, and full of energy but beneath his bouncy exterior lies a gentle heart that just wants to love and be loved. He can be sensitive in new situations and still finds the world a little overwhelming at times, but with people he trusts, his sweet and loyal nature shines through. Once Flash bonds with you, he is yours for life.

Recently, he’s been showing us more of his loving side. On rainy days when we huddle together out of the downpour, he rolls over for belly rubs, brings his toys for attention, and happily drifts off to sleep during a cuddle. It’s in these quiet moments that his true personality comes out, affectionate, trusting, and eager to please.

Flash’s training is going from strength to strength. He’s mastered “touch” (booping his nose to your hand) and is now learning “place.” He still gets a little mouthy when he’s overexcited, but he’s come a long way since his arrival and continues to improve with patience and consistency. He’ll need his future family to have ex-breeding experience and to continue this gentle guidance in the home so he can keep building on all the progress he’s made.

Being an active breed, Flash loves his walks and enjoys exploring the world at his own pace. He’s happiest in calm, quiet areas where he can relax and take everything in without feeling rushed. He will need to be the only pet in the home, as he prefers human companionship over other animals, and he’s not a fan of pigeons or seagulls either!

Flash has had successful surgery for entropion in both eyes, he received care for mild dermatitis around both eyes, but this has since cleared. He is currently being treated for sore and sensitive ears.

What Flash truly needs now is a calm, understanding, adult-only home with ex-breeding experience and with someone who’s around most of the time, someone who can offer him patience, structure, and all the love he deserves. With time and trust, Flash will repay his person a hundred times over with loyalty, affection, and that special spark that makes him so unforgettable.

Please don’t overlook this beautiful boy. Flash has come so far and is ready to start the next chapter of his life he’s just waiting for that one person to believe in him and bring him home.

Flash will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Flash has officially been waiting for a home for a whole year. After a first few months of (a lot of) patience and training, it's then blossomed into the most incredible remaining months where we’ve really seen Flash’s true heart and soul. This dog is phenomenal in more ways than one, and it’s so sad he’s now become part of the MT furniture, and that the rescue has now become his home.

So for Flash’s 1 year anniversary, I took him off site to the nearby country park for a lovely stroll, followed by a visit to McD’s for some chicken nuggets.

Flash was suuuuuuch a good boy on his walk. He took in all the new smells, and took the new environment in his stride. He was even approached by 3 off lead small dogs, and didn’t react at all. He trotted along the park, with the world at his feet and it was the most amazing thing to see.

He is an absolute darling in the car, so we made a swift visit to McD’s for a box of 20 nuggets to eat together in our on site flat.

It was so nice to see Flash in a home like environment, he jumped straight on the sofa, and wandered around inspecting every room. We sat on the floor together eating our nuggets, and he eventually rested on the raised bed and had a little snooze.

It was heartbreaking putting him back in his kennel, when he seemed so at peace and settled in the flat. I just wish there was someone out there who could see him for everything he is and more!!!

Our beautiful, bonkers Flash has learnt a new trick and we thought we would share.

Flash has also been enjoying the sunshine with lots of walks and plays in the yards this week.

Flash continues to work hard on growing his calmness around new people and he is doing ok. He has now been 10 months here at the rescue and has an increasing fan base amongst the staff but he of course longs for a home and people of his own.

When I first started working with him, I was apprehensive. He was a much larger dog than I was used to working with, and he would mouth you til his hearts content. Not because he is a nasty dog, or means any harm whatsoever, but simply because he has come from a home (just out of puppyhood) and he has become extremely anxious and unsettled being in a kennel environment. On top of that, he has been taught 0 manners which definitely didn’t help with the matter!!! I struggled to bond with him, I struggled to understand why he wouldn’t listen when being told, and why all he wanted to do was treat my arm like a toy…

However I found myself thinking, what has Flash been through in his life that was ever HIS fault? He didn’t ask to spend so much of his life in kennels. He never asked to be put in situations where his anxiety gets the better of him, it was never his decision to not be trained to behave normally. So I decided to buck up my ideas and realise he’s not as scary as he seems, and he’s probably just as anxious being around me as I was him. And from that moment on, our relationship has blossomed…

This boy is truly a superstar in every sense of the word. He is SUCH a goofball, and can have you in fits of laughter within seconds of being with him. His personality is infectious, and as soon as he is comfortable with you and realises you are no threat to him, he shines like the star he is. It’s gutting that Flash doesn’t allow every staff member to see all sides of him. The side that shows his softness, his sweetness, his kindness. But that just makes me so much more grateful that he feels comfortable enough around me to do so.

You can see from his pictures, Flash is muzzle trained. Not because he is an aggressive dog, not because he is a violent dog, it’s simply due to his anxiousness. On one hand, Flash is a super intelligent Poodle but on the other hand, he doesn’t really show it. His anxiety gets the better of him, and he puts himself in uncomfortable positions with new people & then panics whilst he’s in it. It is SUPER important that whoever adopts Flash’s main priority is keeping him safe, and keeping him from making decisions that he feels uncertain about. He wants to make friends with everyone, but also decides halfway through some interactions that he’s not to keen on the thought too!

Among (of course) all of the other precious angels I look after the rescue, Flash is one of the reasons I get excited to go to work. You shouldn’t really have favourites, but Flash does take the cake. I cherish every single moment I get with him. Our lovely strolls up the country lanes, our snuggles in the back of his kennel after a long day, our zoomies down our big play yard. Every single moment & memory I look forward to recreating every single day. Nothing tops being around this dog, nothing else matters when you’re with Flash.

If I was in a position to take him home & work with him through his quirks, I absolutely would, in heartbeat in fact. There is just something so special about him, and I truly envy whoever is fortunate to adopt this incredible young man. And for as long as Flash remains in kennels, I will advocate for him, make him feel safe, comfortable and most of all loved.

Flash has completely changed my mind about Poodles. I am absolutely in love with him. He might not be the sharpest boy in the bunch, but he more than makes up for it with his goofy charm and endless silliness.We are still working on his mouthing when he becomes overexcited. Progress is steady, and every small step forward feels like a real achievement. Flash loves his freedom. We take daily trips to the big yard where he runs around like the happiest whirlwind you have ever seen. He would really benefit from visits to private dog fields where he can safely zoom and explore to his heart’s content.Meeting new people can still be a little tricky for him, but we have a careful plan in place to help him do so safely and comfortably. For those of us who know Flash well, he shows a side many would not expect. Beneath his anxiousness and the need for a muzzle at times is the sweetest, softest boy who adores snuggles and head tickles.He loves to stay close, gently resting his head in your lap until he drifts off to sleep. At the end of each day, we share a quiet moment together, curled up side by side until his eyes close and he is peacefully dreaming.Flash truly is a special boy who deserves a very special home. He needs someone who can offer love, patience, and understanding. In return, he will give unwavering loyalty and companionship for life.

Flash is an absolute character, this boy is full of life and once he knows you he adores you but his introductions to new people always need to be slow as this sensitive boy can be easily overwhelmed.

Flash works well within a routine, he has an abundance of energy and a super inquisitive nature which can sometimes lead to him becoming quite lively, he will often revert to ‘mouthing’ and jumping up when he is uncomfortable or unsure.

Flash has a super inquisitive nature and loves to observe what’s going on at a distance. This boy can also be an absolute cuddle monster and adores a snuggle with his favourite people, and will fall asleep next to us when we have the opportunity to sit quietly with him. One of flash’s unique traits is his love of a pamper session! I have never known a dog who enjoys a bath and hairdryer the way he does and he becomes quite docile under the hair dryer whilst having a gentle brush.

Flash’s ideal home would be a quiet an experienced dog owning home (adults only) with humans that have the patience and time to help grow his confidence and who also understand the need to grow calmness in him. Flash has had a few dog friends at the rescue but his high spirted nature can be a bit much for some dogs and he does not seem to like male dogs, for this reason a home where he is the only pooch would suit him best.

Flash walks well on lead but can become very excited when he sees other dogs, walks in quiet areas would be perfect for him, he loves to be outdoors and often just enjoys sitting in the yard with me watching birds, but he will equally enjoy time spent just hanging out with his humans at home. Flash really is a wonderfully, lovable, giant puppy, looking for kind and understanding humans to provide him with the security and love he deserves.

Flash has had a brilliant few weeks. He celebrated his second Birthday and was treated with his first snow day, which he loved frolicking about in. Unfortunately, he did have to spend his birthday in kennels, but I made sure it was still a very special day for him. We hopped in the car, and I took him for a little walk before heading to the pet shop to pick out some birthday treats. He chose a dinosaur toy and a knuckle bone, which he thoroughly enjoyed. I also bought him some special birthday biscuits to keep him going through the week.

After that, I truly spoiled him, and we decided to go to Burger King for a burger! Flash was quite confused at first, but once he had a taste, he couldn’t get enough.

Flash truly is a special boy and will need a special home to match. He can be very wary of strangers and doesn’t always show clear signs if he’s uncomfortable. For this reason, he is muzzled when out on walks, which I make sure to do whenever we go out.

Flash will need an adult-only home with no visiting children. He cannot live with cats or any small animals

The stunning Flash had a little pamper today, which he absolutely loved. He was as good as gold whilst in the bath and sat very contentedly on the grooming table looking out the window enjoying the warmth of the blowers. I have never known a dog to enjoy bath time as much as he does, he becomes quite sleepy and cuddley, it’s the cutest thing.

After his wash and blow dry he got to open some Christmas treats out in the yard sent in from the lovely folks out there that support Many Tears, Flash particular enjoyed the food presents.

Flash really is the most wonderful boy once you get to know him, and we see improvement every day in his sometimes lively and skittish nature. This fantastic boy will make the most awesome and loyal of friend with the person or couple that are prepared to put the time and love into him he so deserves.

Today, Flash and I went on a little adventure to the local pet shop, finishing off with a much-needed pupcup! He was an absolute angel in the car—he hopped right in, buckled up, and sat calmly for the whole journey. I watched him in the mirror as he gazed out at the world passing by. When we arrived, we popped his muzzle on as a precaution since he can sometimes be wary of strangers. Flash wandered around the shop, taking in all the sights and smells, until he discovered the pick-and-mix treats—which of course we had to get. After choosing his goodies, he rummaged through the plushies and picked out a squeaky monkey to take home.

As we headed toward the till, another dog suddenly rushed around a corner and startled Flash, causing him to react. I managed to whisk him away with a distraction, but he became very on edge and tucked himself into me for comfort. A lovely lady then came around the opposite corner and, despite having seen his reaction, kindly stopped to say hello. She happened to be a previous Many Tears adopter, and her own pup is doing wonderfully. She chose to ignore Flash at first to give him space, and once he settled, he allowed her to gently stroke his head. After wishing us well, we carried on with our day.

We sat outside Costa in the sunshine, and Flash absolutely loved his pupcup, so much so that he managed to get it all over his nose.

I’m incredibly proud of Flash today. It was his first outing since arriving in kennels, and I could really see how scared he can be underneath it all, and how much he relies on his human for reassurance. Flash needs someone devoted, patient, and willing to put time into training and working through his reactivity toward other dogs. He truly is a special boy.

Another bleak day at the rescue with the rain pouring down non-stop, but it meant I got to spend some more quality time with the dogsI’ve never been one for poodles but Flash really has stolen my heartToday I really did see his loving and caring side as we cuddled away from the downpour. He rolled around, brought me his toys and chews before receiving belly rubs and head scratches until he fell asleep

If you’ve been to the rescue I’m usually walking Flash around the reception area in order for him to build his relationship with humans and other dogs but it was nice to just have some one on one time with him today, once you’ve created a bond with this boy he is yours for life.Flash’s’ training is still continuing and has managed to learn ‘touch’ where he boops his nose to the designated hand and is in the midst of learning ‘place’.

In a home will still need some training in order for him to thrive.

Flash is still a little mouthy when he gets super excited but is doing much better to when he first arrived with us.

It's been almost 4 months since Flash arrived here and I feel he has been very much overlooked. Deep down he’s a big cuddle bug and thrives on attention.

I tried spending most of my time with him today as kennel life is very stressful for him. We visited the big yard multiple times, went for a stroll and even met 2 dogs on a walk and greeted them with such kindness. Might I say he walks beautifully alongside you!

We met some new people in the reception area, which can sometimes make Flash a little uneasy but he did fantastically and even accepted some treats. For this he is muzzle trained as he can be mouthy when he’s a little too excited!

The last task of the day was to be groomed. I never thought I would see this boy sit still for more than a few seconds, but he amazed me and hopped up onto the grooming table ready to be pampered! And he now looks so good! Flash really doesn’t mind being groomed which will be helpful for the future.

I absolutely adore this beautiful boy. Flash is best described as an oversized puppy at heart. He has a playful, goofy nature but sometimes forgets his size, which can make him a little overexcited and mouthy, especially if he’s unsure or feeling frustrated.

Flash can be a sensitive soul who is often scared of his own shadow and needs plenty of reassurance and gentle confidence-building when faced with new experiences (like the umbrella he discovered today!). Because of this, kennel life is very tough for him, and I truly believe he will thrive so much more in a loving home.

Once Flash trusts you, he shows his affectionate side. He adores snuggling in for a cuddle and loves being pampered.

Flash’s ideal home would be an adult-only household where he can be the only dog. He isn’t aggressive with other dogs but can become boisterous and overwhelming. A quiet location with a secure, good-sized garden would be perfect, ideally with adopters who enjoy long walks and hikes.

He walks beautifully on the lead, enjoys all weathers, and has the stamina to go for hours. While he may sometimes react to new situations or get excitable around other dogs, his confidence and manners are improving every day. Flash will need adopters who are home most of the time or able to include him in their daily lives, as he finds being left alone difficult and may struggle with separation anxiety.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle who has come to us from a home as his owners no longer had time for him and couldn't offer him the exercise he requires. Although he has lived in a home before, Flash is a worried boy who finds new experiences and people quite daunting. Because of this, Flash is looking for an experienced, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time, patience, and love to give. He needs adopters who won’t give up on him and who will allow him to settle in at his own pace.Initially, Flash can be wary of new people and unsure of their intentions, but once you’ve gained his trust, he begins to show his affectionate and loyal nature. He forms strong bonds with those he feels safe around and shows a deep need for companionship. He does not cope well with being left alone and has shown signs of separation anxiety, getting very worried and anxious when left on his own. He will need an adopter who is able to be with him all of the time and who will work on this with him, slowly building up any time he is left. We are told he was crate trained in his previous home, which may help with this process.Flash is particularly sensitive to loud or sudden noises, which can cause him to panic. He feels safest in quiet, familiar surroundings and finds walks outside of the rescue grounds very difficult at the moment. When taken beyond his comfort zone, he becomes overwhelmed and spins in circles in an attempt to return to safety. While he can walk on a lead, his adopters will need to help him grow in confidence very gradually and may need to begin with simply enjoying time in the garden or short walks in peaceful areas.Flash would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as he can be grumbly when meeting other dogs. This is something his adopters will need to work on with him with patience and positive reinforcement. Because of this, he must only be allowed off lead in secure areas with no other dogs present. He also cannot live with cats or small animals and we are told he isn't a fan of pigeons or seagulls.Flash will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and where his adopters will help him settle into a consistent routine so he can feel safe and secure. We are told that he is house trained but he may need some reminders of this in his new homeAlthough he is currently worried about going for walks, he is an active breed who will need to be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. We have been told that he has previously done some agility and scent work, so once his confidence grows this is something he may like to explore again in the future. His previous owners also said he enjoyed being groomed and bathed, though we haven’t yet introduced this at the rescue.This beautiful boy has so much potential in the right hands. If you have the time, experience, and understanding to give Flash the security and stability he needs, he will reward you with trust, loyalty, and love. Please don’t overlook him, he’s waiting for that one special person to believe in him.Flash has an entropion in both eyes, which has been repaired by our vets but does have some dermatitis around his eyes.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Dutch
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is being trained to wear a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Grape
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I’ve learnt how to walk on lead but its still a bit scary for me.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training.

Grape came into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was a very worried little girl who clearly hadn't experienced much human interaction and found the world an overwhelming place. Despite her fears, she always tried so hard to be brave, gently accepting strokes while she learned that people could be kind.

Size wise Grape weighs approximately 14.5 kg. She's a lovely medium-sized girl, around the size of a cocker spaniel.

Fast forward a few months, and Grape has come on in leaps and bounds. She still has a sensitive soul, but each day we see more of the happy, playful little girl she was always destined to be.

When Grape first arrived, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, she recently enjoyed a proper makeover to show off what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped brilliantly, and by the end she was a gorgeous fluffy princess, looking every bit as special as she is.

One of Grape's biggest achievements has been her growing confidence. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she isn't quite 100% confident yet, particularly with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

She absolutely adores other dogs and gets on wonderfully with every dog she meets. Their company gives her confidence, and because of this shewill need a kind, confident resident dogin her new home to help guide and reassure her as she continues to settle into family life. We recently caught Grape playing for the very first time, doing joyful little bounces around a tennis ball. It may seem like a small thing, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step away from the life she once knew.

Although she's still a little nervous about human fuss, she now greets us every morning with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. She's also a complete sucker for treats, making winning her over much easier! She is still learning about life in a home, so her new family will need to continue her house training, build her confidence, and help her discover all the joys of being a much-loved pet. A calm, patient home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs would suit her perfectly.

When Grape arrived she was a little overweight, but with a healthy diet and gentle exercise she has been making great progress. She has also been through quite a lot medically since arriving with us. She has been spayed, had two teeth extracted, undergone a hernia repair, and had a small cyst removed during her spay. Her hormonal alopecia should continue to improve following her spay, and she has also completed treatment for an ear infection.

We truly cannot understand why Grape has been overlooked for so long. She has blossomed into such a sweet, gentle little dog, and while she will need a family willing to continue building her confidence, the rewards of watching her flourish will be immeasurable.

Grape has been given the Gift of Life Wendy Stewart

Sweet, sensitive Grape has now been with us for around three months, and we honestly can't understand why she hasn't had floods of interest. She is such a lovely little dog who has come on in leaps and bounds since arriving at the rescue.

When Grape first came to us, her coat was dirty and badly matted, so her first groom was more of a fresh start than a pamper. Now that her beautiful curls have grown back, we thought she deserved a proper makeover to show everyone what an adorable little teddy bear she really is. The bath was a little scary for her, but she coped so well, and she was an absolute star with the dryer (apart from preferring us not to fuss around her head too much!). By the end, she was transformed into a gorgeous, fluffy little princess, ready to strut around the rescue.

It's not just her appearance that's blossomed. Grape has grown so much in confidence over the last few weeks. She is now walking on a lead and is doing really well, although she's still not 100% confident, especially with people she doesn't know well. With someone she trusts, she is making fantastic progress and continues to improve every day.

One of the loveliest things about Grape is how much she adores other dogs. She delights in every dog she meets and loves having canine friends around her. We even caught her playing for the very first time, doing playful little bounces around a tennis ball. It might seem like an ordinary moment, but for Grape it was a huge milestone and another step further away from the life she once knew.

She can still be a little nervous about human fuss, but every morning she greets us with a waggy tail and the sweetest smile. Each day she lets her guard down a little more, and we're seeing more of the happy, playful girl she was always meant to be. She's also very partial to treats, which definitely helps when making new friends!

Grape would make a wonderful addition to almost any family that's happy to give her a little patience and understanding while she continues to build her confidence. We truly cannot understand why this gorgeous little girl has been overlooked for so long.

Grape is still a nervous girlie and is taking longer to trust humans, given we know nothing of her past this is understandable.

I am trying to show her that all I want to do is help her and show her love, while also respecting her space and going slowly with her, which is what her adopters may have to do depending on where’s she’s at.

She will allow a gentle fuss when she’s in her bed but will not willingly come up and ask for one yet. I think maybe in a calm home she will start to feel more comfortable, kennel life isn’t for everyone, and learn to trust humans.

She is a beautiful girl and I hope she starts to trust soon so we can see that amazing and sweet personality that I’m sure is hiding in her somewhere just bursting to come out.

Grape has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a scared girl who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and clearly isn't used to much human interaction, so finds this quite worrying at the moment. Despite her fears she will let you gently stroke her and is trying so hard to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace and would benefit from adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs. She gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Grape has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Everything will be new to her, so a calm and consistent routine will be important.

Grape has arrived a little overweight, but with a good diet and gentle exercise, she should soon start to shed the excess. She has some hormonal alopecia, but this should start to grow back now she has been spayed. She has had 2 teeth extracted as well as a hernia repair and our vets have noted she has a small cyst, which was removed at the time of her spay. She is also being treated for a ear infection.

Grape is a very worried little girl at the moment, but with time, patience, and the support of another dog, she has the potential to slowly gain confidence and begin to show more of her true character.

name: Davina
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I've started harness training but I'm still too scared to walk just yet.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

17-07-26 Davina came to us from a breeder and is now searching for a patient and understanding forever home. We have been told she is a Miniature Doodle (she weighs just under 10kg), but whatever her mix may be, one thing is certain, she's absolutely adorable.

Davina is a very gentle and sensitive little girl who is still finding the world quite overwhelming. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and relies on them for reassurance while she learns that people and new experiences aren't so frightening. Although she is beginning to observe what's going on around her, she is still a very worried girl who needs time to build trust and confidence.

Because of this, Davina is looking for a calm, quiet home with adopters who haveexperience of ex-breeding dogsand understand that confidence cannot be rushed. She will need people who are happy to let her settle entirely at her own pace, allowing her to make progress in her own time without any pressure or expectations.

Davinamust have another kind, confident resident dogin her new home. Having a canine companion is essential for her, providing reassurance, helping her understand home life and giving her the confidence to follow their lead as she discovers the joys of being part of a family.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be completely new to Davina. She will need help with house training, learning household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to everyday sights and sounds. Lead walking will also be something to build slowly, beginning with gentle introductions in the safety of the garden before venturing further afield when she feels ready.

Due to her nervous nature, Davina is looking for anadult-only homewhere she can enjoy a peaceful, predictable environment while she continues to blossom.

Davina is a sweet little soul who simply needs time, patience and understanding. Watching a frightened ex-breeding dog gradually discover that life can be safe and happy is incredibly rewarding, and we have no doubt that, in the right home, Davina will continue to grow in confidence and become a devoted companion.

Davina has been given the Gift of Life by Ceri Mann

name: Swanny
description:
I could live with dog savvy teenagers who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with a larger male dog. I cannot live with cats.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I do my best to keep my kennel clean, but may need help in a home!

Swanny is a truly lovely little lady who has come to us from a breeder and has been quietly stealing hearts ever since. With her unmistakable Beagle nose, Swanny loves to explore her surroundings and see what’s going on around her. While she can still have a slightly shy side, her confidence has blossomed beautifully during her time with us, and her sweet, gentle nature really shines through. She has become very people orientated and now absolutely loves some fuss and attention!

Over the past few weeks, Swanny has made wonderful progress. She is now walking beautifully on the lead and thoroughly enjoys heading out for walks or having a run around our big yard, where she shows her playful and inquisitive side. She also does her best to keep her kennel clean during the day, which suggests that house training in a home environment should be very straightforward with a little routine and patience.

Swanny has made friends with some larger male dogs here at the rescue and loves to go on play dates in our play yard with them. She can be quite picky with which male dogs she likes and can also be too enthusiastic and doesn't always read other dogs' signals, so she would only be suited to living with a calm, larger male dog who is very tolerant of her. Slow, sensible introductions would be essential. Thanks to her growing confidence, we now feel that Swanny could also live as an only dog in the right, understanding home where she can continue to thrive at her own pace or she can live with a larger, calm male dog. She cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Swanny has never lived in a home before, she will need kind and patient adopters who can help her learn the routines of family life. She could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in. With gentle guidance, consistency, and love, she is sure to settle quickly and become a devoted and affectionate companion. An active family who enjoy getting out and about would be ideal, as Swanny loves having both her mind and body kept busy.

Swanny has cataracts in both eyes, which do not appear to bother her at all. She has had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay, along with two teeth extractions. She also has one fractured pre-molar, which our vets have advised leaving for now, though it may need monitoring in the future. Swanny also has a travel document in place.

Swanny is an absolute delight to care for here at the rescue, and we truly believe that whoever opens their heart and home to her will be gaining a very special little dog who has so much love to give.

Swanny is the perfect dog, suitable to be an only dog. She would thrive in a home with owners who love cuddles and walking. She's the right balance of cuddly and active and an absolute pleasure to work with! She's been enjoying her enrichment toys with her treats and adores anyone who she comes in contact with!

She's honestly perfect and I can't understand how she hasn't found a beagle loving home yet!

Over the last couple of months, we’ve introduced Swanny to many larger male dogs at the rescue in attempt to find her an ideal playmate. Swanny is an absolutely comical girl, and no matter the size of the male dog, she will not hold back!!

Swanny’s main buddy is our Standard Poodle Flash, and every single day they have play dates. She is incredibly tolerant with his exuberant and playful nature, but also gives it as good as she gets. They have such a good balance between them, and once Swanny has had enough she will just take herself away from playing and have a good sniff around our big play yard, or steal some fusses off the first human in sight!

She has also had a play date with Charlie (a Great Dane X Mastiff) and his size did not phase her one bit, he was probably 3-4x bigger than her, but Swanny’s playfulness definitely trumped his size!!!

Swanny is not only an absolute delight to look after, but just being in her presence would make your entire day. She is as sweet as anything, she is kind, gentle, and loving. She is not built for kennels, she is build for sofa snuggles, big adventures, and endless love.

How Swanny has not been adopted yet is a mystery to me .

Perhaps it's her demeanor when meeting new people? Swanny can be a little shy at first but soon makes a connection and there's nothing wrong with being cautious.

Swanny walks beautifully on a lead and loves to sniff and smell the grass.

As Swanny does have enough confidence, she can live as the only dog in the house or equally she would be happy living with a larger male dog.

I would say, to see the true Swanny, you need to meet her, walk her and give her a little time to show affection. It really is rewarding when it happens.

Beagles are really pretty dogs and Swanny is no exception, so if you would like a beautiful beagle in your life, Swanny is ready to be the one.

Swanny is the sweetest angel, and it truly is a privilege to care for her five days a week. She has the most gentle and loving nature.

Swanny can be a little nervous when meeting new people, which is completely understandable, but with a bit of patience and kindness, she soon begins to show her true self.

Once you’ve built that special bond with Swanny, she becomes the most loyal companion you could ever ask for. She loves to  be close to you and will happily follow you around like you’re shadow!

Like a true beagle, Swanny absolutely loves her walks. The moment she’s outside, her nose is straight to the ground, exploring every scent along her way. Watching her take in the world through her nose is such a lovely reminder of how much joy the simple things can bring.

Swanny really is the most perfect dog in her own unique way. With the right family who can give her patience, reassurance, and lots of love, she will truly flourish.

She has so much to offer and would make the most wonderful addition to a caring and understanding home.

Swanny is such a sweet girl who is blossoming in confidence every single day!

Swanny has made so much progress over the last few weeks, I now believe she can be an only dog in the right circumstances.

Swanny does get on with larger male dogs absolutely fine, but prefers dogs who aren’t in the her face and give her the space she needs.

During her time here so far swanny has had a few disagreements with the male dogs she has shared kennels with when they get to much in her space.

Swanny is now walking beautifully on lead, and enjoys spending time going out for walks, or running freely down our big yard!

Swanny also tries to keep her kennel clean during the days, so house training should be a breeze!

Swanny is honestly a delight to look after here at the rescue, whoever welcomes her into their family are going to be very lucky people!

Swanny is a fabulous little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She’s an inquisitive girl with the unmistakable nose of a Beagle, always eager to explore and see what’s going on around her. Swanny can be confident when she chooses, but she still has a shy side, and with the gentle encouragement of her kennel friends, she’s starting to show her sweet, sociable nature.

She will need a confident, larger male resident dog in her new home to help her settle, guide her, and teach her about life in a home. Once she’s comfortable, Swanny would absolutely love an active family who can take her on plenty of adventures and keep her mind and body engaged.

Swanny is an absolute gem and, as she has never lived in a home before, will need patient adopters to help her learn house training, walking on a lead, and all the routines of home life. With kindness, consistency, and love, we believe she will settle quickly and become a devoted, loving companion.

Swanny has come to us with cataracts in both eyes, that does not seem to bother her. She has had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay as well as 2 teeth extracted. She also has one fractured pre-molar which our vets have advised to leave, but this may need to be looked at in the future.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Whimsey
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teens who are sensible and will allow me to settle.

I could live as an only dog, or with a similar sized canine friend. No cats please!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead, but will need guidance in the outside world.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Whimsey came to us from a breeder as a very worried little girl who found the world quite overwhelming. When she first arrived, she was unsettled and skittish, needing plenty of time and reassurance to help her feel safe. Since then, she has made wonderful progress and has really started to show what a special girl she is.

Whimsey has formed a lovely bond with her carers and now greets those she knows and trusts with enthusiastic cuddles and kisses. It has been a joy to watch her confidence grow, and she is becoming more comfortable with the people around her every day.

While Whimsey has come on tremendously, she can still be nervous and unsure around new people. She will need a calm, patient and understanding home that is willing to give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle at her own pace. Once she feels safe, her affectionate and loving personality truly shines through. She could also live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can respect her need for a gentle introduction and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Whimsey walks nicely on a lead, but as she can still be sensitive to new experiences, her adopters will need to continue introducing her to the world gently and at a pace she is comfortable with, helping her build confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Whimsey really enjoys spending time with other dogs and loves socialising with her canine friends in the exercise yards. We now feel she could happily live with another resident dog of a similar size, provided they get along well during a successful meet and greet. Like many dogs, Whimsey can be a little selective about her friendships, so finding the right canine companion will be important. She would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home, where she could soak up all the love and attention from her family while continuing to enjoy opportunities to socialise with other dogs on walks. She cannot live with cats.

Whimsey has such a sweet heart and has already shown just how much progress she can make when given kindness, patience and understanding. With the right home behind her, we know she will continue to blossom into a wonderfully affectionate companion and a much-loved member of the family.

Whimsey arrived with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which has been treated by our veterinary team. Our vets have also noted that she has a fractured canine tooth with no root or nerve exposure. At this stage, no treatment is required, but it should be monitored by her adopters and their own vet. She has also received treatment for a urinary tract infection, which has been successfully managed under veterinary guidance.

Oh, my heart. Whimsey has completely stolen it.

She is honestly one of the most loving, affectionate, and gentle girls I've ever met. The moment I walk into her kennel or sit with her in the yard, she melts into me. All she wants is kisses, cuddles, and to be as close to you as possible. She has so much love to give!

She's doing so well with her dog socialising too and absolutely adores her best friend, Royal.

Whimsey is going to make the most incredible addition to a very lucky family. She deserves so much more than just being someone's dog. She deserves to be a cherished member of the family, included in all of life's little moments, loved unconditionally, and never made to wonder if she's enough again.

I truly can't wait for the day she finds the home she's been waiting for. Whoever gets to call this beautiful girl theirs is going to be incredibly lucky.

Whimsey has come on so well since she first arrived. She’s bonded with me so much and always welcomes me with a big kiss and cuddle.

She can be nervous and unsure around new people, but with time, patience, and understanding, she’s going to make the most wonderful addition to someone’s home.

Although she needs to be the only dog in the home, she can happily socialise with other dogs and loves going down to the big yard with her friends.

Whimsy has come to us from a breeder and is a very worried girl. When she first arrived, she was very unsettled at the moment and could be quite skittish, finding so many of the sights and sounds of the world quite overwhelming. Since arriving she has started to settle in and come out of her shell, but will still need time and TLC as she settles in to her new life. Once she gets to know you, she will quietly approach you and allow a gentle fuss.

Whimsy needs time to learn and to trust, and needs a calm and quiet home home that understands ex-breeding dogs and will allow her the space she needs to learn about trust at her own pace. She will need a calm, patient, and understanding family who are willing to let her take things slowly and gently as she begins to discover the comforts of home life.

She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her home that she can look to and rely on as she learns about home life and settles in. Having a canine companion to guide her will really help build her confidence and show her that the world can be a safe and happy place.

Whimsy does walk well on a lead, but as she can be a bit skittish, her adopters will need to take the outside world at her own pace, allowing her the time she needs to gain confidence in her surroundings without feeling pressured.

Whimsy seems like she has such a sweet heart, and with time, patience, and kindness, she will begin to show her loving and gentle nature. She just needs someone special to help her learn about trust and companionship and to show her that she is safe and loved.

Whimsy has come to us with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which is being treated by the vets. Our vets have noted that she has one fractured canine, but no root or nerve exposure and so it is advised to leave it at this time, but will need monitoring by her adopters and their vet. She is currently being treated for a UTI and will be rechecked once the course of medication has finished.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I haven’t met cats

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I still haven't mastered toilet training so please be patient with me.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has now spent a week back in foster care and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people and enjoy all the love and affection he has missed out on. While he is still worried by some men due to his past experiences, once he trusts you his affectionate nature really shines through.

Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in his foster home and sleeps happily alongside them through the night. Although he enjoys their company, his foster carer feels he could also be very happy as an only dog, where he can soak up all the cuddles and attention he so craves. In the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he would thrive.

One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He now walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. He has settled quickly into his foster home's routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, but this has already improved over the last few days as he has established a routine. His adopters should still be prepared to continue his house training with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.

Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly, and you would hardly know he has any issues with his eyesight. He has also had all of his teeth removed, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.

Crispin really is a special little boy who has had a difficult start in life but has so much love to give. He is looking for a very special family who will understand his worries, cherish the affectionate little dog he has become, and give him the love and security he so deserves. In return, they will gain the most devoted and loving companion.

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.
