name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am a beginner on the lead but I'm not ready for walks yet.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who was understandably overwhelmed when she first arrived and desperately needed kindness, patience and TLC as she began to settle and learn that the world could be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialled on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a typical dog.

Since moving to a new section of the rescue, Nora has made huge leaps in her confidence. She is now harness trained and happily wears her harness throughout the day. She has become much more comfortable with handling and confidently walks on her harness to and from the exercise yard. Although she is not yet ready to venture out on walks beyond the rescue, she is making steady progress and becoming braver every day. Another wonderful milestone is that she now chooses to sit at the front of her kennel, curiously watching people and dogs come and go, rather than hiding away at the back as she once did.

Since arriving with us, Nora has slowly begun to show glimpses of the gentle and affectionate dog she has the potential to become. Like many nervous dogs, she can be vocal when she feels unsure, and her deep, defensive howl is very much in keeping with her Beagle heritage. However, with patience and a calm approach, she soon settles and begins to reveal her softer side.

Although Nora is still learning to feel comfortable around people, she is making wonderful progress. She is beginning to choose to settle near her carers and, once she has had time to relax, becomes much more accepting of gentle interaction. In these quieter moments she happily allows us to stroke and handle her, which is a huge achievement for a dog who once found every interaction so overwhelming.

It is clear that Nora's worries stem not from a dislike of people, but from uncertainty. Having had such limited life experiences, she simply does not yet understand who we are or what to expect from us. As her confidence grows, she becomes increasingly willing to be approached and reassured, and each small step forward is a testament to her resilience.

Nora would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. She will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. We believe that what Nora needs most now is the stability, security and reassurance that only a loving home can provide.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence. While Nora has successfully shared her kennel with smaller dogs, we feel she would be happiest living alongside a dog of a similar size or larger.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She is now comfortable wearing a harness and walking around the rescue grounds, but she is not yet ready to explore the outside world. Her adopters will need to continue building her confidence gradually, beginning with familiar surroundings before introducing new places at a pace she is comfortable with.

Although Nora is still a sensitive and sometimes worried little girl, the progress she has made has been nothing short of remarkable. Beneath her fears is a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a dog like Nora slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences imaginable, and with love, patience and understanding, we know she will continue to blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every step of that journey worthwhile.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.

name: Nuzzle
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with a dog my size or larger. I'm fine with cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have a Grade 1-2 heart murmur and have had 2 teeth extracted.

Nuzzle is a truly gentle, special little girl who has already come so far on her journey. She originally came to us from a breeder and, after a short adoption, sadly found her way back to the rescue as it was not the right fit for her. While in the home, she did make progress, but she was fearful of the man in the household and reacted out of fear on two occasions, showing that she needs very understanding, experienced adopters. She is now in a foster home where one of her fosterers is male and has settled in beautifully, which shows great progress for her.

When Nuzzle first arrived with us, she was an extremely nervous and flighty soul, spending most of her time hiding at the back of her kennel, too scared to join in or even accept touch. The world felt overwhelming, being in the yard, meeting people, or simply being handled was terrifying for her, and she lived in a constant state of panic and flight.

Since then, the transformation in Nuzzle has been truly heart‑warming. With patience, kindness, routine, and consistency, she has slowly begun to blossom. She now approaches her carers for gentle fusses and, when she feels safe, will even ask for more. She enjoys being groomed and is walking nicely on the lead.

She shared her kennel well with other dogs of a similar size and is now in a foster home where she is getting along well with the other dogs in the home. Nuzzle thrives when she has another kind, confident dog by her side and will need a resident dog, her size or larger, in her new home for emotional support and confidence-building. She can bond quite closely with her doggy friends and can get quite protective of them, so may prefer to be homed with just one other resident dog who can be her bestie. She is in foster with cats and is fine with them so could potentially live with a dog savvy cat.

Nuzzle is not a dog for busy or noisy environments and will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be patient, gentle, and consistent, allowing her to progress at her own pace.

Despite her fears, Nuzzle is a sweetheart who adores comfort, routine, and affection. She enjoys cosy beds, soft fuss, tasty treats, and the safety of familiar people and dogs. She is house trained and really enjoys the comfort of home life.

From a medical point of view, Nuzzle has a Grade 1–2 heart murmur which does not currently require treatment but should be monitored by a vet. She has had two teeth removed when she was spayed, and she also has a fatty lump on her side which currently requires no action.

Nuzzle has already achieved so much and continues to surprise everyone with her courage and gentle nature. She has incredible potential and, in the right home with the right support, she will continue to grow in confidence and trust. She is a quiet, affectionate companion who simply wants a safe, loving place where she can feel secure and cherished.

With the right family who will celebrate every small step and understand her past, Nuzzle will flourish beautifully and become a deeply rewarding companion.

Today I've had a very busy day. I'm so tired that, as I'm typing this, I'm falling asleep.

I've been for a walk with my foster brother, and it wasn't our usual walk, so I had lots of new smells and sights to check out. Afterwards, we both went to my foster brother's groomer, and I had another groom. I was so good and looked beautiful afterwards (as always!).

Then we visited Foster Nanny, where I had a treat and got to test out her sofa.

Nuzzle recently went out with her foster parents to visit some friends and was such a good girl. She happily accepted treats from everyone, enjoyed playing in the garden, and had a lovely time with their little dog, Beau. She was a little nervous when their friends' sister and her husband arrived, but after a little time she found the confidence to let them give her a gentle fuss.

Nuzzle is such a lovely little girl who continues to make fantastic progress in foster care. She has become much more confident with her foster dad and now happily jumps up onto the sofa for cuddles with both him and his wife. She is house trained and is walking very nicely on the lead in quiet areas while she continues to build her confidence.

Today was my first grooming day with my foster brother. As my foster brother was due to be groomed my new foster parents thought they would treat me to one too and I was so brave and good. Although I wasn't very keen on the dryer and I'm still not very keen on being picked up, I did so well. Now everyone says I look so beautiful and fluffy!

Little Nuzzle has been with us for week now and it brings me to one question, and that question is why has this little darling not got a forever home already?She really is a little star from day one she has been nothing but a pleasure to foster. Her toilet training is 100% (only one accident on the first day she came), she gets on well with all the other dogs here and also gets on well with our cats. She's had 4 other dogs visit and was fine with them also.She sleeps well throughout the night, eats well, loves treats and will take them out of your hand. She walks on a lead with encouragement in quiet areas. She will allow you to fuss her but can be a little hand shy when putting on her harness and lead so does need vocal encouragement.Nuzzle is looking for preferably an adult only home with at least one other fur baby to help her continue with living her best life. Potential adopters must also be aware of her grooming needs.

Nuzzle is desperately missing her home comforts and I think she would love nothing more than to be back in a warm, cosy house. The weather at the rescue has been SO bad over the past couple of months and even though her kennel is set up like a palace because she’s so good, it’s still not the same as a home. She ADORES being snuggled up in bed and it’s definitely her happy place. I can only imagine how grateful she’ll be once she’s back on a sofa. We can dream!!!

This sweet girl completely has my heart and is breaking it at the same time. I cannot emphasise enough how easy she is to look after at the rescue. She quite literally doesn’t put a paw out of place in any aspect. She keeps her kennel and herself sparkling clean, she runs to and from the yard and back to her kennel perfectly every time, she shares everything including food and toys with her friends, and she’s easy to bath and groom. From the perspective of a kennel mum, she’s pretty perfect.

Her best friend got adopted a couple of weeks ago and she has been a little quieter since, but she now has a new kennel friend that she cuddles with a lot and has taken a shine to. I would so love for her to find her forever brother or sister soon because it would make her so happy to have a constant soulmate in her life.

Nuzzle has been back at the rescue for just over a month now and I have to say it’s been an absolute pleasure to look after her. She was on my section the first time she was here over a year ago and it’s been so lovely to see the difference in her. She was a very, very frightened girl back then and extremely panicky all the time. She was basically living in flight mode and it was so hard to have to watch. When she arrived back last month I was SO surprised when she approached me to ask for a little fuss on the first day. That is definitely not the same dog I knew!!

For the first couple of weeks I left her to decompress and settle back into my routine, and thankfully she did this pretty quickly. Since then, we’ve been doing lots of harness practice and she’s doing SO well. She’s been so much of a good influence that she’s even helped her best friend Denise learn how to walk too - so now they go out together on little strolls up the road and back. She’s still not perfect and won’t be up for going for big hikes anytime soon, but she’s getting better every day.

Her favourite thing in the world is being snuggled up in the back of her kennel under a heat lamp. She has a huge donut bed which she shares with Denise and you’ll find her tucked in for the majority of the day. They often enjoy a dental stick each while in the donut bed too, and it’s so sweet to watch!!

Nuzzle has SO much potential and I am so certain that in the right home with adopters who know what they’re doing with ex-breeders, she will thrive. She’s come such a long way and I know she has more to give, so please give her a chance soon.

Nuzzle is a truly gentle, special little girl who has already come so far on her journey. She originally came to us from a breeder and was adopted for a short period of time but has unfortunately found her way back to us as it was not the right fit for her. While in the home, Nuzzle did progress in some ways but was fearful of the man in the home and acted out of fear on two separate occasions without warning.

When she first arrived with us from a breeder, she was an extremely nervous and flighty soul, spending most of her time in the back of her kennel, too scared to join in or even accept touch. The world felt overwhelming, and every new experience, being in the yard, meeting people, or even being touched, was terrifying.

But since, returning, oh how far she has come! With patience, kindness, and the comfort, Nuzzle has slowly begun to blossom. She now approaches her kennel mummy for gentle fusses and, when she’s ready, will even ask for more. She’s learning to walk on a harness, enjoys being groomed, and moves confidently to and from the yard as part of her daily routine. She shares her kennel with a few other dogs of a similar size, and she gets along beautifully with them, sharing food, curling up together in bed, and finding reassurance in their company.

Nuzzle thrives when she has another kind, confident dog by her side, and in the right home, she will continue to grow in confidence and trust. She still relies on her canine friends for comfort, so she will need a resident dog of a similar size or larger. She also needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be patient, gentle, and consistent as she navigates life at her own pace.

Despite her challenges, Nuzzle is a sweetheart who adores comfort and love. She has shown that she can be fully housetrained in the home, but may need a few reminders in her new environment. She enjoys cosy beds, soft fuss, and tasty treats, and has a bright, promising future if given the right support. She does have a Grade 1–2 heart murmur, which does not currently need treatment but should be monitored by a vet, and she had two teeth removed when she was spayed. She also has a fatty lump on her side which requires no action currently.

Nuzzle has already achieved so much and continues to surprise us with her courage and gentle nature. She is a quiet, affectionate companion who just wants a safe place to feel loved and secure. With the right family who will celebrate every little step she takes, Nuzzle will flourish beautifully.

name: Carys
description:
I need a calm and quiet home, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

24-07-26 Carys is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a larger girl with a typically sweet Cavalier nature. Carys is good with her kennel friends and clearly enjoys having other dogs around. She is easy to handle, although she can be scared when approached and may become submissive while she works out that she is safe.

Carys gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Carys has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and give her time to adjust to her new surroundings.

Carys will need an adult-only home that is calm and quiet as she settles into her new home. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand nervous dogs.

Carys has arrived with sore skin and a thinning coat. She will need a good diet and grrom, and our vets will monitor her to ensure she receives any care she needs. This will need to be continued in her new home.

Carys is a very sweet girl who is still learning that people can be kind. With the support of a friendly dog and a patient family, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the comforts of home life.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Millie
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

Millie is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She has been described as a big softy, and it's easy to see why. Although she has come from a breeder, we have been told that she has never had any litters. She has now moved into foster care, where she is gradually settling into home life. Millie is still a very worried girl who needs plenty of time and patience, but she is making gentle progress every day.

Millie spends much of her day relaxing in her favourite safe spot in the garden, where she feels most comfortable. She is still nervous around people and can become submissive when she is unsure, often lying down while she works out that she is safe. However, she is beginning to build trust with her foster carer and will now come over when called, lying down to allow a gentle fuss once she feels comfortable. She is particularly wary of men and remains especially nervous around her foster dad, so her adopters will need to understand that gaining her trust will take time and should always be done at her pace.

We have been told that Millie gets along well with all the dogs she meets, with a particular fondness for Poodle breeds! She is happiest with canine company and will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her reassurance. We still feel she would thrive in a home with just one other dog, as larger groups can overwhelm her and cause her to retreat into herself. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to help keep her safe while she settles.

Millie is becoming more comfortable with her daily routine in foster care. In the evenings, she comes inside and settles quietly in the kitchen, happily relaxing nearby while her foster carer goes about the evening. She sleeps peacefully on the landing outside the bedroom and is gradually becoming more familiar with life in a home. However, she is not yet ready to wear a harness or venture out on walks, and her foster carers are allowing her to progress entirely at her own pace. As she has never lived in a home before, she will still need help with house training, lead training, and learning all the basics of family life. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who will respect her need for space and allow her to settle at her own pace.

Millie is a gentle, affectionate girl who is trying so hard to be brave, but her worries still hold her back. She is looking for a very patient and understanding family who won't expect too much too soon. With a kind canine companion by her side and adopters who will give her all the time and reassurance she needs, we are confident Millie will continue to blossom and grow in confidence.

Millie is continuing to settle into foster care, but she is still a very worried little girl who needs plenty of time and patience. She spends much of her day relaxing in her favourite safe spot in the garden, where she feels most comfortable.Although she is still cautious around people, she is beginning to make gentle progress. When her foster carer calls her, Millie will now come over and lie down, allowing a gentle fuss once she feels comfortable. She is much more wary of men and remains especially nervous around her foster dad, so her adopters will need to understand that building trust with her will take time.In the evenings, Millie comes inside and settles quietly in the kitchen, happily relaxing nearby while her foster carer goes about their evening. She sleeps peacefully on the landing outside the bedroom each night and is gradually becoming more comfortable with the household routine.Millie is trying very hard to be brave, but her worries still hold her back. At the moment, she isn't ready to wear a harness or venture out on walks, and her foster carers are allowing her to progress entirely at her own pace. She will be looking for a very patient and understanding home that won't expect too much too soon. Given the time, kindness, and reassurance she needs, we are confident Millie will continue to make steady progress and grow in confidence.

Millie is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She has been described as a big softy, and it's easy to see why. Millie can be a little apprehensive in the kennel environment, but once she feels comfortable, she really enjoys attention and a gentle fuss. Although she has come from a breeder, we have been told that she has never had any litters. However, she will still need adopters with experience to allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Millie can be nervous when meeting strangers and will sometimes lie down and become submissive while she works out that she is safe. Taking things at her pace and letting her build trust will help her settle.

We have been told that Millie gets along well with all the dogs she meets, with a particular fondness for Poodle breeds! She is currently kennelled with dogs of a similar size and enjoys their company. Millie will need another kind, confident dog in her new home to help her settle and show her the ropes. We think she would be happiest in a home with just one other dog, as she can become overwhelmed in larger groups and tends to retreat into herself. She will need a secure garden of at least 6ft to help keep her safe as she settles in.

As Millie has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and give her time to settle into her new routine. She can live with older dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Millie is a gentle, affectionate girl who just needs a quiet home where she can feel safe. With a kind canine friend by her side and patient adopters, we hope she'll grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gary
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home with 4ft boundaries.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am missing my left eye, and I have been castrated & have had 1 tooth removed.

Gary is a very sweet and sensitive boy who has come to us from a breeder. He has now moved into foster and, despite his worries around people, has taken to home life like a duck to water. Everything is exciting to him, and he approaches the world with curiosity, happily exploring every room and taking new sights and sounds in his stride. Household noises don't seem to faze him at all.

Gary has also discovered his playful side and has very much switched into "puppy mode". He is as cute as a button and is always looking for his next adventure. If you turn your back for a few minutes, there's a good chance he'll have found something interesting to carry around! Thankfully, he is happy for his foster carer to gently take items away from him. He enjoys his food and treats, loves playing with toys, appreciates the freedom of the garden, and has quickly decided that sleeping on the family bed is the perfect place to spend the night.

Gary takes enormous comfort from the company of other dogs and is very dependent on his resident canine companions. He has formed a particularly lovely bond with the older male Dachshund in his foster home and is wonderfully determined to persuade him to join in with a game. Because of this, Gary will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his forever home to help guide him, reassure him, and continue building his confidence.

Although Gary has settled brilliantly into home life, he remains extremely frightened of human touch and handling. If he feels pressured or overwhelmed, he may react defensively out of fear. His adopters will need to understand that there will be no quick fix for this. Instead, they must be committed to earning his trust, respecting his boundaries, and allowing him to build confidence at his own pace through gentle, positive experiences. He is already showing what an intelligent and resilient little dog he is, and every small step forward is a huge achievement.

As he is now in a home, he will begin to learn all about house training and lead walking when he is ready, lead walking. A secure garden will be essential, giving him a safe space to explore while he continues to gain confidence.

Due to his sensitive nature, Gary is looking for a calm, adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs, where he can settle without pressure and be accepted for who he is. Gary has come to us missing his left eye, but this doesn't slow him down in the slightest—if anything, it adds to his unique and endearing charm.

Gary is a truly special little boy. He has already shown just how well he can adapt to family life when given patience and understanding. With adopters who are willing to invest the time to earn his trust, we have no doubt that he will grow into an incredibly loyal and rewarding companion and become a wonderful ambassador for his breed.

At the time of his castration, Gary had one tooth removed.

Gary has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Little Gary arrived in foster and has taken to home life like a duck to water. Everything is exciting and is to be explored and conquered, with no household item or sound yet phasing him.

He has turned on his puppy mode, cute as a button but if you turn your back for 5 minutes, he is off with something new in his mouth, but is happy for you to take this away.

He enjoys his food and treats, loves his toys, and very much appreciates the freedom of the garden and the security of sleeping on the family bed at night.

He is very dependent on my resident dogs and has taken a real shine to our older much bigger male dachsie showing great determination in persuading him to play.

Gary does however remain extremely scared of human touch/handling and if you push this, he may act out defensively in fear. There will be no quick fix. Instead this will be a journey of earning his trust, respecting his boundaries and slowly desensitising him to these fears. However this little boy is going to be so worth the investment and in time, will be a credit to the dachsie breed.

Garry is just the funniest little dude, and works hard ever day to become braver with us humans. Thanks to the kindness and perseverance of staff at the rescue Garry slowly grows more confident with us.

Garry has been deeply affected by his rough start in life and arrived terrified of everyone, hating being touched or just being near us. But day by day Garry gets braver and will now allow a little scratch under his chin or take a treat (he loves his food). It’s hard not to fall for Garry there is just something about him and within a patient loving home I believe the true Garry will shine through.

When you seem him playing with his friends in the yard he’s just adorable and happy. Garrys ideal home would be experienced with nervous rescues, have a resident dog and no children, or visiting children.

Gary is a very sweet boy once he gets to know you, although this can take a few meetings. He is very shy and timid in his kennel but will put on a brave front when you're outside it.

Gary is currently undergoing muzzle training as he can be tricky when handled. He is doing really well and is now able to tolerate gentle touches under his chin during his training sessions. Thankfully, Gary is a big foodie, which makes muzzle training much more engaging and rewarding for him.

I’ve been at the rescue for a little while now, and I’ve started to make some two-legged friends. I love the food they give me, especially the squeezy paste in a tube, and I’ll go right up to them now for that tasty treat. Sometimes, when they’re not looking, I’ll creep up behind them and check to see if there’s any in their pockets (but they don’t know I do this, so don’t tell them!).

I prefer it when the two-legged ones move slowly and quietly. It’s very unsettling for me if they rush about, and I’ll find a corner to curl up in and make myself feel safe when they do. On the whole though, they’re okay, and I love it when they let me go out into the big yards. I may be quite tiny, but that doesn’t stop me roaming around for all the good sniffs, and I don’t mind if they sit and chat with me while I go about my business.

Yesterday, one of the two-legged ones sat in the kennel with me. I curled up in my bed and watched them, and I even let them give me a little scratch. I think I would quite like some of these two-legged friends of my own, as long as they’re quiet and gentle (none of the small, bouncy ones!). A cosy bed of my own does sound rather nice, and of course I’ll need a four-legged friend as well.

Perhaps I’ll find some lovely two-legged friends soon… let me know if you hear of any.

Gary is a very sweet and sensitive boy who has come to us from a breeder. He currently finds human interaction quite overwhelming and can be touch-sensitive, so he needs time and patience to build trust. He is very much on the worried side and can react by snapping if he becomes frightened when being picked up, so it’s important that his adopters take a gentle, hands-off approach and allow him to come to them in his own time.

Although he is still nervous, Gary is beginning to take treats from people he knows well and has spent time with, which is a lovely sign of progress and shows his potential to build trusting relationships.

Gary takes great comfort from his kennel friends and has always lived alongside other dogs, so he will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, reassure him, and show him the ropes as he settles in.

As Gary has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be understanding while he learns about house training and walking on a lead. He is not yet used to lead walking, so a secure garden will be essential, giving him a safe space to explore and build confidence at his own pace.

Due to his sensitive nature, Gary is looking for a calm adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where he can settle in at his own pace without pressure. He will need plenty of time, love, and reassurance, but with patience and consistency, he will continue to make progress and grow in confidence.

Gary has come to us missing his left eye, but this doesn’t slow him down at all, if anything, it adds to his unique and endearing charm.

Gary is a little superstar who is trying his best in a world he finds quite overwhelming. With the right support, he will continue to blossom and form a deep, loyal bond with his future family.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jerry
description:
I need a calm and quiet adult only home with adopters with experience of collies.

I could live with another dog, or by myself. I cannot live with cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would like an active home and love to go for walks.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Jerry is a lovely boy who originally came to us from a breeder a few years ago and went on to find a wonderful forever home. Sadly, through no fault of his own, he has now returned to our care due to his adopters' ill health.

Jerry is a Collie lover's dream! He is affectionate, clever and eager to be part of the family. He is house trained, walks beautifully on the lead and we are told he has excellent recall too. He is a very smart boy who already knows a range of commands includingsit,wait,off,dropandleave, and he would thrive in an active home where he can be kept mentally and physically stimulated.

Since moving down to one of our field kennels, Jerry has become much more relaxed and settled. Being in a quieter environment has really allowed his wonderful personality to shine. He is incredibly loving and has shown us just how well he can socialise with other dogs. In fact, he has been so calm and sensible around them that he has even been used during one-to-one behaviour sessions with reactive dogs, where he has been an absolute superstar. Because of this, we feel Jerry could happily live with another well-matched dog, although careful introductions would still be important.

Jerry would still be best suited to an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of Collies and rescue dogs. He would love a rural or quieter home where he can continue to enjoy a peaceful lifestyle, and he would benefit from adopters who are around for much of the day and have plenty of time to spend with him.

Jerry has shown some signs of separation anxiety in the past, so his new family will need to continue building up the time he is left gradually. We are told that he is happy being left for short periods but will need patience and understanding while he settles into his new home.

One area where Jerry has made fantastic progress is with his noise sensitivity. While he can still notice unexpected noises, he is coping with them far better than before. Rather than becoming distressed, he is now much more likely to simply look towards his handler as if to ask, "What was that?" before moving on. His growing confidence has been wonderful to see, although his adopters should still be prepared to continue supporting him with gentle reassurance and positive experiences around unfamiliar sounds.

Jerry has settled back into rescue life beautifully. He loves a cuddle, enjoys a good play session and is an incredibly rewarding dog to spend time with. He is a truly special boy with so much love to give, and we know he has all the qualities to make an exceptional companion for the right family.

Jerry previously had a wound on his right paw which caused a limp. This has now healed well and he is no longer showing any signs of lameness.

Jer-bear, Jerry! This handsome boy is going to melt someone’s heart.

Jerry has come in from a home with a variety of noise related triggers but do not let this put you off meeting him, for he is one quick brave border collie. He was once visibly stressed at the sight of a can of pop and more stressed when carbonated drink cans/bottles were opened. He has improved and is not as stressed when he sees a can of pop and due to him moving around the rescue we have given him some time to settle as he wasn’t feeling himself in his previous kennel.

Since moving he has been showing us bit by bit his playful sassy side. He loves going for his morning walk to take a break from the overwhelming kennels, Jerry has even been socialising with other dogs. We have found that he gets on well with other dogs however if put into an overwhelming situation he is likely to redirect onto his kennel buddy so is safer for him and any other dogs if he is not homed with one. We have found that once he is comfortable with his people, he is quick to desensitise to certain triggers.

For example: one of his handlers is diabetic and uses cans of lucozade to treat hypos on walks and in kennels. He has become alert but has not reacted and is less anxious at the sight of cans or bottles now

When I first met Jerry I had heard about his triggers and was very curious, he is a very interesting young dog who is bound to be the light of someone’s life!

I have been working with Jerry for a little while now and have found that his can/bottle related trigger is a bit deeper than we were led to believe, the visual prompt causes him some stress, but found that he is quick to look for comfort. He really enjoys spending time with his doggy friends and looks to humans for comfort, and enjoys going out for walks, he seems to feel more relaxed on walks and have found once triggered by a noise he over analyses the indoor environment not so much the outdoor space.

During Jerry's stay here I plan to slowly introduce new noises and help him to understand that new noises are not necessarily a bad thing.

Jerry is a lovely boy who originally came to us from a breeder a few years ago and went on to find a wonderful forever home. Sadly, through no fault of his own, he has now returned to our care due to his adopters ill health.

Jerry is a Collie lover’s dream! He is affectionate, clever and eager to be part of the family. He is house trained, walks nicely on the lead and we are told that he has good recall too. He is a very smart boy who already knows a range of commands including sit, wait, off, drop and leave, and would thrive in an active home where he can be kept both mentally and physically stimulated.

Jerry would like to be the only dog in his forever home. He would be best suited to an adult only home and would benefit from adopters with collie and rescue dog experience. He would love a rural home, as he can be sensitive to certain sounds and so homes in busier areas wouldn't be suitable for him. He would really benefit from adopters who are around for much of the day and have plenty of time to spend with him.

Jerry does show some signs of separation anxiety, so his new family will need to continue building up the time he is left gradually. We are told that he is happy being left for short periods but will need patience and understanding while he settles. He isn’t keen on car travel, and he can be sensitive to sounds and may react to sounds such as fizzy drink cans or bottles opening, sneezing, coughing, nose blowing, printers, hoovers, microwaves, lorry reversing beeps, motorbike revving, army range noise and fireworks. He will bark towards you but with reassurance he settles quickly. He has never bitten and is just worried but his new owners will need to continue noise desensitization training in the home. It may never be something he entirely overcomes.

Jerry has settled back into the rescue well and is a wonderful boy who is already enjoying snuggles and really loves to play! He is a truly special boy who has so much love to give and is ready to find a calm, understanding home to call his own once again.

He has had a wound on his right paw that has caused a limp, which has since healed and he is no longer showing signs of limping.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to be the only dog in the home, and I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

22-07-26 Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

name: Nicole
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. When she first arrived, she was understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed. It was clear she hadn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands were quite worrying for her.

She has recently moved into a wonderful foster home where she is learning all about home life for the first time ever. She is settling in well and has a wonderfully inquisitive nature. She is still very worried about being handled and can bark when she's unsure, but she is making so much progress already. She will now take treats from her fosterer and absolutely loves her food.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust. She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole had never lived in a home before moving to her foster home, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her continue to learn everything about home life. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Toucan
description:
I would like an active, adult-only home with plenty of adventures and love!

I need to be the only dog in the home, and cannot live with cats!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden with 6ft+ fences to play in.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I am in a foster home and am house trained.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but unfortunately found himself back in rescue.

Toucan is a bright and friendly boy who enjoys meeting new people and, given time to build a bond, forms lovely relationships with his humans. He is affectionate and engaging, and with the right guidance, will make a wonderful addition to a committed home.

He is an active lad who loves his walks and exploring the world around him. At present, he can be strong on the lead as he is eager to get out and sniff everything he sees, so his adopters will need to continue working on his lead training and help him learn to walk more calmly. He is currently being trained to walk on a halti here. His absolute favourite thing in the world is playing with a ball and he just lives to play fetch! He would choose his ball over a treat any day and has proven himself to be the best ball catcher the rescue has seen!

Toucan is a clever boy who is picking things up quickly. He will benefit from a consistent routine and ongoing training to help him feel secure and understand expectations. Providing him with structure, alongside quiet resting spaces where he won’t be disturbed, will be key in helping him manage any anxieties. Although he has lived in a home, he may need some reminders about home life and skills like house training as he settles back into home life.

Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult-only home where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed.

Toucan spent some time in a foster home, but sadly it became clear that his preference was to be an only dog and he didn't enjoy sharing his home with another dog. He does get along well with other dogs when out and about and is fine passing them on walks etc, he would just prefer not to share his space with them. We think he is going to love being the only dog in the home where he can get all the love and attention for himself.

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn’t causing him any issues.

Toucan is a fun, intelligent, and affectionate boy who, with the right experienced adopters, routine, and understanding, will grow into a fantastic and rewarding companion.

Toucan has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Hale

Another month has gone by here at the rescue and still Toucan remains, poor boy isn’t having any luck.

Recently he’s started going out for long walks with one of our experienced volunteers and to say he loves it is an understatement, come rain or shine this boy loves to be outside, either walking or running around the big yard chasing his ball.

The lady that was fostering him also comes up regularly to spend time with him and he gets so excited when he sees her, which shows that once he loves you, he loves you forever and you have a friend for life.

Toucan is a very smart boy and you can’t really fool him by pretending to throw the ball because he catches on quickly that you haven’t, also he is very good at knowing where I’m pointing to. I don’t mean if I’m next to something and pointing right at it, I mean if he can’t find his ball for example, I can point in the direction it went and he’ll look at me and go that way, very very smart boy.

As much as I love Toucan and really enjoy his company, it’s time now for him to find his forever home, I know there’s someone out there for him, the right person could be reading this right now. If you think it could be you but your hesitant, don’t be, honestly Toucan is an amazing dog and everyone that has met him has nothing but lovely things to say about him.

Toucan spent some time in a foster home, but sadly it became clear that his preference was to be an only dog and he didn't enjoy sharing his home with another dog, so he has come back to kennels to continue the search for his perfect home.

Toucan is an absolute angel, but he does find kennel life quite stressful and can become vocal when unsettled. As a result of kennel stress, he can lose weight, so I’m keeping a close eye on him and making sure he’s getting all the nutrition and care he needs.

Toucan is a very active boy! His favourite thing in the world? A ball! He lives to play fetch. I can offer him a treat, but if there’s a ball around he’s much more interested in that. He is the best ball catcher at the rescue, the focus he has on that tennis ball is honestly something I admire. Besides his love for all things round, he is a genuinely sweet boy, who enjoys a fuss and of course a walk. He can be strong on a lead so for this reason I’m currently halti training him and although he’s not a huge fan yet, he is doing really well with it and is currently tolerating it.

Toucan is very trainable and tries his best to figure out what you’re asking him. He’s very smart and it breaks my heart that this beautiful boy is spending his days in kennels instead of out there in the world, playing fetch to his hearts content.

If you’re looking for a smart, active and adventurous best friend then please consider Toucan, he really is an amazing dog and he’s very handsome too.

Toucan is a lovely boy who has settled in as though he’s always been part of the family. He’s very confident and affectionate, and has happily met family and friends - he loves everyone, including my 17-year-old nephew.

He has a big love of food (including everyone else’s!), so he is fed in his crate using a slow feeder bowl to help him pace himself. He needs to gain some weight, so we’ve been adding extra protein to his biscuits and he’s already starting to look healthier.

Toucan is house clean and travels brilliantly in the car, happily jumping in and out. He gets on amazingly well with the four dogs in the home as well as friends’ dogs.

He is comfortable with the crate and, although the door is now left open at night, he still chooses to sleep in there. Toucan can pull on the lead, which we’re currently working on. He isn’t bothered by loud noises and absolutely loves playing ball - he’s fantastic at fetch.

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but has unfortunately found himself back in rescue. Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult only home, where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed. Please don't let this put you off, as he is truly a wonderful boy and his previous adopters have said how wonderful he is and will be in the right home.

Toucan is is always on the go, eager to explore, and looking for his next task. He has a vibrant, happy-go-lucky personality and would thrive in an active home that can provide plenty of attention, as well as physical and mental stimulation. He is super smart and loves to use his brain and already knows "sit", "paw" and "down." He is a lovely boy who is very affectionate and really enjoys having cuddles and fuss once he gets to know you.

Toucan is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog as long as his adopters had plenty of time to spend with him. He could also be homed with another kind resident dog and has shared his kennel well with dogs at the rescue. He can sometimes be reactive to other dogs when passing their kennels but is fine when out and about on lead. He still needs some training on the lead as he likes to be in charge, pulling us along on his travels.

Toucan has learned to walk on a harness, but he can pull and so will need adopters who can manage this and who are willing to work on this with him. He is obsessed with tennis balls and will play all day if you had the time, so he really hopes his new family will enjoy throwing balls for him!

Toucan can be a little greedy, so at the moment he is fed separately from any other dogs. He is a little and so he is now on a raw food diet to help him gain weight.

He had never lived in a home before his adoption and so home life is very new to him and he will need kindness and patience as he settles in. He was clean in his previous home but may have some accidents as he settles into a new home. With kindness, consistency, and plenty of opportunities to burn off his energy, he will make a wonderful, loyal companion for the right family.

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn't causing him any issues.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Laurence
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I am fine with cats.

I'd like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 16 teeth extracted and would benefit from a soft food diet.

Laurence is a sweet boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a loving forever home. He has been described as an absolute gentleman, and it is easy to see why. Although he can be a little wary when meeting new people, with a gentle introduction he is quick to make friends and enjoys gentle fuss and attention. He has settled beautifully into his wonderful foster home, where he has been experiencing home life for the very first time, and he has embraced it far better than anyone could have hoped.

Laurence has made incredible progress in foster and his confidence has grown enormously. He now walks calmly by your side, taking in the world at a relaxed pace, and thoroughly enjoys getting out and about. He has also taken wonderfully to home life, sleeping soundly through the night and happily settling wherever he is shown. He thrives on the comfort of a routine and has become a fantastic house guest.

Laurence gets on wonderfully with other dogs and relies on their company for comfort, so he will be looking for a home where there is at least one kind resident dog to be his friend, ideally one of a similar size. He loves the company of his canine companions and is beginning to discover the joy of playing with dog toys. He is in foster alongside three resident dogs, two large dogs and one small dog, males and females, and gets along with them all brilliantly. He is also living alongside a cat and chickens, so in the right circumstances he may be able to live with a dog-savvy cat.

A true gentleman, Laurence has now met people of all ages. He is polite and appropriate when meeting new people and, once he feels comfortable, happily accepts gentle fuss and affection. At home, he quietly seeks out cuddles from the people he trusts and has so much love to give.

Laurence would love to find a patient and understanding family who will continue to build on the wonderful progress he has made. He has embraced family life beautifully and is sure to thrive in a loving home where he can continue to grow in confidence. He will need a secure garden with 6ft fencing to ensure he remains safe.

Laurence has had 16 teeth extracted at the time of his neuter and benefits from having some of his kibble soaked to make it easier to eat, although he has an excellent appetite and enjoys a varied diet. He has also had a cyst drained from his left hip, which may recur in the future but should not cause him any problems.

Laurence is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. If you are looking for a calm, kind-hearted companion to share woodland walks, cosy evenings at home and all of life's adventures, Laurence could be the perfect addition to your family.

Laurence has been given the Gift of Life by Deb Huggings

Laurence has made incredible progress since moving into foster care. His confidence has grown enormously, and he now walks calmly by your side, taking in the world at a relaxed pace.He loves the company of dogs of a similar size and is beginning to discover the joy of playing with dog toys. His appetite is excellent, and he enjoys a varied diet, with some of his kibble soaked to make it easier to eat.Laurence sleeps soundly throughout the night and is happy to settle wherever he’s shown. He thrives on the comfort of a home routine and has embraced family life beautifully.A true gentleman, Laurence has now met people of all ages. He is polite and appropriate when meeting new people, happily accepting gentle fuss and affection once he has been introduced and feels comfortable.At home, Laurence enjoys his cuddles and quietly seeks out affection from those he trusts. He has so much love to give and will make a wonderfully loyal companion for a patient family who will continue to help him flourish.If you’re looking for a calm, kind-hearted dog to share life’s adventures—from woodland strolls to relaxing evenings at home—Laurence is waiting to meet you.

Laurence has now been in foster care for just over a week, and he has settled into home life remarkably well. He quickly adapted to the household routine and has been fully housetrained since his very first day.

He currently lives happily alongside three resident dogs - two large dogs and one small dog, both male and female - and has had no issues with any of them. Although he prefers to sleep downstairs on his own, you can often hear him listening to the gentle snuffles of the household upstairs during the night.

At home, Laurence is becoming increasingly comfortable with his foster carers. He now happily accepts gentle strokes much of the time and is beginning to enjoy human affection more and more as his confidence grows.

As with many newly rescued dogs, Laurence is still very aware of open gates and exits. For his safety, his foster home uses a second gate as an extra layer of security, and his future home will need to be mindful of this while he continues to settle.

Overall, Laurence is a wonderfully calm, gentle soul with so much love to give. He is looking for a patient, understanding family who will allow him to continue building his confidence at his own pace. In return, they will gain a loyal and affectionate companion who is already showing just how much he has to offer.

Laurence is a sweet boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a loving new home. He has been described as an absolute gentleman, and it is easy to see why. Although he can be a little wary when meeting new people, with a gentle and patient introduction he is quick to make friends. Once he feels comfortable, Laurence will quietly slink over for more fuss and attention, showing his sweet and affectionate nature.

Laurence gets on wonderfully with his kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so he will need a kind resident dog in his new home to help guide him and give him the reassurance he needs as he settles in and finds his paws.

As Laurence has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. His adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he adjusts to a completely new environment and learns that home life can be full of comfort, kindness, and love.

Laurence is a gentle soul who thrives on calm companionship and reassurance. With the support of a canine friend and a family willing to give him the time he needs, we are sure he will continue to grow in confidence and blossom into a wonderful companion.

A truly sweet and loving boy, Laurence has so much affection to give and will make a lovely addition to a patient and caring home.

Laurence has had 16 teeth extracted at the time of his neuter and would benefit from a soft food diet going forward. He has also had a cyst drained from his left hip, this may recur in the future but shouldn't cause him any issues.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears.
