Please note that Bentley would thrive in an adult-only home where he can live safely with his strict diet and no temptation for food outside of his prescribed meals.

We know Bentley has so much love to give, and with your help, he’ll find the perfect home where he can live the rest of his days surrounded by warmth, love, and cuddles. Thank you for considering giving this incredible boy the life he deserves!

name: Mischu
description:
Mischu is an 11 year old male Cross-Breed. He must live in a dog and pet-free home. Mischu came to us with his sister Iza after spending 8 years in a shelter with very little human socialization.

When they came to us they were very scared and shy dogs. He is very bonded with his sister but isn’t keen on other dogs so if they are rehomed separately he needs to be in a pet and dog-free home.

When they arrived they were both very scared of everything, but over time have relaxed into life here and become firm favorites with our volunteers.

Mischu is the most confident of the two, but his little sister Iza definitely wears the pants in their relationship.

Mischu loves doing the zoomies, snoozing, food, and a cuddle.

He will need work on lead training so his family will need a secure home and garden to begin his training.

If you can offer him, love, comfort and patience we would really like to hear from you.

name: Tessa and Tosca
description:
Tessa and Tosca are 5 year old female Cross-Breeds. They must live in a child-free, pet-free, and dog-free home and would ideally be rehomed together. Tessa and Tosca were in a shelter together for 3 years before coming under our care.

During that time they were well cared for but did not receive as much human attention as they perhaps needed. As a result, they came to us as very timid pups and have both been adopted separately and come back to us as they were too timid apart to live in a home.

We would therefore love to see these girls adopted together as they rely on each other for their confidence.

At the rescue they enjoy playing, sleeping, and cuddling.

Tessa and Tosca have done a little lead training at the rescue, but we would need a family willing to put in the time and effort to gain their trust and work on their training slowly and with our support.

We know it’s a big ask to find these two a home together, but we like to dream big for our dogs.

name: Bullet
description:
Bullet is a young male bull lurcher; about 15 months old and 27″ to the shoulder.

Bullet is fine with children (but too boisterous to be rehomed with very young kids because he might knock them over).

Toilet trained. (but currently in kennels, so may need to readjust to being in a home again)

Bullet is being trained to walk nicely on a lead – currently he pulls quite strongly.

Any new owner will need to be prepared to continue with this training.

Bullet shows some signs of distress at being left so will need patient new owners who are around for much of the time (at least to start with); and who are prepared take time to build up how long he is left home alone.

Bullet is at LURCHER LINK RESCUE, near Halifax, West Yorkshire.

name: Mozze
description:
Mozze is a 2-year-old male cross-breed dog, currently in foster in Oxfordshire, UK.

He’s a firm favourite among the staff at Perrera Dogs UK.

Despite spending the last two years at the shelter due to his hip dysplasia, Mozze is a stunning and friendly boy who deserves a loving home.

He is dog, cat, and child-friendly (ages 10+), although he is nervous around men.

The charity has agreed to cover the cost of his necessary hip surgery, but potential adopters will need to be assessed for their suitability for his lengthy recovery period post-surgery.

Mozze is of medium size, fully vaccinated, and has undergone a health check.

name: Max
description:
Max – 5 year old male Whippet x Terrier mix is about 23 inches to the shoulder. He was adopted from Lurcher Link two years ago but has come back due to his owner’s declining health.

Max is now sharing his kennel with Dolly. They love playing together, and Max is actually pretty tolerant of the very exuberant Dolly! We think he would be best rehomed with a steady female dog.

Max can be a little nervous around strange dogs and may bark, but he’s fine with other dogs once he gets to know them. He was a bit nervous with strange people when he first arrived back at the kennels, but he’s absolutely fine with everyone here now, including all the volunteer dog walkers.

Max is anxious about being left home alone and can be quite vocal. He will need to be adopted where he is only left for short periods (at least to start with) while his separation anxiety is worked on.

Not suitable to live with cats or young children.

Max is at Lurcher Link Rescue, near Halifax, West Yorkshire.

Homecheck and adoption fee will apply. More details about Max can be found on the Lurcher Link Rescue forum.

name: Travis
description:
Travis is a 6 year old male German Shepherd Cross. He is from Romania born on the 30 Oct 2017 and came into rescue along with his 2 siblings and has not been rehomed with them yet due to his disability.

Travis has been with us in the UK since May 2018 and now we would love to find a very special home for this very special boy.

Travis was born with issues in his hips and the many vets in Romania diagnosed many different things but it was only when he came into our care and saw our vets (and had more X-Rays) that we confirmed a diagnosis. Travis does not have any hip sockets – they never formed.

So his hips do not stay in place and move about which he moves. He has never needed any pain relief and is a strong dog and copes very well and isn’t in any pain.

Initially, our vets said he should be PTS but after seeing him playing very happily, in no pain and with the strength that he has in his front end he agreed he has a great quality of life and deserves a chance to live it to the full.

Travis loves running around the garden and playing so needs a nice big garden and lots of space.

We do need his home to have an understanding vet who is willing to work with us if necessary for any decisions on his future treatment and this would be part of our adoption contract. Fabulous with other dogs especially boy dogs.

Travis can be funny with new people and can be a bit barky. It doesn’t take him long to warm up and we think it’s a bit of territory guarding as he is fine when out and about.

Travis walks fine on a lead and travels well in the car and has been well-behaved at the groomers.

Travis would be perfectly happy in a home where he never goes for a walk as long as he has a big garden to run around and people to give him love and attention.

Travis is a very sweet soul. If you can offer Travis the extra special home and family he needs we would like to hear from you.

name: Mojo
description:
Handsome Mojo is a 3-year-old male dog currently residing in a Romanian private shelter. He was rescued from a distressing kill shelter and has undergone rehabilitation at the CHR Pet Rescue Centre.

This gorgeous boy is now prepared to make his way to the UK in search of a loving home.

Mojo, a 27kg neutered dog, has been fully vaccinated and undergone blood testing, including screening for brucella. Despite his challenging past, Mojo has proven to be an affectionate companion, showing a deep appreciation for his caregivers.

Prospective families interested in welcoming Mojo should be active, committing to providing him with two daily walks and engaging in mental stimulation activities. In return, they can expect to be rewarded with the companionship of an amazing dog.

It’s important to note that Mojo is compatible with another active female neutered dog, but he is not suitable for households with cats. Additionally, Mojo thrives in the company of older children, making him an ideal companion for families with kids aged 7 and above.

For those considering adopting this wonderful dog, the Pennypaws rescue team offers full support. As a registered charity with the number 1200959, Pennypaws is dedicated to ensuring that Mojo finds a caring and responsible forever home.

If you are ready for the rewarding experience of welcoming Mojo into your family, please consider providing a loving home for this handsome boy.

name: Bobby
description:
Bobby is a 5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a friendly and resilient dog who, despite being a tripaw, enjoys going out for walks and exploring at his own pace.

While he is not overly energetic, Bobby still appreciates regular outings and would enjoy being part of an active, yet relaxed, household.

He is good with other dogs and previously lived with a female Lurcher, suggesting he could be a good companion in a multi-dog home.

Bobby is also suitable to live with children over eight years old, mainly due to his strength. His nature is gentle, and he thrives with human companionship.

Bobby’s journey has been difficult. He was adopted by a loving owner, but sadly lost his home again when his adopter passed away just six months later.

Now in rescue in North Wales, Bobby is ready for another chance at finding a permanent, loving home. He is neutered, immunised, microchipped, and has been treated for fleas and worms.

Bobby would be an ideal companion for someone looking for a loyal, steady friend. He deserves a home where he can be loved and feel secure, especially after all he has been through.

name: Lenny
description:
Lenny is a 5 year old male Labrador Retriever Cross.

Lovable Lenny is a big goofball who has so much love to give, we are pretty sure that his heart is just as big as he is!

He’s a giddy, animated boy who loves to play with toys.

He is not one for sharing but enjoys a game of fetch, be careful on the way back though as he has no brakes!

Once he has had a good run Lenny is a real couch potato who he enjoys his own space.

We often find him snoozing on a lounger in the sun or lazing about in his bed.

Lenny can be unsure of strangers and will require slow, sensible introductions.

He can react defensively if he is unsure about a situation or feels threatened.

He will need an experienced and confident owner who is familiar with handling reactive dogs, someone who can read his signals and keep him safe.

We are looking for an adult only home for Lenny, without visiting children. He could be left alone for several hours as he is clean and non destructive.

Lenny is a bright boy and loves food which makes training a breeze.

He needs stability and routine, once he knows what is expected of him he is very well mannered and compliant.

Lenny is selective with other dogs and prefers the ladies, however we do feel he would be best suited to being the only dog in the home. He cannot live with cats.

He is extremely bright, wants to learn, has no idea of his size, weight or what is acceptable behaviour at the moment. Because he gets excited very quickly, he can also become frustrated very quickly so any training that is to be done with Lenny needs to be very short, with plenty of reinforcement of the good elements we want to encourage.

Lenny wants to do the right things, but is confused sometimes. So calm, confident and very clear work is to be done to help him move forwards.

If he gets confused he can jump up so it is really important you are calm around him. We would then advise that to encourage a sit/wait and reward it. He is not able to cope with ‘no’ or negative interactions at all.

It appears that Lenny struggles to relax and calm his mental ability down to think rationally. This is another reason why any interactions need to be short at the beginning. Short and regular is going to help Lenny develop more concentration, less questioning and confusion, and in turn proper self confidence.

Lenny wants to do the right thing and is eager to please. However, if the timing is not right then frustration can easily take over. He is also developing the stabilising part of his brain at the moment and that is why he can handle some interactions, but not lots of stimulus.

He needs to go to a home with space, a large garden, calm large breed experienced owners who will be willing to help him learn and make the right life choices.

Lenny is truly is one of the forgotten ones, one of ‘the dogs that no one wants’ and it breaks our hearts as he is the most beautiful boy.

We are hoping that someone with the right knowledge and skills can see the potential in this black beauty.

Part/full time foster homes will also be considered for Lenny.

name: Reggie
description:
Reggie is a 3-year-old Bull-Lurcher, a delightful young lad brimming with joy and playfulness.

Standing at 25″ to the shoulder and weighing around 26kg, Reggie is an intelligent and trainable companion. His repertoire of tricks includes sit, paw, high 5, and wait, showcasing his sharp mind and eagerness to please.

Affectionate and fond of cuddles, Reggie is excellent with people and enjoys engaging with his favorite toys, particularly balls.

While Reggie can display initial exuberance on the lead, he typically settles down during walks.

Unfortunately, his previous owner had to relinquish him to Lurcher Link Rescue due to the demands of a full-time job, leading to separation anxiety issues.

In a foster home, Reggie’s separation anxiety improved with careful handling, but he still requires an understanding owner willing to gradually build up his tolerance to being left alone.

Consequently, he wouldn’t be well-suited to prolonged periods of solitude.

Reggie is compatible with other dogs during walks, but it’s advised that he does not share a home with another canine companion.

Neutered, microchipped, and vaccinated, Reggie is currently residing at Lurcher Link Rescue near Halifax, West Yorkshire.

Please note that a home check and adoption fee are applicable.

name: Bravo
description:
He is a Romanian mioritic (mio) cross. He is four years old and currently in foster in Essex.

Bravo is excelling in the care of his fosterers, he’s now just waiting for the perfect forever family to come along and fall in love with him too!

Bravo is more suited to someone who knows about the typical mioritic traits. He has been tested around livestock, he’s not a fan of horses, but sheep he does not seem to mind.

He is a rather large boy! 37kg! A strong handler would be better suited for bravo. He is not a fan of cats or children I’m afraid! Bravo doesn’t mind being the only dog in the home but he wouldn’t mind a nice calm dog, that would happily leave him to it.

Bravo bonds tightly with his people so a careful and slow paced introduction to his new humans will have to happen.

When bravo does bond with his people though it is done very strongly and he loves cuddles! He is neutered and vaccinated and has been health checked.

name: Stormzie
description:
Meet Stormzie, an 18 month old male Rough Coat Lurcher who is truly special.

Stormzie had a rough life before coming to us and was on the run for over a week before being trapped and rescued.

It has taken a long time for him to trust his foster parents, as he is nervous around new people and remains a timid, scared boy.

Stormzie is house trained and loves all the dogs he has met, often doing amazing zoomies in the garden.

His best friend is Bramble, and they play and run around the garden like overgrown puppies.

His forever home must be prepared to do several meet and greets at the foster home.

The ideal home will need a fully fenced garden and someone who can be around often.

Stormzie cannot live with cats, and the home should have children aged 14 years and older.

name: Meghan
description:
Meghan is a 2 year old female Spanish Mastin.

Meghan was first taken into rescue at 6 months old, when she was found wandering the streets of Spain on her own. She was adopted in the UK and was raised as a pet for the next year.

However, due to the intensity of her character and her propensity to guard, she ended up back in foster – this time, on a farm that has working livestock guardian Mastins.

It was quickly evident that those same instincts that made her a handful as an adolescent pet could be molded into the traits that make up an amazing livestock guardian dog.

Now, 8 months and a lot of training later, Meghan is a tried-and-tested working livestock guardian dog with an impressive set of skills. She has been trained with poultry – chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese.

She naturally protects against both land predators (foxes, badgers, otters, and more) and aerial predators (in our case, magpies, crows, and buzzards) – basically, anything that shouldn’t be in, near, or above her boundaries will be chased away. This includes mice/rats – a very useful skill for a poultry guardian dog to have!

Through a fence, after being properly introduced, Meghan is friendly with male dogs. She will happily interact with male dogs when on a lead too but shouldn’t be off-lead with them.

She’s prone to resource guarding random things from them, which can lead to a fight. Like many female LGDs, Meghan doesn’t like female dogs. She will mostly ignore them from a distance but makes a lot of noise if they approach her fence line.

Meghan isn’t 100% trustworthy around cats. It’s best that she doesn’t have direct access to them, but can coexist with them on the same smallholding. The 2 cats she currently lives with choose to stay away from her.

With people, Meghan is extremely friendly and sociable. She is gentle and sweet with children too. She loves being the centre of attention but also always has one eye on her surroundings – she will quickly abandon a cuddle if she spots something that needs to be investigated further!

Meghan is a very independent and intelligent dog. She needs an adopter who understands how sensitive yet stubborn livestock guardian breeds can be. The two of you will need to be a team, so the focus at the beginning needs to be on bonding.

She isn’t a machine that’s going to immediately start working for you on day one, but once she has a solid connection with you, she would give her life for you/your animals. She is an amazing protector of her boundaries.

Meghan is currently in foster in Aberdeenshire, Scotland. We’re hoping to find her a local-ish home, so that we can do a gradual transition. However, if you live further afield but have the perfect home for her, we would consider that too.

name: Maia
description:
Maia is a 1 year 3 month old female Spanish Mastin Cross who was found as a puppy, with her mother and siblings, and taken into rescue.

One year later and she’s still in kennels, constantly overlooked in favour of fluffier and “cuter” dogs.

Since Maia has spent most of her life in kennels, she hasn’t seen much of the world.

As a result, she’s shy around strangers, but bribe her with some treats and she’ll soon be asking for belly rubs!

Maia’s mum is a small Mastin, and Maia has inherited the Mastin ‘look’ and typical calm/gentle nature.

She’s much smaller than a Mastin though – she’s currently only just over 30kg.

Maia is currently in kennels with her sister, Tootsie. The two get on incredibly well – they spend a lot of time alone together and don’t ask for much.

It would be amazing if they could be adopted together, but they can also be homed separately.

They are currently in Spain but can travel to the UK/EU.

Please get in touch if you’re interested in adopting Maia (or Maia and Tootsie together!).

name: JiJi
description:
JiJi is a 1 year old female Cross-Breed. She has travelled from N.Macedonia for a new and safe life. She was hit by a car at just six months, she suffered from a fractured pelvis. This is now healed but there are signs of historic injury in her gait.

JiJi has lived with other dogs, is tolerant of cats and after initial nervousness adores her keeper.

Jiji is having to grow up fast in an unsympathetic country that doesn’t allow a puppy time to be just that, hence the move to the UK.

Stunningly beautiful, Jiji will win hearts with her good looks. She is immunised microchipped flea/wormed and spayed. She has travelled on a current passport.

name: Daphne
description:
Daphne is a young female lurcher (born Jan 2024). She is 24” to the shoulder and weighs 25kg. She has settled down well in her foster home in Falkirk, Scotland

Daphne loves other dogs and gets on well with the 3 other dogs in the foster home. She absolutely loves playing with them but is boisterous, and plays roughly and often noisily.

She has been slowly learning some manners around the other dogs and will respect the one dog who doesn’t want to play.

Daphne is excellent at meeting other dogs outside of the house. Daphne’s ideal home would be one where there is at least one other confident dog who would enjoy plenty of boisterous play.

Daphne loves all people and loves a cuddle; she’s very friendly . She gets very excited and will jump up at people (and lick them!); her foster carers are working on teaching her to keep all 4 paws on the floor instead.

She’s very bouncy and can still sometimes be a bit mouthy, so would not be suitable to live with young children.

Daphne currently pulls on the lead and is quite strong; her fosterers are working on improving her lead walking. Daphne needs a good off-lead run everyday in an enclosed secure field or large garden. She will need a secure garden with 6-foot fences.

Daphne is very eager to please and quick to learn, and is very food motivated. Daphne has been to a 1-2-1 flyball session, and she absolutely excelled – the trainer was so impressed with her and how quickly she picked it up.

She really enjoyed it and was so tired afterwards. An activity like flyball, scent work or agility where Daphne can use her brain and could channel her energy would suit her. Daphne also enjoys puzzle and search games in the garden.

Daphne is toilet trained and travels well in the car. Daphne sleeps right through the night.

Daphne does not like being left home alone for too long. She has been left successfully for a maximum of 1 hour in the company of other dogs.

This is something that can be worked on, and the time spent left home alone should be able to be built up once she has fully settled into a new home (this cannot be rushed).

Ideally a home with at least one other confident dog would be best, to provide her with support and company when left home alone.

Daphne can be possessive over food and toys; she will growl at the other dogs and try to steal all the toys. Therefore her fosterers have been carefully supervising any playtimes with toys and she is being fed separately from the other dogs.

The fosterers think that Daphne resource guards due to insecurities and lack of confidence.

She has not lived with other dogs before but has made some progress in her foster home – with sensible guidance it’s likely she will continue to slowly improve.

Daphne cannot be rehomed around sheep (due to an unfortunate incident with her previous owner), and must be kept on-lead when walked in areas with livestock.

Daphne’s ideal forever home is one where there is at least one other confident dog to help her with her separation anxiety and has similar energy levels and would enjoy lots of playtime; but who is also tolerant of her resource guarding.

Alternatively she could be rehomed as an only dog (so the resource guarding wouldn’t be an issue), but she’d need a lot more exercise and mental stimulation and the separation anxiety would be more challenging to improve.

name: Varja
description:
Varja is a 3-year-old female Galga with a caramel coat, standing 60cm tall and weighing 20.8kg. She was rescued unexpectedly when she entered a trap cage meant for another dog.

When the person who had organised the rescue refused to take her, Galgos del Sur stepped in and took responsibility for her care. Varja arrived in the UK on 14 December 2024 and is currently in Essex.

She is neutered and in good health, although she has tested positive for Leishmaniasis, which is stable and well-managed with daily Allopurinol and a low purine diet.

She also has microphthalmia in one eye. Despite her difficult beginnings, Varja is a noble and sweet-natured dog who simply needs a quiet and safe environment where she can build trust and feel secure.

Varja is calm by nature but becomes scared in the presence of humans, particularly in unfamiliar situations. She requires a patient, experienced home with another confident, gentle dog who can help her feel at ease.

She is sociable and submissive with other dogs, showing no signs of dominance. While shy with strangers, she blossoms when given time and understanding.

Her favourite things include food, especially peanut butter, sleeping, and peaceful countryside walks. She has a few special talents—like appearing seemingly out of nowhere, being incredibly sweet, and showing brave resilience despite her fears. She is also cat workable, which adds to her suitability for the right home.

Varja’s ideal home would be in a quiet, rural area with a patient family and a resident dog to support her confidence. With kindness and time, Varja is sure to become a cherished companion.

name: Fraggle
description:
Fraggle is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed who is disabled; he’s never going to be winning a marathon or climbing a mountain, but he is a young dog with lots of mischief on his mind!

The perfect home for Fraggle will have at least one other dog to bomb around with – he is used to a whole pack and would enjoy a variety too.

He likes the attention of children, but his disability makes him clumsy and spatial awareness isn’t his speciality so he would knock a very small one over.

He can live with cats but if they are going to run away from him then he will make a game of chasing. A bold cat that will bop a nosey dog on the nose is fine.

A garden is essential for Fraggle. He does like to lie outside, as shepherds do and he isn’t physically capable of doing several long walks a day so he needs a nice garden to play in.

Fraggle is extremely friendly and affectionate with all people including groomers and vets.

Fraggle is 2 years old and we’ve spent several thousand pounds on his treatments and investigating his future prognosis.

We will not be abandoning him and we are happy to discuss foster-to-adopt and future security for possible big vet bills that won’t be covered by insurance.

We want Fraggle to have the same chance to be adopted as everyone else with financial assistance from us.

name: Victor
description:
Gentle is the word that we would first choose to describe this handsome Shepherd boy.

After being rescued, Victor was placed in private kennels for over 3 years sponsored by his rescuer. But life in kennels is not what a dog deserves, especially this sweet boy.

We are so happy that he’s with us now and we will make every effort to make sure that this lovely boy finds his happy ever after!

Victor is an absolute sweetheart! He’s affectionate and always up for a cuddle even with people that he’s only just met. We think that he’d be happiest as an only dog as he seems wary of other dogs.

Even though he was in kennels for so long, he wasn’t integrated with other dogs and it has left him a little fearful of them. Victor shows no aggression towards dogs, but he isn’t trusting of them.

Now that he’s relaxing into his new surroundings at the sanctuary, his playful side is coming out. He likes toys and will run after them and enjoys a game of tug. He walks well on a lead and we believe will be very responsive to positive reinforcement training.

We’re all in love with this gorgeous boy and think that he’s going to make a wonderful companion for someone. Homes with children over the age of 14 will be considered.

SPDC adoption package and homechecks apply.

name: Celine
description:
Our extra special girl Celine is approximately three years old and a medium sized cross breed.

Celine weighs twenty-three kilos and measures fifteen inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned on the streets, Celine has been in our Cyprus shelter for three months.

Celine is the most strikingly attractive dog. She has a soft brown and white coat, gorgeous ears and beautiful eyes that are totally and absolutely engaging.

The shelter manager describes Celine as an exceptionally loving girl. She so loves socialising, and her biggest passion is her tennis ball.

Celine is pleasant, well behaved and affable which presents her as an easy-going low maintenance adoption candidate.

Whoever is Celine’s fortunate adopter they will be truly blessed and very lucky to have her as part of their lives.

Celine mixes perfectly well with cats, other dogs and children. She walks nicely on her lead albeit with a foible. Celine stops after approximately four paces and then likes to catch up.

name: Dobbie
description:
Our extra special boy Dobbie most certainly is extra special! He is approximately two years old and a Greek Shepherd cross. Dobbie weighs a mere thirty-five kilos and is magnificent.

He was surrendered to our Corfu shelter a year ago with his sister as their owner was unable to keep them any longer.

Dobbie is striking and a real showstopper. His black coat with his white chest, tummy and tips are just glorious. The breed is known for its gentility and kindness and Greek Shepherds make wonderful family pets.

Experienced adopters will recognise however that there can be a tendency to be a little overprotective with their loved ones.

Dobbie loves water and thoroughly enjoys his walks and recreational pursuits. Sadly, Dobbie walks with a slight limp having had surgery for hip dysplasia. A veterinary report is available.

Dobbie walks nicely on his lead. He seems to mix well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Bim
description:
Meet Bim, a two-year-old neutered male originally from Cyprus.

Bim doesn’t have a disability, but he was living with his pack on a beach next to a busy main road. We are slowly finding homes for all the dogs that live on the beach, and we hope not too slowly.

In the summer, they are fairly safe because the tourists who attract them to the beach feed them, but at the end of the season, when the tourists are gone, the dogs start to cross the road looking for food.

This is the dangerous time for them, when they will be hurt or killed, so we need to find great homes now.

Bim lived on the beach with his mother and sister. His mother is adopted in Warrington, and now it is Bim’s turn to find a home.

Bim is very sweet and friendly. We believe he is a cross between a Labrador and a Pointer. He is a lover of the outdoors and would be a loving companion for a family with teenage children who want an active dog.

Bim is immunised, microchipped, and flea/wormed. He has a current Cypriot passport, so he can travel with his family.

Wolfies Legacy adoption donation applies, and a home check is required. Usually, your dog will join you within a week.

name: Lennox
description:
Lennox is a 2 year old male Lurcher. He needs a new home. Lennox is one of the lucky ones, we had a space for him when his time was up at the stray pound. Lennox is 25-26″ to the shoulder. We don’t know anything about Lennox’s past because he was found as a stray.

When Lennox first arrived he was very anxious around strangers, especially men; however, over time he has become much more confident around people he knows, and only takes about 5 minutes or so to warm up to new people (he’s initially scared and backs away).

Lennox is not suitable to live with cats or other small furries, and we won’t rehome him with young children as we do not know what he will be like with them. Lennox may need housetraining – we do not know if he has ever lived in a house before.

Lennox is friendly with most other dogs and is very lively and playful with the right dog. He can be initially a bit selective with who he likes/dislikes, however. OVERALL LENNOX IS A NICE LAD WHO JUST NEEDS SOME TRAINING AND STABILITY IN HIS LIFE. He is neutered, microchipped and vaccinated. Lennox is at LURCHER LINK RESCUE, near Halifax, West Yorkshire.

name: Bailey
description:
Bailey is a 7 year-old male lurcher. He’s 25″ to the shoulder. (Mum was a greyhound x whippet, dad unknown)

Bailey was rehomed by Lurcher Link 5 years ago. Sadly his current owner is no-longer able to care for him and so he is looking for a new home.

Bailey is fine to be left home alone for reasonable amounts of time.

Bailey knows some commands : “sit”, “down”, “wait”, “look”, “come”.

Bailey has not had the exercise he needs recently due to his owner’s ill-health. Unfortunately this has meant that he has become reactive with other dogs and can be anxious at times – for example at the vets (due to the proximity of other dogs).

For this reason we think Bailey would be best rehomed somewhere where he will not meet many other dogs on his walks, while his new owners work on building his confidence and resolving this problem.

Bailey has previously lived with children.

name: Rio
description:
Rio is a neutered male Cross-Breed of 18 months old.

As a pup, his front leg was damaged, and after two failed surgeries, it was amputated.

The decision was made to bring him to the UK, as he was too sweet and gentle to survive the streets of Romania. Now he is looking for his lifelong home.

Rio is good on the lead, fully house trained, immunised, microchipped, flea/wormed, and has a current passport.

He has been in training for six weeks, living with other dogs and children, but he is not suitable to live with cats.

Rio is a very good boy and will be the best member of any family.

name: Delia
description:
Delia is a 2-year-old female Spanish Mastin Cross, with clear sighthound traits in her appearance and behaviour. She is looking for a forever home where she can continue to build her confidence and trust.

When she was first rescued, Delia was extremely shy and fearful, struggling to adjust to her new surroundings. However, thanks to the patience and care of her foster home, she has made remarkable progress.

Now, Delia is much more relaxed and even seeks out affection from those she trusts. She enjoys cuddles and is beginning to show her loving and gentle personality. When out on walks, she is happy to meet new people and other dogs, showing how far she has come in her journey. Her ability to adapt and grow is truly heartwarming.

She gets along very well with other dogs and would benefit from having a calm and confident canine companion in her new home. A steady presence would help her continue to blossom and discover the world at her own pace. Delia is also great with cats, making her a versatile addition to a multi-pet household.

As a sensitive and affectionate soul, Delia deserves a family that will provide her with love, patience, and security. She is currently in Spain but is ready to travel to the UK for adoption. With the right home, she will thrive and form a deep bond with her new family.

If you are interested in giving Delia the loving home she deserves, please reach out to learn more about her and see additional videos.

name: Toby
description:
Toby is a 3-year-old male Cross-Breed who is an extremely friendly and gentle boy.

This gorgeous dog weighs around 40 kg and stands approximately 65 cm tall.

Toby has a loving nature and adores people, making him a wonderful companion.

He is neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped, and also comes with a lifetime RBU (Return to Base) offer, ensuring support throughout his life.

Toby is ready to find a loving home where he can continue to share his affectionate personality and enjoy a fulfilling life.

name: Heidi
description:
Heidi is a 5-year-old female Schipperke Cross. She is a small-sized dog who can be a little worried at first, but once she trusts someone, she becomes incredibly affectionate.

She loves to greet her favourite person with excitement, cuddling into them and rolling over for tummy rubs.

In the home, Heidi is clean and non-destructive. She is comfortable being left alone for a few hours and enjoys her walks and little adventures. She will be a devoted and loyal companion to the right person.

Heidi can be anxious at times and requires an experienced owner who understands her needs. She is protective of her person and may guard them from others, so she will need a one-person household.

A quiet, adult-only home with minimal visitors would be the best environment for her.

While Heidi mixes well with other dogs, she prefers to have her own space and should be the only dog in the home. She cannot live with cats.

name: Jerry
description:
Jerry is a 3.5 year old male large terrier cross, currently in kennels in Humberside.

Jerry is a sensitive and complex soul with a big heart, seeking an experienced owner who can provide the structure and love he deserves.

Sadly, Jerry’s life has not been smooth since arriving in the UK, spending much of his time in kennels.

He loves calm people and enjoys walking, playing, and exploring, though he gets stressed in new situations.

Jerry thrives in a rural environment and is clean in his kennel.

This loyal boy needs a semi-rural or countryside home without children or small animals.

He is unsure of cyclists but loves his food and would benefit from ongoing training and support to help him feel safe and loved.

name: Lucky
description:
Lucky is an 18-month-old female Cross-Breed.

Lucky is a medium-sized, friendly dog who has spent most of her life in a foster shelter in Romania.

She stands about 49 cm tall and is known for her sociable nature.

Lucky is comfortable around other dogs, as she currently shares a kennel with them and could potentially live with another dog in her new home.

She is neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, and has her own pet passport.

Lucky will be delivered directly to her new adopter after completing the necessary admin checks.

We offer lifetime rescue back-up for all our dogs, ensuring ongoing support for both the dog and their new family.

name: Meg
description:
She is one of two siblings who are currently awaiting their forever homes.

Despite her age, Meg is still a young and vibrant dog who has been waiting for a year without any interest from potential adopters.

Meg is known for her friendly and approachable nature.

She has been neutered, ensuring she won’t contribute to overpopulation. Meg is microchipped, which helps in identifying her should she ever get lost.

She is fully vaccinated, providing her with protection against common canine diseases.

Additionally, she has been tested for Brucellosis and other relevant conditions, ensuring her health status is well-documented.

Although Meg has not yet found her forever home, she remains hopeful and ready to bring joy and companionship to a new family.

If you are looking for a loving and well-cared-for dog, Meg might be the perfect addition to your home.

name: Sam
description:
Sam is a 9 to 10 year old male Cross-Breed, looking for his retirement home!

He is a small Cross-Breed dog and a handsome chap.

He is waiting in foster in Kings Lynn, Norfolk and on reservation, he would be brought over directly to his new owner’s home.

Sam is a little shy at first and is a bit wary of men, but with time and love, he would be fine.

He would suit a couple or individual, possibly retired.

He deserves to spend the rest of his life in his forever home with lots of love.

We are told that he is about 9 or 10, but he looks younger.

Please consider this gorgeous boy. We provide lifetime RBU.

name: Angel
description:
Angel is a 3-year-old female Cross-Breed. She exudes a charming and friendly demeanour, often engaging in playful antics that highlight her affectionate nature.

Her gentle personality and warmth make her a lovely companion, whether during playtime or quiet moments at home.

Angel’s playful side is balanced by her calm and loving temperament, making her well-suited for a variety of households.

Having been neutered, fully vaccinated, and microchipped, Angel is in excellent health and ready for her forever home.

Her responsible care has ensured that she’s in great condition, both physically and emotionally. Weighing 26 kg and standing at around 50 cm tall, she is a moderately sized dog, reflecting her mixed-breed heritage.

Her size makes her adaptable to different living environments, whether in a larger house or a cosy home.

Angel’s endearing personality extends to her social interactions with other dogs.

She gets along well with them, showing her ability to fit in with a multi-dog household. Her friendly and approachable nature is sure to make her a delightful addition to any family.

name: Cerys
description:
Cerys is a 5-month-old female cross breed dog who was discovered alongside two other female pups abandoned on the roadside in Romania.

Currently, she is under the care of an English lady living in Romania. She is described as a smallish mixed breed dog and has been socialized with larger resident dogs, exhibiting good compatibility with them.

Cerys has completed her vaccination regimen and has been microchipped, in addition to undergoing all the necessary blood tests to meet DEFRA regulations for dogs originating from other countries.

It’s anticipated that she will grow into a small to medium-sized adult dog, weighing approximately 15 kg to 18 kg.

Cerys is adaptable to various living situations, suitable for a family, a couple, or an individual, and she has a laid-back demeanor for her age.

While she would appreciate having a canine companion, it’s not an essential requirement for her. Although she hasn’t been tested with cats yet, there’s a possibility of conducting such a test before her relocation.

Full rescue support is provided for all dogs, including Cerys, when necessary.

She eagerly awaits the opportunity for a fresh start in the UK and would thrive in a loving home environment. Her sisters Inca and Holly are also seeking new homes.

name: Minnie
description:
Minnie is a 10 month old female Cross-Breed puppy, playful and trusting, yet sadly overlooked. She is small-medium in size, weighing 16 kg and standing at 50-51 cm, perfect for a knee-height companion.

MINNIE was originally found near the road, her mum was hit by the car and didn’t survive. She was a tiny puppy and had no chance to survive if volunteers in Belarus would not rescue her.

She went to a Foster family together with her brother Alex. Alex was happily Adopted in UK. Minnie arrived in UK in June , and still dreams about her forever home.

MINNIE is at Foster now, with other dogs and older kids. And this is what they say:

” What a joy it’s been to train such a smart and eager pup like Minnie! In just 3 weeks at our foster home, she’s made remarkable improvement in impulse control, obedience, and even tried her paw at agility exercises with so much excitement. Can you believe how far she’s come in such a short time?Previously, we mentioned some of her challenges, but let’s see how she’s improved:

“Can be unsure around pushchairs.” Not anymore! Minnie is now completely calm around pushchairs, whether they’re coming toward her, walking beside her, or passing by. She’s unbothered and confident.

“May bark or chew on your shoes sometimes.” While Minnie still loves to carry shoes around the house, we’re working on giving her a more appropriate comfort object. It seems to be a part of her young age, but she’s already shifting her focus to healthier chew options like bones, Kongs, or long-lasting treats like dried ears and tails.

Minnie’s even turned it into a game—she loves tossing treats in the air and chasing them around the house. And the best part? No more barking at home! When she first arrived, she was quite demanding, but now she patiently waits for her meals, even with our two other dogs around.

She’s grown more confident and no longer feels the need to follow us like a shadow. While we haven’t left her alone at home yet, she’s happy to stay in a room by herself as long as the door is open.

“Reactive on walks.” Minnie can be reactive if we’re not fully focused on her, but we lovingly call her our “mindfulness trainer” for this reason. When we stay engaged—by changing pace, asking her to come, throwing treats for her to find—she’s fantastic.

No distractions from birds, squirrels, or even people. It’s only when we get distracted ourselves that some of her reactivity returns, so with the right attention, Minnie is a joy to walk!

“Sometimes unsure around kids or female dogs.” Minnie is improving here, too. She’s now playful with most dogs, regardless of their size or gender.

When it comes to children, she can still be a bit reactive, especially when they approach her too quickly, but with patience and positive reinforcement, she’s getting better.

MINNIE is adorable pup, too young to be perfect in everything. She is can be nervous and shy at start but she is very friendly and playful. She is very loving, very curious and smart.

MINNIE can be unsure of young kids,  but she loves older kids 13+. She will perfectly suit home with the other friendly and confident  large or medium male dog as really enjoy canine company

MINNIE has no known health issues; not spayed (arrived 5 months ago at early age, rescue will contribute to costs). Full vaccination pack, provided worms treatment, microchipped. Brucella C. tested.

name: Poppy
description:
Poppy is a 7-year-old female Cross-Breed. She was abandoned in the woods of Romania alongside another mother and eleven puppies.

Sadly, only six of the puppies survived and have since been adopted, but Poppy has remained in the shelter for two and a half years, patiently waiting for her forever home.

She is a shy but loving girl whose entire demeanour brightens when she receives human attention.

With gentle care, she blossoms into an affectionate and grateful companion. She gets along well with other dogs and cats, making her a great addition to a multi-pet household.

Poppy walks well on the lead, though she will need time to adjust and may benefit from some further training. At around 35 kg and 50 cm tall, she is a medium-sized dog with a gentle presence.

She has been spayed and is fully vaccinated, ensuring she is ready for a fresh start in a loving home.

After waiting so long, Poppy deserves a family that will cherish her. She is looking for a patient and understanding owner who will help her settle into home life.

Could you be the one to offer her the home of her dreams? Full rescue backup (RBU) is provided.

name: Murphy
description:
Meet MURPHY, a gentle, loving, and resilient small boy around 4.5 years old, who resembles a charming mix of Corgi and Chihuahua. He is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven.

Available for a foster-to-adopt. Already in UK: Clapham (London), SW11. Adoption fee reduced.

He lost one eye in a horrific incident in Ukraine, but his spirit remains unbroken. He’s now in the UK and looking for a forever home where he can be cherished. Sadly, the family who took him in feels they are not the right match for him and are unable to meet his needs.

They have provided a thorough evaluation of MURPHY, which you can read below.

Rescue Story:MURPHY’s story is one of love, resilience, and heartbreak. He was abandoned in a communal garden in Ukraine, where he was embraced by the local residents. They cared for him, and he became part of their extended family, playing with children and happily resting in his little kennel.

Tragically, some cruel teenagers thought it would be amusing to chase MURPHY and throw a petard into his kennel. After the explosion, MURPHY was left severely injured, his face burned and bleeding, and his eye tragically lost. However, despite this horror, MURPHY’s spirit remained unbroken.

He was rushed to a clinic, treated, and later brought into a rescue. Through it all, MURPHY continued to trust humans, showing the true resilience of a dog’s heart.

A Word from His Current Family:“ He is a lovely little dog, with a strong and great spirit. Murphy is a rescue from Ukraine who came to us in June 2024. He only has one eye due to an incident where he was attacked by some teenagers who threw a firework / explosive into his little den.

Since then he was taken into care and fostered for.

A highly independent little soul, he loves his alone time and is never anxious in these periods. He loves his sleep and will find sun spots and cozy little nooks to snuggle up in.

Positives? Good to be left alone for short periods, very calm and sleeps a lot? Doesn’t destroy things in house? Independent? Enjoys good play time and belly rubs when he rolls over? Not a fussy eater? Will sit for snacks and treats? Handsome? Very low maintenance, will shed a couple times a year.? Travels well, loves car and train journeys

Needs? Child free house? A quieter house, less footfall to not disturb him? Only dog in house

Things to know? Give him space and wait for him to come to you. He will and he loves chin and ear scratches? Resource guard, work on splitting his meals up and make him back away from food bowl before topping up. He has improved.? Don’t pick him up? Leave alone when in his bed (trained safe space)? Keep on lead when on walks? Takes pain relief pills for previous accident.– has snapped on occasion, when was misunderstood, but not regularly and not his fault. Needs patience and understanding for all he’s been through

Due to his injuries and impaired vision he can be easily startled if approached from his right.

Requiring a very calm and peaceful life. Super low maintenance and highly independent, he is equally happy when alone or in company of owners. Give him space and wait for him to come to you, he loves chin and ear scratches. He’s a great little dog to have around and keep you company.

He will nuzzle up to you for some love and scratches and then spend the rest of night tucked up in his bed. He has adapted well to his new life in the UK and is very healthy.

Fully vaccinated and blood tests all came back healthy. He doesn’t require long walks and can be tired out after half hour to an hour”

MURPHY is fully healthy (but missing one eye), neutered. All core vaccines are complete, microchipped, and C.Brucella tested (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

name: Ava
description:
Ava is a 6-year-old female Cross-Breed who is very friendly and playful.

She has been neutered, microchipped, and vaccinated, making her fully prepared for her new home.

Ava weighs approximately 28 kg and stands around 48 cm tall.

This sweet girl is eager to find a home where she can be loved and cared for.

Ava’s playful nature and friendly disposition make her a delightful companion.

She would thrive in a home where she can receive plenty of attention and affection.

name: Bailey
description:
He is a super boy and a lovely goofball. Bailey is neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped, making him ready for his forever home.

Standing at approximately 60cm tall and weighing around 40 kg, he is a friendly and sizeable companion.

Despite his large stature, Bailey’s gentle nature makes him an ideal addition to any loving household.

He is eager to find a home where he can share his affection and playful energy.

Bailey’s charming personality makes him a delightful companion for anyone seeking a loyal canine friend.

name: Pennie
description:
Pennie is an 13 months old, female, cross-breed pup who, along with her siblings, faced abandonment in woodland in Romania at a very young age.

Fortunately, they found refuge in a foster shelter where they have been nurtured ever since.

This sweet and slightly shy pup exhibits a calm demeanor, making her an ideal companion for those with experience in dog ownership.

As a good-sized medium dog, Pennie will undergo neutering before embarking on her journey to a new home in the UK.

Her health is meticulously documented in her pet passport, with full vaccination and microchipping completed.

Comprehensive blood tests have been conducted to ensure a smooth integration into her new life.

Pennie, being fully cat-tested with a video available for potential adopters, proves her compatibility with feline friends.

Ideally suited for a family with older children due to her size, Pennie would thrive in an environment where her adopters possess previous dog ownership experience.

To facilitate a seamless transition, we offer full rescue backup and a commitment to ongoing support, ensuring the continued well-being of our canine charges.

Pennie eagerly awaits a loving home, ready to bring joy and companionship to a family in the UK.

name: Holly
description:
Holly, 1 year old female Cross-Breed, and her two sisters were found dumped by waste bins in an alley in Romania at six weeks old.

They have been in a foster shelter since then, and their English foster mum has brought them on well.

They are in a pen with some other pups and a surrogate mum and dad dog, which teaches them doggy manners!

Holly is neutered and fully vaccinated. She is also microchipped.

She would be delivered directly to her new owners once admin checks have been done.

It would be wonderful if she could have a doggy friend to live with, but this is not essential.

Two of her kennel mates have already travelled to their new homes in the UK, and it would be lovely if Holly could too.

Full rescue backup is given on all of our dogs.

name: Freya
description:
Freya, a 5 year old female Labrador Cross, has been patiently waiting in the foster shelter for quite a while after being rescued from a kill shelter in Romania.

We can’t understand why someone hasn’t fallen for her before.

Freya loves attention from her humans and lives with other dogs.

She has been neutered and fully vaccinated as well as microchipped.

She would be delivered directly to her new adopter once admin checks have been carried out.

Please consider this lovely girl for a place on the Happy Bus to a new life here in the UK.

name: Iris
description:
Iris is a 2-3 year old female Lurcher. She is great with people. Iris will need a pet and child-free home.

We are looking for either a foster or a forever home. She’s a fun-loving dog. Who just wants to be loved? If you think you can offer her lots of love and a sofa to sleep on.

name: Pearl
description:
Pearl is an 18-month-old female Cross-Breed who was originally found in a forest with her siblings and brought into foster care. She was only 5 months old when she first entered rescue, and since then, she has spent the majority of her young life in foster care.

Despite her early start in rescue, Pearl is a friendly and sociable young dog who is now eagerly searching for her forever home.

Pearl is expected to grow into a medium-sized adult dog. She has already been fully vaccinated, microchipped, and has had all the necessary blood tests required to come to the UK. This means that she is in good health and ready to move to her new home once the right family is found.

Being a young dog, Pearl is very adaptable and social, and she enjoys being around people. She thrives on human interaction and would make an affectionate companion.

As Pearl has spent most of her life in care, she is used to the attention and care provided by foster families, which will make her transition into a permanent home easier.

In addition to her physical health, Pearl comes with full RBU (Return to Base) support. This means that her new family will have ongoing assistance throughout her life to ensure that any questions or concerns are addressed.

This safety net is a great reassurance for potential adopters, knowing that they will not be alone in the process of welcoming Pearl into their lives.

Pearl is ready to find a home where she can continue to grow and thrive. Her sociable nature and friendly disposition make her an ideal companion for those seeking a loving and active dog.

Whether as part of a family or as an individual pet, Pearl is sure to bring joy and affection into her new home.

name: Aran
description:
Aran is an 18-month-old male Cross-Breed.

He has spent his entire life in a foster shelter, patiently awaiting his forever home. As one of several siblings in need of adoption, Aran has developed a friendly and sociable nature, making him a wonderful companion.

He is cat-tested and has demonstrated a good ability to coexist with feline friends, which is a positive trait for potential adopters with cats.

Additionally, Aran is accustomed to living with other dogs, showing that he can thrive in a multi-dog household.

Expected to be a small-sized adult dog, he would be well-suited to various living environments, including smaller homes or apartments.

Aran is fully vaccinated, microchipped, and has undergone all the necessary tests for travel, ensuring that he is well-prepared for his new home.

His affectionate disposition and readiness for adoption make him an excellent choice for anyone looking to add a loving and well-adjusted dog to their family.

name: Millie
description:
Millie is a beautiful temperament, always happy, loving cross-breed girl of around 2 years old.

She is super friendly with everyone – kids, dogs, cats. Great on the lead. Housetrained. Based in Peterborough, available for foster-to-adopt. Reduced adoption fees

Unfortunately, a few days ago, Millie had to go to boarding kennels as all our current fosters are fully booked. While this is likely one of the best kennels you can find, staffed by true dog lovers with great facilities, an on-site behaviorist, and a focus on rehabilitation, it’s still not the same as a home.

They offer wonderful care, take the dogs on walks, and play with them, but it can’t replace the love and comfort of a real family. We’re praying that this sweet girl finds her forever home soon.

Before this Millie was at foster in UK and this is what they say:

“Millie is a very sweet, attractive and affectionate young dog. She likes people and to be with people and is normally docile and friendly. She likes to be stroked and groomed and to have her belly rubbed.

She likes exploring but doesn’t try and escape from the garden or run off when out for a walk. She likes to play with toys, especially in the evening out in the garden. She will readily sit on command and shake a paw!

She is very good off the lead, walking along paths, in fields and in the woods etc in the countryside, and she will regularly look back and check that you are there and come back when called.

She is very friendly with people she meets and will regularly sniff them (to check they are human) as you walk along, though she is slightly nervous of other larger dogs until she gets to know them. She will happily chase and play with other dogs she feels comfortable with. If they are too much she will do a little growl and they will usually back off.

However, we have come across a few behavioural issues. The main issue appears ‘resource guarding’ and the things she guards have increased and changed whilst she has been with us. This can be unpredictable and takes us by surprise at times. For instance we might be happily working in the same room as Millie who’s in her bed, coming and going and talking to her.

Suddenly she will change and growl, snarl if we re-enter the room. She also will suddenly and unpredictably snarl in other places where she’s lying down. Another example is that we are both hesitant of trying to move her off the sofa.

The only safe way is to call her from another room, sometimes with a treat to lure her. This may be because for some reason Millie has not really settled with us after nearly four weeks and still feels insecure.

I think Millie will need to be with family who are experienced with dogs, who can interpret her body language and behaviour, and be able train with her to reduce and prevent her very marked resource guarding (rescue will be happy to provide useful and working materials to treat it). I think this shouldn’t be a family with young children but teenagers and older children should be okay if they are aware of what not to do.”

MILLIE is active but not hyper, always happy, not pushy. Very loving and loves cuddles and fuss. Loves people company and being nearby.

MILLIE is very smart, loves learning new things. But the most she likes is walks being active and having attention from people.MILLIE is good in the car and loves it.

MILLIE has no known health issues. Spayed, vaccinated, microchipped. Brucella C. tested.

name: Bowie
description:
Bowie is a 5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is an affectionate big dog full of love and is craving human care.

This sweet boy has been waiting for a while to find his forever home. Bowie is neutered, fully vaccinated, and microchipped, making him a well-prepared companion for a new family.

He weighs between 32 kg and 35 kg and stands about 52 cm tall, making him a large dog with a gentle personality.

Bowie currently resides in a run with another dog but could also thrive as an only dog in the right home.

His loving nature makes him well-suited to live with a couple, an individual, or potentially a family with older children. He seeks companionship and affection and would benefit from being in a home where he can receive the care and attention he craves.

Bowie has waited for a long time to find his special person, and he would love nothing more than to settle into a home where he can be loved for life.

The rescue offers lifetime support to ensure Bowie transitions smoothly into his new home. His calm, affectionate nature makes him a great fit for someone looking for a loyal and loving companion.

He is ready to bring joy to a family or individual who can provide the space, care, and affection he needs.

name: Stevie
description:
Stevie is a 1 year old male Cross-Breed. This young fellow was abandoned with others and has been taken into foster with an English lady in Romania.

He is living with other pups and a surrogate mum and dad dog, so he is getting lots of doggy socialising.

Stevie has never lived in a house, but most of our dogs adapt quite quickly.

It is very hot over there at the moment, so the dogs tend to stay in their shelters, but we managed to get a few photos of this good-looking chap.

He will be a medium-sized adult and would love a doggy friend to teach him the ropes.

He will be fully vaccinated, wormed, and given flea treatment before he travels.

All our dogs have pet passports which contain all of their medical interventions.

Hopefully, we will be able to neuter him before he travels. He will travel by van directly to see his new adopter in the UK.

name: Albi
description:
ALBI – A War Hero Who Found His Smile Again: A New Dog in a New Life. ALBI is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Adoption fee significantly reduced

Meet ALBI, a 9 -year-old small-sized corgi type. ALBI once walked the front lines of war, shoulder-to-shoulder with Ukrainian soldiers. But in the UK, we misunderstood him terribly.

We thought he needed peace and quiet. We placed him with elderly people, in silent homes with no other pets. But he was miserable. He was misunderstood, unhappy, and reactive—trying to tell us something we failed to hear.

Then something beautiful happened. When ALBI was just days away from being sent to kennels, a wonderful foster stepped in—and everything changed.

Now living in an active household with children and dogs, ALBI is a completely different dog. His foster says:

“He’s the most perfect dog I’ve ever met. Kind, loving, grateful. He adores being part of the action—bonfires, walks, games, relaxing by your side—he just wants to be included.”

“He loves kids—especially calm, dog-savvy ones—and he adores other dogs. Even shy or reactive dogs feel safe with him because he reads them so well and gives them space. He’s playful, gentle, and so grateful for every moment. Even visitors don’t upset him anymore—he’s just relaxed and joyful.”

ALBI has finally shown us who he really is. This is his fresh start. And now he needs the right home to match.

Rescue StoryALBI is a war survivor. He lived with soldiers in trenches under shelling—eating scraps, keeping watch, offering comfort. They described him as the “most loyal companion” they’d known. After the war, he was rescued and brought to the UK. But sadly, he ended up passed from one wrong home to another—quiet places that didn’t match his spirit.

In one of those homes in England, ALBI was terribly mistreated. He was misunderstood and punished—possibly even physically. His stress and anxiety spiralled, and shockingly, he was booked for euthanasia by someone who claimed “he doesn’t deserve to live around people.”

Thankfully, we found out in time and took him back. When he returned to his previous foster, she was heartbroken to see how much he’d changed—nervous, reactive, broken in spirit. But even after all of that, ALBI’s heart was still open.

But ALBI never gave up. And today, in a home full of life and love, is ALBI finally at peace.

Detailed InformationALBI is full of heart. He loves other dogs and needs to live with them—they help him feel joyful. He’s clever, wise, and respectful, especially around timid or fearful pups. He also absolutely adores children—but only gentle, calm ones who understand dogs.

He loves his walks, his garden time, and just being part of the family routine. His former reactivity? Gone. His fear of visitors? Gone. Even around men, he now behaves beautifully, simply because he’s happy and no longer stressed or bored.

ALBI sleeps soundly, enjoys soft beds, and lives for companionship. He’s not a loner—he wants to be where his people and his pack are. He doesn’t need a mansion, just a home full of love and movement, and people who will include him in their world.

Ideal HomeALBI is seeking an active, loving home with at least one other friendly dog (the more the merrier). A secure garden is a must. The older children who are kind and respectful will be welcomed by him with open paws.

He’d suit a home where someone is around most of the time—he loves his humans deeply. A calm but lively household where he can be included in walks, playtime, and snuggles is exactly what he’s been waiting for.

ALBI is a new dog in a new life. After everything he’s been through—from war trenches to emotional neglect—he’s finally happy. And we owe it to him to keep it that way.ALBI has come through war and heartbreak, and still, he chooses to love. He was let down—more than once—and yet here he is, smiling again. He just needs a family to keep that smile on his face.

If you’ve got a home with wagging tails, gentle hands, a few muddy walks and space on your sofa for a small, loyal war hero… ALBI is ready to give you his whole heart.

Health InformationALBI is in good health. Neutered. Fully vaccinated. Microchipped. Needs mild weight loss and joint supplements. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before the trip (owners receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Rupert
description:
Rupert is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed who is a loving young boy and would love a home of his own. He is such a playful chap.

He is the last of his litter to find a home sadly.

Rupert has been cat tested which is great and he is fine with other dogs.

A suitable home would be one with no small children as he is not used to them but with a family, couple or individual who can give the attention he craves.

He is neutered, microchipped and has been fully vaccinated.

He has also had all the required blood tests to comply with DEFRA.

He would be transported to his new home via an accredited transport van.

Please consider him. He is so wanting a home of his own and an owner to play with!

name: Tim
description:
Tim – A Gentle and Quiet Soul. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Arriving in UK on 13th June.

Meet TIM, about 2 years old, very friendly but little shy medium size boy. Despite his challenging start, TIM has grown into a calm and affectionate companion who is ready to share his quiet love with the right family.

Rescue Story:TIM’s life began on the outskirts of an industrial warehouse area, where he and his siblings struggled to survive as stray pups. Luckily, he was rescued as a puppy, but his time living in survival mode left him cautious and reserved.

Over time, TIM has learned to trust people and embrace the kindness of those around him, but he still faces the world with a touch of hesitation, needing patience and understanding to truly bloom.

Detailed Information:TIM is a calm and quiet dog who thrives in a peaceful environment. While he may be shy at first, once he feels safe, his loyalty and affection shine. He loves his walks, enjoys car rides, and is well-mannered on the lead.

Tim has a calm and gentle nature, making him a wonderful companion for a serene household.

He does best when paired with another dog, as their presence helps him feel more secure. He’s good with other dogs but needs a little time to adjust to new canine friends. With cats, TIM is largely indifferent indoors but might give chase outdoors if tempted.

While not aggressive, TIM is sensitive to loud noises and changes, so a quiet home without small children is ideal. He is house-trained for three walks a day and has never been left alone without the company of another dog, making him best suited for a family with an existing furry companion.

Ideal Family:TIM’s perfect home is one that values patience, understanding, and a calm lifestyle. He’d thrive in a household with another friendly dog to guide and comfort him. A family that enjoys walks, quiet companionship, and providing gentle encouragement will be the ideal match for Tim.

Health Information:TIM is fully healthy. Neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, and treated for parasites. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Zulu
description:
Zulu is a 4-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a friendly and sociable dog who enjoys the company of people and other dogs.

His affectionate nature makes him a wonderful companion, and he thrives in a home where he can interact and bond with both humans and canines alike.

Although Zulu is good with other dogs, he is a bit timid around cats. While he does not show aggression, he may need careful introductions and a patient approach when living with feline companions.

His social nature means he enjoys spending time with others, making him a great addition to a multi-dog household.

Zulu is also well-suited to living with children, provided they are aged 10 years or older. His temperament suggests he would do well in a family environment where children understand how to respect a dog’s space and needs.

He would appreciate a loving home that offers both companionship and structure.

Currently, Zulu is in foster kennels in Romania, waiting for his forever home. His background in foster care suggests he has had some experience with a home-like setting, though he may still need time to adjust once adopted.

With the right family, he will surely flourish and become a loyal and loving companion.

name: Oreo
description:
Oreo is an 11-month-old male Cross-Breed. He is currently living in Norfolk, UK, after being rescued from a difficult start in life where he was kept on a chain.

Now in foster care, Oreo is learning what it means to be safe, free, and loved. Despite his rough beginnings, he has a playful and affectionate nature that shines through once he feels secure around new people.

Oreo has a soft and gentle side, which makes his name quite fitting. He adores his toys, with footballs being his absolute favourite, and he shows real joy in play sessions.

He’s also very food-motivated and quick to learn, which makes training both effective and enjoyable. Walking on a lead comes naturally to him, and he does so beautifully.

Oreo thrives around other dogs and would benefit from a home where he has canine company. He would love a patient and loving household with access to a garden where he can enjoy his playtime.

He is suited to families with children aged 12 and above, making him a good fit for a more mature family environment.

Oreo has been neutered, fully vaccinated, and blood tested, so he is ready for his forever home. His rescue, Pennypaws Rescue, provides full backup and support, and a home check will be part of the adoption process.

This sweet boy is searching for the right people to give him the love and stability he deserves.

name: Buddy Boy
description:
Welcome the handsome gentleman, Buddy Boy.

Buddy Boy – 4 year old male Alaskan Malamute, is around 18 kilograms in weight and full of charm.

His story is a sad one. As the result of a family breakup in Spain, Buddy Boy has found himself behind bars. A young woman cared for him for as long as she could and still visits him regularly to walk him, which shows the depth of feeling he inspires.

Now, he needs the stability of a permanent, loving home.

Importantly, Buddy Boy is used to living in a home and understands family life. With his gentle, loyal nature and playful spirit, he will make a wonderful companion for the right adopter.

A home check and call are then arranged. When this has been completed successfully, the balance of costs is due. Travel preparations are then finalised, and Buddy Boy will make his journey to the United Kingdom where he can finally begin his new chapter.

Buddy Boy deserves the chance to leave his kennel behind and return to a home where he will be loved and secure.

If you are interested in adopting, please send some basic information about your circumstances.

We ask that you include any experience you may have with the breed, the type of home you can offer, how many people are in the household and the ages of any children, details of other pets, and whether your garden is secure.

This helps us to match each dog with the right family and ensures the best possible outcome for both the dog and the adopter.

name: Kim
description:
Kim is a 5-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is a medium-sized dog who has been neutered and was rescued from a kill shelter over a year ago, alongside another dog named Cassie.

Kim is generally good with other dogs, although she can be a little nervous when meeting new people.

Her time in the kill shelter was clearly traumatic, and as a result, she needs time and patience to rebuild her trust in humans.

She hasn’t been tested with cats, so it’s uncertain how she would respond to them. Given her timid nature, she would be best suited to a quiet household without small children.

Kim has been neutered, fully vaccinated, and has had all the necessary blood tests completed.

She also has her own pet passport, which allows for safe and approved travel. She will be delivered directly to her adoptive home by a professional and authorised transport team.

Full rescue back-up (RBU) is provided to ensure her ongoing welfare. Kim is looking for a loving home that understands her need for calm and patience.

name: Zorro
description:
Zorro is a 7 year old male Shar-Pei cross Labrador Retriever.

He originally lacked confidence and he hadn’t walked much but his true character is showing now he has come out of his shell.

He has lived with cats, chickens, and guinea pigs and doesn’t seem to have any prey drive at all. He is reactive to other dogs, especially small energetic ones, so would need to be the only dog in the household.

Zorro is fit and healthy but his eyesight is not as good as what it should be in low-light situations. He loves a good cuddle with his human friends and is a pleasantly affectionate boy.

He really loves his long walks and would be best suited in an active home. Zorro could be rehomed in an adult only home.

He loves his food and treats which will make any further training that much easier and more fun.

name: Lillian
description:
Lillian is a 4 year old female small/medium cross breed.

Lillian is one of three dogs that we are trying to save from a shelter which is soon closing in Romania.

She is about four years old and is neutered.

She loves other dogs. She is curious about life but is a little shy with humans.

She will need an adopter who will be patient with her while she learns to trust.

She will need a quietish household. She could live with a family with dog savvy older children, a couple or an individual who would love a four-legged friend.

She is fully vaccinated and microchipped.

Unfortunately, we haven’t been able to catch test her.

Lillian has had the blood tests needed to travel to the UK and comply with DEFRA.

We give lifetime rescue back up for all our dogs.

name: Luna
description:
Hey there. My name is Luna I am about 5 years old with the most beautiful colors and smile

I may be a big girl, but don’t let my size fool you—I’ve got a nose for adventure! I’m equipped with a super strong sniffer that can detect treats from a mile away. My love for food will make training with me super fun and easy.

Life didn’t start out on the right paw for me. I was found with a broken back leg, but thanks to some incredible humans I have received the best vet care and I’ve made a full recovery.

You wouldn’t even know I had a surgery because I’m as good as new! I’ve proven that nothing can keep me down—I’m a superstar, through and through.

Sure, I may be a bit strong on the lead, but hey, nobody’s perfect! The good news is that I’m a foodie at heart, and that makes training a breeze. Just wave a tasty treat in front of my nose, and I’ll be your eager student, ready to learn new tricks and impress you with my smarts. I also love water.

I also need slow introductions when meeting new dogs for the first time, I need someone who will help me to learn that new dogs can be lovely and I’ve got nothing to fear.

Once I know them, I’m their best friend. I am at the shelter for over 2,5 years now and I have shared with many many dogs, males and females and I love my doggie friends. I’m sorry I’m just not very good at new introductions.

So, dear humans, if you’re searching for a big-hearted, playful companion who will fill your life with joy and cuddles, look no further.

I’m here, waiting for my forever home, where we can create memories that will make our tails wag forever. Adopt Luna, the joyous ball of furry sunshine!

name: Blue
description:
Blue is a 3 year old female Husky Cross. She was originally rescued from Cyprus and arrived in the UK in October 2020.

Since then she has been given so much love and been well cared for, but sadly her family feel that they’re just unable to give her the lifestyle and environment that she truly needs to thrive.

Blue is thought to be a combination of Labrador, Shepherd and Husky and is a genuinely beautiful dog. Ultimately, Blue needs a rural home outside of the city.

Right now she is living in London and we feel this is where the vast majority of her behavioural concerns have stemmed from because the environment is simply too much for her to cope with.

First and foremost let’s start with the positives. Blue is a wonderful companion and a very devoted dog with those she knows and trusts.

Blue has so much personality and is a highly intelligent dog who picks up new tricks and games very quickly.

Blue thrives on mental enrichment and appreciates her ‘rest days’, playing more indoor brain games than physical, which gives her a chance to reset from the triggers that make her anxious outside.

Blue loves playing tug, and ‘find it’ in the house with toys and treats – her sense of smell is amazing! She also loves her sleep and when relaxed she can snooze for hours. Blue is an active dog and benefits from a good, long walk.
