Blue is much happier in big open spaces with lots of places to sniff – this is also a really good activity for decompressing.

In a more rural environment where she has these opportunities on her doorstep, rather than walking through busy London to get to more quiet places, we think she would be so much happier. Unfortunately, Blue is reactive to other dogs and gets overwhelmed even at long distances.

Blue does have a select few doggy friends that she enjoys going for sniffy walks with, but it’s taken time for her to reach this point. With gentle, patient introductions she can make friends very gradually, but this still requires management.

Blue is also not confident around strangers, especially when they enter her home. With those she does know and trust though, she is nothing but love, and gets super wiggly around them!

We feel that a lot of Blue’s triggers are exacerbated by her environment, and in a location where her cortisol levels can decrease and she can enjoy a much calmer, quieter lease of life, we would expect to see some of these issues lessen.

Regardless, Blue needs a patient, understanding and experienced adopter to help her make progress. They also need a secure, private garden. Blue is looking for a pet-free home without any other dogs and no cats.

Blue has a high prey drive and will chase given the opportunity. Although she’s never responded negatively to a child based on Blue’s anxiety at the moment we’re looking for a home without any kids.

We just want a laidback home setting for her, where she can gradually adjust, decompress, and hopefully feel much more content. Blue’s journey will take some hard work but seeing her progress will be extremely rewarding.

Blue is currently based in Walthamstow, London, and has a clean bill of health minus some mild allergies. She is ready to find her new forever home.

name: Missy
description:
Missy is a 9 year old female Akita. She came to us because she was a sad and underweight girl.

Missy was lucky and found herself a fabulous foster home to wait in until she finds her new forever family and she has blossomed, she is now a healthy weight which her carers are maintaining.

Missy has a fabulous personality, she loves her food and will become vocal if her after-breakfast treat of a toothbrush chew doesn’t arrive on time or is forgotten!

Missy loves her toys and has her toy box, she meets her foster family with her favourite in her mouth when they return home, and then it is time to play.

Missy is very bright and knows what is hers, even if this is a newly purchased toy, taking it from your hand or bag, she enjoys finding treats in her puzzle balls and snuffle mat.

Missy has not been destructive when left on her own and will only chew on her toys and chew treats. She is a very clean girl and there have been no accidents in the house.

Missy knows how to let you know that she wants something. She is a very loving girl who is happy to curl up in the evening and watch TV.

Missy knows it is bedtime and will take herself off to bed with a toy she has carefully chosen. Missy is very active and will need a few decent walks each day.

Her foster carers are working on her reaction to other dogs which can vary between nervous and reactive.

Missy is looking for a home where there are no other dogs and she cannot be rehomed with cats. She travels very well in the car and does enjoy adventure.

Missy has proven to be very much a man’s dog, she loves them both but much prefers the company of her foster Dad to her foster Mum.

Missy can live with children over the age of 12 years of age. If you have a lot of love to give and would like to offer Missy her forever home we would love to hear from you so please get in touch. She is currently fostered in Northumberland.

name: Senna
description:
Senna is a 2-year-old male Griffon in search of his forever home. This handsome boy is gentle and sweet-natured but can be shy when meeting new people. Initially, he tends to freeze and stay still, but once he builds trust, he reveals his affectionate and loving side.

Senna is very good with other dogs and will need a home with at least one balanced canine companion to help him feel secure. He thrives in the company of other dogs and benefits from their guidance and reassurance.

On the lead, Senna does quite well, but he is easily startled by loud noises and sudden movements. His adopter will need to be extra cautious to prevent any risk of him escaping. A patient and understanding home will be essential to help him gain confidence.

While Senna is scared of cats, this may be due to a lack of familiarity rather than aggression. He is quite good when travelling in a car, making trips and outings more manageable for his future family.

Currently in Italy, Senna is available for adoption in the UK, with full rescue backup provided. He will need a loving, patient home where he can continue to grow in confidence and feel safe.

name: Mike
description:
Mike, a charming 1 year old male cross breed medium-sized dog, is now living in Blackpool, in the UK.

With his vaccinations up to date and his flea and worm treatments complete, Mike is ready to embark on the next chapter of his life with a loving family.

Although still too young to be neutered, Mike’s bright personality shines through, making him an irresistible addition to any home.

As a puppy, Mike thrives in the company of others, whether it be canine companions, feline friends, or children aged 5 and above.

His adaptable nature and playful spirit make him a joy to be around, bringing laughter and love wherever he goes. Despite his recent arrival in the UK, Mike is already making strides in his training, showing promise in both toilet and lead manners.

However, as with any puppy, ongoing training and guidance will be essential to help him reach his full potential.

With his friendly disposition and affectionate nature, Mike has quickly captured the hearts of those around him. He is fully vaccinated and has shown compatibility with other dogs, making him an ideal companion for families seeking a furry friend to join their adventures.

Whether it’s playing in the yard, going for walks, or simply snuggling up for some cuddles, Mike promises to bring endless joy and happiness to his forever home.

name: Tim
description:
Tim is a 1 year old male Griffon. He’s been fostered for more than a year and he is now ready to be adopted. Tim arrived petrified and scared of everything.

Tim is a very young dog and we do not know if he was mistreated or maybe not socialized, so Tim needs a super special and generous family.

Tim has been working with a behaviourist to allow humans to touch him. He has improved a tons but he still runs away if he doesn’t know someone. We think that living in a home will help him progress faster.

Tim has never walked on the lead so he will need a bit of work on that department too. Tim is the most gentle, noble and submissive soul one can meet.

Tim is scared and insecure but he has never had a bad word or shown any aggression towards any being.

Tim loves other dogs, he loves playing, running, and sleeping with them, and he’s super dog-friendly. So a home with at least another young, balanced, friendly, playful doggie is a must.

We believe kids are not a good idea right now as he’s too scared to tolerate the stress of living with little children.

With patience, time, love and routines, Tim will show his loving character and he will be an amazing addition to the family.

Please if you are an experienced person, and you want to help this little chap, contact me. He’s in Spain & we arrange everything for him to travel to the UK once an adoption appears.

We are looking for a secure garden with fencing or walls to a minimum of 5ft. We also need the dogs to be kept on a lead, long lunge lead or for people to use enclosed fields for off-lead exercise as these dogs are scent hounds & have hunting backgrounds. We do not rehome with children under 8 years old. He is full rescue backup is provided.

name: Godello
description:
Godello is a 1 year old male Griffon Cross. He needs a home and he is good with other doggies although he needs to be fed separately as he’s food possessive towards other doggies.

Godello is sociable with people he trusts, he’s a bit scared of strangers.

Godello is in Spain and we arranged everything for him to travel to the UK once an adoption appears. We are looking for a secure garden with fencing or walls to a minimum of 5ft.

We also need the dogs to be kept on a lead, long lunge lead or for people to use enclosed fields for off-lead exercise as these dogs are scent hounds & have hunting backgrounds. We do not rehome with children under 8 years old. He is full rescue backup is provided.

name: Amlet
description:
Meet Amlet – A Gentle Soul Ready for His Second Chance

Hello, friends! My name is Amlet, and I’m a sweet-natured, friendly black Labrador cross, around 7 years young. For the past 2 years, I’ve been living at CyDRA shelter, patiently waiting for a forever home. Could it finally be with you?

I might not love labels, but I do embrace one classic Labrador trait with pride: I absolutely love food! Yes—I’m a proud foodie, and after what I’ve been through, I think I’ve earned it.

You see, I spent my entire life chained up, barely surviving on scraps of food and little water. Then one day, everything changed. A kind stranger saw me and contacted the vet services, who quickly called in a rescue team.

That’s how I finally got a chance at a better life—and moved into the shelter, where I learned what it means to be treated with love and respect.

Because of my difficult past, I can be a little unsure around other dogs at first. But with slow introductions, I warm up—and once I trust, I love deeply. I’ve shared my kennel happily with several female dog friends, and I do best in calm, respectful company.

There’s still so much of life I haven’t experienced—walks, treats, exploring, cuddles on the couch—but I’m ready to start now. I’m looking for a quiet, loving home where I can feel safe, relax, and show off my affectionate personality (and yes, my adorable fluffy tail).

I’d do best in a peaceful home, either as an only dog or with a calm female companion. Most of all, I just want someone to give me a chance—to help me write a new chapter filled with love, comfort, and joy.

I’m ready to pack my bags. Will you be the one to open your heart and welcome me home?

name: Monty
description:
Monty is a 3 year old male Cross-Breed living in Scarborough, UK.

Let me introduce Monty and tell you a little about him…

This boy was born in a shelter in Romania; his mum was rescued and gave birth while in rescue, so lucky for this boy he didn’t have to face the streets.

His mum is a beautiful German Shepherd type girl and she is here within the UK, also adopted. This boy has not been so lucky.

He arrived in a home here in the UK as a small cute boy, and it seemed like his forever home. It wasn’t meant to be; it lasted a while, and he started to grow up and it just didn’t work anymore.

We had to act quickly, and he ended up in a shelter in Blackpool. This boy just needed someone to see past his size and the fact he hadn’t really been fully socialised. He spent a few months in shelter and even met his brother there.

Eventually, he ended up getting a foster placement with an amazing lady with bags of experience. He has settled as part of her pack, even down to living with a little doggie with disabilities. It hasn’t always been perfect.

He is very food-led and likes to bench surf; this is something that will need lots more work. He has had an argument or two with the other doggies, but let’s be honest, while dogs are finding a pecking order, this can happen.

He loves his walks, as you can see from the pics, and has lots of doggie friends on those walks. His foster truly has done all with him that he should have had when he was younger.

Now let’s find this boy a happy ever after like he deserves and help free his foster to help another.

Given Monty’s size and energy, he needs a home without young children and with experienced owners.

Monty loves routine and would make a great addition to a home that can provide him with the structure he loves.

name: Arthur
description:
This lovely lad is Arthur, an 8 year old male Akita. He came to us from the stray dog pound, where he was all alone and awaiting rescue.

Arthur is very lucky to have found himself a foster home to wait in comfortably until he finds his new family.

He has proved to be a fabulous and well-behaved boy in the home, housetrained and non-destructive, and he adores being around people.

He loves being out and about on an adventure, although he does initially pull a little on the lead. His foster carer is currently working on improving his lead training.

As Arthur came to us with no history, we are looking for an adult-only home or one with older, large-breed-aware children over the age of 12 years.

Arthur cannot be rehomed with cats, and although he walks fine with other dogs, we feel he would thrive as the only dog in his home where he can receive all the love and attention for himself.

If you think you can offer our handsome and loveable Arthur his forever home, we would love to hear from you.

name: Nori
description:
Nori is a 10 month old female Saluki crossx who was born in Oman in November 2023. She’s quite small and weighs 14.5 kg. She’s currently in a foster home in Oman.

Nori was found when she was about 6 months old in a dangerous area in Muscat. Sadly, her siblings had been killed but Nori managed to get away. However, she was then hit by a car and suffered internal bleeding.

Consequently, she struggled to find food and was very malnourished and fearful of people when rescued.

She has been in a foster home since her rescue and has improved drastically. She has put on weight and now looks healthy. She knows a few commands such as paw, sit, come and is a very fast learner!

She loves being outdoors and is energetic when she wants to be. She is definitely slower to trust men over women, so will need very patient owners who will give her the time she needs to trust you and know that you aren’t a threat.

Nori gets along with cats, as there are cats currently in her foster home. She also enjoys the company of other dogs. Her foster mum says that Nori is “very playful, loves naps, and loves cuddling close to a person when sleeping.

She still shows signs of triggers from previous abuse but is open to trust if we’re patient.”

Nori is fully vaccinated, microchipped, and spayed. She will be ready to travel to the UK in January 2024.

name: Elvis
description:
He is 4 years old and a larger medium boy Cross-Breed currently in Blackpool (UK).

Elvis came to the UK as a young pup with his siblings after being saved in Romania and abandoned by his brothers and sisters.

He is a beautiful bouncy boy but he likes his time running and playing then likes nothing more than curling up and relaxing. Elvis likes routine and as he is nervous a couple of short quiet walks and the rest of the time just in the garden.

Elvis has had such a difficult time and never had a committed home.

At his first home, he was not properly cared for and when they took him to kennels his nails were overgrown to the point of causing pain and he had sores on his body and was terrified of everyone and everything.

Since then he has never found a home that has given him the time to settle and adjust to life in a loving home. He can’t be rushed and just needs time and lots of cuddles.

He is now back in an amazing rehab kennel in Blackpool where he has come on leaps and bounds and loves to play and bounce around with the staff who all love him dearly.

Elvis is a little too bouncy to live with children as he is described as Bambi on ice as he isn’t the most coordinated dog

He is good with dogs but we are looking for pet-free as he is so desperate to be loved that he struggles a bit to share his people

name: Beanie
description:
Beanie is a 4-year-old female cross-breed.

Beanie endured hardship in Macedonia, where she was mistreated due to her origins.

Rescued and brought to Blackpool, UK, she experienced love from a caring woman but faced abandonment again when her owner needed surgery.

Now, Beanie seeks a child-free, female-only home, as she doesn’t get along with other dogs or cats. Despite her past, she’s spayed, vaccinated, and dual-chipped.

Trust takes time for Beanie due to her difficult past, but she’s ready to find a loving forever home.

name: Raina
description:
Raina – 8 month old female Cross-Breed is a large-sized puppy who will grow into a large adult dog. She was abandoned alongside her sister Mischa at a kennels in November 2024 when they were young pups.

Raina and Mischa are only just beginning to explore their independence. For weeks, they stuck close together, but now they’re starting to show their own personalities.

Raina, the more confident of the two, is soft, squishy, and sweet-natured. While she may be a little shy initially, she warms up with time, trust, and reassurance, showing potential to become a wonderful companion.

Raina is playful and enjoys running in the paddock with other dogs, often cheekily stealing toys from her sister. She’s food-oriented, making her a good candidate for basic training using treats as motivation. Her experience on the lead is limited, so her new family will need to help her with training and routine.

Raina is looking for a semi-rural home with a calm atmosphere, a garden, and an active yet balanced lifestyle. Although not essential, she would likely adjust more quickly with a resident dog.

Raina is currently based in Cyprus and has a clean bill of health. She is ready to travel once she finds her forever home.

name: Tigi
description:
She has spent some time in a home environment, where it was noted that she resource guards items.

We are looking for an understanding home that can manage her resource guarding behaviour and has a good knowledge of the Akita breed.

Ideally, someone with an outside kennel setup for giving her some time out when needed.

Tigi is very loved at the kennels, but it’s not the same as having a home and family of her own.

She loves her walks and playtime, but she knows her own mind, and things are very much on her terms.

However, once you build a bond with her, it is incredibly rewarding.

name: Mischa
description:
Mischa is a shy and reserved girl who, along with her sister Raina, was thrown over the wall of a kennels in November 2024 when they were only young pups. At around eight months old now, Mischa will be a large-sized adult dog, but she is a complete softie.

Mischa and Raina were abandoned in the right place with the right people. For the first few weeks, they were glued to each other, but as they’ve become more settled, they are becoming braver and coming into their own personalities.

Mischa tends to hang back while Raina takes the lead, but she’s improving each day. Routine and consistency will be key in helping her feel settled in a new home. She’s gentle, sweet, and soft, just needing reassurance and confidence building to blossom into a confident dog.

When it comes to other dogs, Mischa is very playful and enjoys interacting with her sister and other kennel dogs. She loves playing in the paddock and has bursts of speed, often being chased by Raina.

Mischa would be best suited to a semi-rural home with a calm household atmosphere and a moderately active lifestyle. She needs a garden and a resident dog to help her adjust to a companion lifestyle.

Mischa is currently based in Cyprus, has a clean bill of health, and is ready to travel to her forever home.

name: Mollie
description:
Mollie is a 3-year-old female Cross-Breed dog with stunning blue eyes, currently residing in Blackpool.

She’s a delightful companion, often found cuddled up on the sofa, cherishing moments of warmth and affection.

While walks might not be her forte due to her nervousness on the lead, she does appreciate having a garden to explore and roam freely.

In terms of companionship, Mollie is excellent with cats, displaying a friendly disposition towards them. However, she prefers to be the sole dog in the household, as she thrives better without canine companions.

Particularly, Mollie gravitates towards female company, making a female-only household her ideal environment.

Mollie has been neutered and is dual-chipped, ensuring her safety and compliance with regulations.

Given her preference for a tranquil environment, Mollie’s ideal home would be without children, providing her with the peace and stability she craves.

name: Larry
description:
Larry is a 2 year old male hound cross who was born in May 2021 and is currently in a foster home in Oman.

Larry was rescued two years ago after he was reported living on the streets in an area that is dangerous for dogs. Unfortunately, we got to Larry’s friend too late and he was poisoned before we could rescue him but we luckily managed to rescue Larry.

He is a timid guy who’s wary of new people. This is unsurprising as he was treated badly on the streets, he had rocks thrown at him and was shouted at. He never associated humans with kindness.

He has been in a foster home with other dogs for over one year and has come on a long way. He will need a home with at least one other dog to make him feel more comfortable.

He will need very kind and patient owners who are understanding of his past and he will need time to settle in, trust and gain confidence. Larry is currently living with cats.

He is leash-trained and will go out for walks with the other dogs. He is not used to being around young children so a quieter home/ older children would be best for him.

He is healthy, weighs around 22kg, is neutered and is fully vaccinated. He is ready to travel to the UK now.

name: Roxie
description:
Roxie is a delightful almost 4-year-old female cross-breed dog currently being fostered in the Poole.

She has shown remarkable adaptability during her journey to her foster home, indicating she travels well. Roxie is lead and harness trained, making walks a joy for both her and her owner.

Moreover, she’s already toilet trained, easing the transition into any new home environment.

Regarding her interactions with other pets, Roxie is described as “dog savvy” with cats, implying she can coexist peacefully with feline companions.

However, she’s not suitable for living with other dogs, as she exhibits reactivity towards them during walks. Therefore, it’s essential for Roxie to be the sole dog in her new home.

Additionally, she’s deemed suitable for households with older children aged 15 and above.

Despite her minor reactivity issue with other dogs, Roxie is affectionate and enjoys spending time with her human family, including cuddles and learning new commands.

A secure garden would be ideal for her to exercise and play freely.

To ensure her safety during walks, it’s recommended to use a no-escape harness.

name: Benny
description:
Benny is a 3 year old male crossbreed, currently at our shelter in Southern Spain but can travel to the UK.

Rescued from a municipal pound, Benny is a lovely happy-go-lucky dog who is great with people – he especially loves children and helping them to put away their toys!

He is an active dog who loves to run and play with other dogs at the shelter, and more than anything he loves sniffing and will spend most of his outside time pottering around the trees and bushes.

He can show dominant behaviours with male dogs and doesn’t like them entering his kennel space, but is fine around them when he is outside. He prefers females but if a male dog is relaxed, he is happy to be around them.

He is playful and really loves his walks but when he returns to his kennel, he is quite calm and happily waits until his next walk. Benny would suit an active home who will take him on lots of long walks and make sure that he gets lots of appropriate enrichment.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella. All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised.

Benny is neutered. Please note that we will advise results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Cora
description:
Cora is a 7-year-old female Sabueso Hound. She weighs 21.6kg and has a height of 59cm, a length of 101cm, a neck circumference of 42cm, and a chest measurement of 69cm.

She was brought to the shelter because she was not suited for hunting, but she has many qualities that make her a wonderful companion.

Cora is an active and energetic girl who is always happy. She enjoys being around people and other dogs but also appreciates having some time to herself. Her lively nature means she would do well in a home that can provide her with regular exercise and mental stimulation.

She is good with other dogs but prefers to be in charge, so she would be best suited to a home where she can establish her role or with an owner experienced in managing confident dogs.

She is super sweet and sociable with people, making her a loving addition to the right home.

Cora needs some work on lead training as she is quite strong, but she is very obedient, which will help with further training. She travels well in the car, making her an easy companion for trips and outings.

So far, she has shown little interest in cats, but further introductions would be necessary.

Cora is currently in Spain but is available for adoption in the UK. Full rescue backup is provided to support her transition into her forever home. With her affectionate and lively personality, Cora will make a fantastic companion for the right owner.

name: Jamie
description:
Jamie is a 5 month old male Cross-Breed puppy currently based in Cyprus, patiently waiting in kennels for his forever family.

Sweet, baby Jamie is still waiting patiently in our kennels in Cyprus, dreaming of the day his forever family finds him. Despite being overlooked time and time again, we know the right person is out there – someone who will see just how special he truly is.

Jamie is one of the “8 puppies with no mom” – a litter born in heartbreaking circumstances at the beginning of January 2025, with no mother to guide them. But from day one, Jamie has shown incredible strength, resilience, and heart.

Thanks to dedicated care and love, Jamie has grown into a healthy, happy, and wonderfully social pup. He’s playful, affectionate, and already showing signs of becoming the kind of loyal companion families dream of. Jamie is expected to be medium-sized when fully grown – the perfect fit for cuddles on the couch and adventures in the garden.

He’s more than just a puppy – he’s a little survivor, full of love and hope. Now all Jamie needs is someone to believe in him and give him the happiest of endings.

Could you be the one to give Jamie the love he’s been waiting for?

Before travelling to the UK, Jamie will receive a full veterinary check, vaccinations, microchipping, and have his passport prepared.

£155 to reserve Jamie – this allows us to begin his vaccinations and prepare his travel documents.

£385 once his flight is confirmed – this covers transport to the UK.

Our team handles every step of the process to bring Jamie safely home to you. Adopting from abroad is simpler than you may expect – and incredibly rewarding! We’re here to support you throughout, with a dedicated UK team and a large community of adopters across the country.

Interested in Jamie? OUR NEXT FLIGHT IS 15th JUNE, HE COULD BE HOME WITH YOU SOONER THAN YOU MIGHT THINK!

When getting in touch, it helps if you can share a few details:

A brief description of your garden and the lowest fence height

Ages of children in or regularly visiting the home

How long Jamie might be left alone and how he’ll fit into your lifestyle

Please note:Adoption is subject to a satisfactory application, home check, and a commitment to neuter Jamie at the appropriate age (at your own expense).

If your circumstances change, you must notify Dali Dog Rescue UK immediately. Should rehoming become necessary, we will assist in placing Jamie directly from your home or, if needed and space allows, he must be returned to an approved Dali Dog Rescue volunteer.

Dogs may not be transferred to another UK rescue organisation under any circumstances. We are committed to Jamie’s lifelong welfare.

name: Duque
description:
Duque is a 5-6-year-old male Griffon who is currently in Spain and available for adoption in the UK.

He is a gentle and affectionate dog who may be a little shy when first meeting new people, but once he builds trust, he absolutely loves being cuddled.

Duque has a calm and endearing nature, making him a wonderful companion for the right home.

He gets along well with other dogs and is sociable in their company, making him a good candidate for a household with existing dogs.

Duque is also good around children, particularly older ones who can give him the gentle encouragement he may need at first.

He measures 69cm in length, 52cm in height, with a 65cm chest and 36cm neck, placing him as a medium to large-sized dog. Although he has not been tested with cats, his temperament suggests he may adapt well with proper introductions.

Duque is searching for a calm, understanding home that will give him time to adjust and show his sweet nature.

name: Hank
description:
Hank – 3 year old male Anatolian Shepherd Cross-Breed

Hank is a beautiful rescue boy from Cyprus, currently in the Atherstone, West Midlands area and now looking for his forever home. He’s around 37kg, house and crate trained, and travels well in the car.

Hank loves his walks, is good on the lead, and enjoys the company of other dogs. Ideally, he would suit a home where he is an only dog or with a friendly older female dog to show him the ropes and boost his confidence.

He lives alongside a cat currently — while he may chase if the cat runs, he’s happy to coexist peacefully when the cat stays calm.

Hank is a real gentle soul once he bonds with you. He would suit an experienced home with older, dog-savvy children simply due to his size and strength. He has been great in his former home with the young children there.

A secure, safe garden to play and relax in

A quieter environment without too much coming and going

If you think you could be Hank’s perfect match, please get in touch. When contacting us, it would help greatly if you could include:

Information about other pets or dogs in your home

How long Hank would be left alone each day

Minimum adoption donation of £300 applies. Adoption is subject to a satisfactory application, home check, and agreement to our post-adoption policies.

Let’s find Hank the home he truly deserves!

name: Ziggy
description:
Ziggy is a 6year old male cross breed located in Spain.

Gentle boy Ziggy is a large Retriever-cross boy with a black, soft, lush coat. Poor boy has been in Foster since last April, as he was very poorly when he was rescued, but now is in very good health and has come a long way by benefitting being in foster care.

He has learnt how to respond very well to commands, and also he is ok with other dogs on his walks, and good on lead. Ziggy is house trained, and he travels well in the car, and can be left home for short periods without any issues.

He is a gentle plodder and very affectionate and well behaved. Unfortunately, his foster mum has had an accident and can no longer walk Ziggy, and we really don’t want him to have to return to the shelter.

So now, we urgently seek a quiet home with or without other friendly dogs and children over 10 years.

Ziggy has sponsorship which makes his adoption fee reduced

His Best Points:Affectionate, gentle, inquisitive and puppyish all in one.

Foster Report:Ziggy is a special fur baby (aren’t they all!). He has blossomed from being almost a walking skeleton and almost unable to see, to a lively, sweet, affectionate dog who wants to be friends with everybody, human and canine.

He has no issues walking past dogs on leads but does not really like loose dogs approaching.

He does not really notice cats unless they run. He is a big dog but still has puppy energy and needs a considerate owner who will continue to work with him to build him up, inside and out and assure him the world isn’t a scary place.

He has now learnt to walk to heel. He is learning commands such as sit and lay down with the aid of treats. Ziggy knows the “LEAVE” command. He has become used to travelling in the car, but needs reassurance when exiting in particular, as he can get disorientated.

It’s best Ziggy is fed alone as he can occasionally be protective over his food. Ziggy can be left alone for an hour or two with no evidence of separation anxiety. Ziggy has been aound young children was perfectly behaved even when they tried to ride him!! Well done Ziggy.

name: Felix
description:
Felix is an 11-month-old male Cross-Breed. He was rescued from a council pound after his seven days were up and no one came to claim him.

It is believed he was deliberately abandoned by his previous owner, as he wasn’t microchipped and no one came forward. Thankfully, he was taken into a safe kennel foster space, sparing him from a tragic fate.

Felix has clearly had some training in the past, as he knows basic commands like sit, lie down, and ‘finish’—a position where he sits by your left side.

He is intelligent and eager to learn, offering great eye contact and responding well to positive reinforcement, especially treats. He is also fully house-trained and loves affection and fuss.

Felix is playful and active, enjoying games of fetch and running around the garden. He gives off a high-pitched bark when playing and a deeper bark when alerting to something unusual. He’s curious and nosey, often standing on his back legs to get a better look at what’s going on around him.

He walks best using a headcollar harness and a dual-control lead, as he can be strong on the lead but is improving with training. Felix could potentially live with a calm, well-mannered female dog, but he may react if approached aggressively by other dogs.

Due to the lack of background information and his size and energy levels, Felix would be best suited to an adult-only home or one with children aged 12 and over. He is not cat tested, so his compatibility with cats is unknown.

An experienced owner who has previously had large-breed dogs is recommended to help guide Felix into a balanced adult life.

name: Indiana Jones
description:
Indiana Jones is a 1-2 year old male Cross-Breed, currently at our holding kennels in Southern Spain. He was thrown over the fence at the municipal pound one night and left to his fate.

Unsurprisingly, when admitted into our care, he was very nervous, and he is still a bit wary of people that he doesn’t know. However, the moment he realises that you are not going to hurt him, he’ll jump up and shower you with kisses!

Indi is a medium active dog and loves to run but in moderation. He is also good with all the other dogs at the shelter and loves to play with them.

Indi would be better in a home with another resident dog as he gains confidence from having other dogs around. He will need a low-activity quiet home who can give him lots of time.

Indiana Jones is negative for all infectious diseases, including Brucella canis.

name: Frederick
description:
Frederick is a 1 year old male drahthaar cross, currently at our holding kennels in Cordoba, Southern Spain.

Admitted as a 6-month old puppy after having been abandoned at a municipal pound, Frederick was understandably scared of everything around him.

He was very nervous and didn’t understand how to walk on a lead or socialise with humans and other dogs.

After some months in our care, and with lots of new friends to give him confidence, he has really come out of his shell and has turned into the sweetest, most affectionate dog.

He can still be a bit nervous of people when he first meets them, so a low-activity home without children (over 8 for adoption only please) would be better for him.

He really wants to be friends with the humans he meets, but he waits until he is sure that they are not going to harm him before he makes a commitment – he will back off until he is sure so his adopter must be patient and understand his need to be introduced to new people and situations in his own time.

Frederick is still a puppy and loves to run and play but he is not destructive and will relax if nothing is going on, and considering his age, he is very well behaved.

He shares a kennel with his best friend, older Breton Aroa, who he adores – it would be amazing if they could be adopted together but he can also be adopted alone, as long as there is a welcoming calm resident dog in the family, who will help him with his confidence.

Frederick is a Drahthaar X and may have been a working dog – please research the breed-specific needs of the Drahthaar before applying.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella canis. All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised.

Frederick is neutered. Please note that we will advise medical results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck, adoption checks and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Benji
description:
BENJI is a 4 year old male podenco, currently at our holding kennels in Cordoba, Southern Spain.

We rescued Benji from a very busy municipal pound in central Spain. He had been collected by the authorities from a breeding hunter with his two equally terrified siblings, and was having a terrible time, sitting and shaking at the back of the pen, only daring to venture out if food was thrown.

He is much more confident since arriving at the shelter but it’s still difficult for him to trust – he still finds it difficult if somebody makes a quick movement or if he hears a loud noise, which is completely understandable given his background.

An escape artist, he jumps and scales very well so his adopter will need to be experienced with this type of dog and put into place proper security measures to keep him safe.

He loves other dogs and finds security in having them nearby so a home with a resident dog or dogs is essential for Benji. Ideally, a home in Spain is sought so that Benji doesn’t have to travel, but we will consider the UK if the right home is found.

Benji is a Podenco and was a working dog – please research the breed-specific needs of the Podenco before applying.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised. Benji is neutered. Please note that we will advise medical results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck, adoption checks and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Simba
description:
Simba is in need of a forever home. He is a 4 year old male JagdTerrier Cross. He is currently in foster and has been there for 6 months now where his foster has been carefully working with him and assessing him and his needs.

We now feel that we have enough information to find the home that he needs as we do not want to have to keep moving him around.

Unfortunately, his needs mean that he cannot stay with his foster, even though they care for him very much, the mutual agreement is that Simba has specific needs and is not able to continue living in a busy, built up area.

This boy has been through a lot. We are seeking a quiet, more rural home where he will feel safe, learn to let his guard down and have a bit more freedom to explore, sniff, and release some of his prey drive energy.

His foster believes if the opportunity arose, he would make a good working dog where his breeds strengths could be used. He needs an experienced owner who either knows his breed well, or has experience dealing with a reactive/prey driven dog.

This is a big ask, but we believe there is someone out there for this beautiful boy. We will be thoroughly vetting all applicants, so please only serious, experienced applications.

If anyone knows someone/a page that specialises in german hunting terriers/terriers, please let us know.

A note from Simba’s foster on his personality and behaviour:

“Having had very little exposure to normal life before coming to the UK, since being in foster Simba has learnt how to relax and is less bothered about daily household and living environment noises, but he has a tendency to have reactive behaviours when out and about and managing this can be challenging and is a work in progress.

Simba is very sensitive to sound and sight and has a very high prey drive. Outside the house, he is on high alert to anything that moves, which includes all vehicles, people, children, cyclists, cats, and joggers, so he needs very careful management and handling. He gets anxious in narrow or enclosed spaces and can get overwhelmed very quickly and needs to be given lots of space, or shielded when walking past reactivity triggers to avoid him lunging out, and he is conscious and anxious of things approaching from behind or suddenly appearing.

He has learnt some recall but can only be let off lead in certain circumstances when there are not too many distractions and unfamiliar people such as joggers, cyclists, children, etc. He can be very unsure of people he has not been introduced to, but is fine with those he has met regularly since being in foster, particularly those who have dogs, and those he has been carefully introduced to, but it has taken time for him build trust.

He can occasionally be a little reactive to some dogs he meets when he is on a short lead and so it is best to not let him approach new unfamiliar people and dogs unless carefully managed, and kept brief. Simba is always keen to see what’s going on on the other side of things both in and out of the house, and so he would need a VERY secure garden at home.

He finds busy built up places with people and cars challenging and needs careful management in those situations as they are triggers for reactivity, so I think a quiet rural setting would mean life is less challenging for him. Underneath his anxiety, Simba appears to be a submissive sensitive boy with a cheeky side to him.

Since being in foster, Simba has not been tested with children but has shown reactivity towards them when seeing them out and about, I’m not sure if he finds them exciting or threatening, but I don’t feel I would trust him with children. Simba has been trained to accept a muzzle, although he doesn’t like it.

Simba has a very, very strong hunting instinct, and is constantly looking and listening for prey to hunt or flush out, he would therefore need someone who is familiar with hunting dog instinct and experienced in managing reactive behaviour, and who is able to provide him with the mental and physical stimulation that his breed needs for his all round wellbeing.

Simba will want to chase cats, I believe there is a level of anxiety and fear that comes with seeing a cat. Simba developed extreme anxiety with moving objects when travelling in the car, and so he now travels well in a covered crate in the car. Simba cannot live with cats as his prey drive is too high.

Simba may do well with another calm dog in the household for company and playmate, preferably a female, but I think he has benefited from one-one attention and training while in foster. Simba will need a transition period from foster to a forever home in order to build trust and familiarity with new surroundings.”

Simba is microchipped, rabies vaccinated, infectious diseases two times vaccinated, bordatella vaccine will be recieved before transport, castrated, Mediterranean diseases tested-negative.

Adoption fee and home check applies, and full rescue backup is provided by Ninas Haven.

name: Alexander
description:
Alexander is a medium-sized 4-year-old mixed breed dog with a lot of energy. He loves engaging in playful activities, particularly displaying a keen enthusiasm for football, and would greatly appreciate a companion who shares his passion for the sport.

This vibrant canine has undergone vaccinations, neutering, and comprehensive health checks, ensuring his well-being and making him a robust and resilient companion.

Friendly towards most dogs, Alexander showcases a sociable nature that can contribute to a harmonious canine environment. Despite his amiable disposition, he would thrive best as the sole dog in a household, and he is not particularly fond of sharing his living space with cats.

Alexander’s exuberant personality and zest for life make him an ideal match for an individual or family looking to add an active and spirited canine member to their home.

With a clean bill of health, vaccinations up-to-date, and the assurance of being neutered, he is ready to be bound into a new home and capture the hearts of those who appreciate his vivacious spirit.

The prospective adopter will find in Alexander a loyal companion, ready to embark on various adventures and share moments of joy in the journey of life.

name: Skipper
description:
Skipper is a 2 year old Croatian Shepherd cross with a remarkable and resilient story.

Originally discovered in a ditch in Croatia at just 6 weeks old, he faced the challenge of adapting to life with only three legs, believed to be a condition from birth, along with a broken pelvis.

Despite these early hardships, Skipper has blossomed into a gorgeous, happy, and loving boy.

This resilient canine companion is currently seeking a new home due to compatibility issues with other dogs in his current household. His ideal home would be one with an experienced owner, preferably as the only dog.

Skipper, though he may bounce a bit due to his three legs, is a loyal and affectionate companion. He walks well on a lead, has good recall, and enjoys the outdoors. However, he may get sick in the car, though he has medication to address this.

Skipper’s loving nature is apparent in his eagerness to please his owners. He appreciates cuddles, adores going on walks, and has a keen interest in treats, making him amenable to training.

It’s essential to note that Skipper is protective of his humans and prefers not to share them with other resident dogs. He’s sensitive about his remaining back leg, and caution is advised when handling it. Maintaining a healthy weight is crucial for Skipper’s well-being.

Microchipped, rabies vaccinated, infectious diseases two times vaccinated, and castrated, Skipper is ready to find his forever home. While he may not be the best fit for a household with other dogs, he might coexist with a dog-savvy cat.

It’s recommended that any potential adopter has experience with dogs and can provide a secure environment for Skipper.

If you’re looking to give Skipper a loving home, situated in Milton Keynes, UK, and can offer him the undivided attention he craves, please consider adopting this resilient and charming canine companion.

A £395 adoption fee applies, and a home check is required, with Ninas Haven providing full rescue back up.
